> **Intellectual failures and the heart’s unbelief, lust, and deceit permit departure together. Deleting either set cuts the sentences. The failures are identified without being pardons, and the vices are named without making the turning unintelligible.**

---

# 70.56 Competing Claim: Speed Proves There Was Never a Truth to Leave

> **They turned quickly. They were so soon removed. They believed only for a while. Therefore the prior state was counterfeit, and the doctrine of turning is a mistake about names. Nothing was left, because nothing had been had.**

The claim fails as a general account, because it contradicts the premises the speed-texts themselves state.

Exodus 32: the way was commanded, and the turning is out of it. The charge is unintelligible if there was no way. Galatians 1: they were called into the grace of Christ, and they received a gospel, and the removal is from the caller unto another gospel. Galatians 5: ye did run well. Galatians 3: Christ was set forth before their eyes, and they received the Spirit by the hearing of faith. Luke 8:13: they hear, receive the word with joy, and for a while believe, and then fall away. Hebrews 3: the fathers heard, and saw the works forty years. Second Peter 3:17: fall from your own steadfastness, addressed to those who know these things before.

Some passages in the writings distinguish a profession that was never the thing. They do not authorize the deletion of “out of the way,” “received,” “did run well,” “for a while believe,” and “your own steadfastness.” Where the text says the prior possession was real, the turning is a leaving of a real possession. Where the text withholds that premise, this chapter does not invent it. The speed-claim invents a universal negative the exhibitions will not bear. It also makes the marvel at Galatia theatrical. One does not marvel that a people left a caller they never had, on the ground that they left so soon. The soon is grievous because the calling was theirs.

The claim’s grain of truth is narrower and already kept: a joyful hearing is not a root, and a name is not a being. That truth does not convert every quick departure into evidence that the word was never given. It converts joyful hearing without root into a warned condition, which is what Luke 8:13 is.

Thus:

> **Speed and brevity are features of some turnings, not proofs that the given truth was imaginary. The way commanded, the gospel received, the race run, the while of belief, and the steadfastness possessed are the texts’ premises. The turning is a leaving of those premises, not a retroactive denial that they were stated.**

---

# 70.57 Competing Claim: This Chapter as Already Chapters 71–73 or Movement X

> **Once the turning has been named, the heresies have been judged, the dryness has been diagnosed, the unskillful have been described, and the labour of study has been commanded. Leaven is already accepted heresy. The itching ear is already aridity. Not-understanding is already *apeiros*. “Give the more earnest heed” is already *spoudazō*. The later chapters are surplus.**

The claim fails.

The locked TOC distinguishes the assignments in distinct sentences. This chapter examines the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside and identifies the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth. Chapter 71 examines how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. Chapter 72 examines aridity in connection with deficient intellectual engagement, poor judgment, and failure to labour properly in the Word. Chapter 73 develops *apeiros*, inexperienced and unskillful in the word of righteousness. Movement X examines scholarly labour, *spoudazō*, rightly dividing, and readiness for the First Principles. Distinction of assignments is not a delay of nerve. It is the knowledge-flow.

A pious form of collapse says: the effects are visible, so write the later files now. Visible effects are the warrant that the turning is grave. They are not the normalization, the loss of reasonability, or the formation of skill. Chapter 69 already refused the collapse when it was offered as “the displacement is already the pathology.” This chapter refuses the remaining half aimed at itself: the turning is not already the acceptance-file, the dryness-file, the unskill-file, or the labour-file.

“Many shall follow” has been used as a following that slanders the way of truth. The use is not the finished account of how an error becomes the ordinary doctrine of an age, or of why a synod’s vote cannot make the error true. The itching ear has been used as the mechanism by which teachers are heaped and the truth is left. The use is not the finished account of aridity. Not-understanding what one affirms has been used as an intellectual failure that permits vain jangling. The use is not the finished account of Hebrews 5:13. Earnest heed has been used as the contrary of drift. The use is not the finished account of diligence, endeavour, and study. Hebrews 6:1–2 has not been opened as the foundation-list. Second Timothy 2:15 has not been opened as the approved workman.

Thus:

> **This chapter is not already Chapters 71–73 or Movement X. The causes and mechanisms of turning aside are the object. Later questions remain later.**

---

# 70.58 Reason Through the Evidence

The inference can now be exhibited.

**Premise 1.** The Graphē is the primary written authority. The record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. The Scripture cannot be broken. Truth is conformity to reality and is not created by belief, popularity, or institutional acceptance (Chapters 1–3, 57, 62–63, and 65, used not retried).

**Premise 2.** The authority of that writing is distinct from the authority claimed for a later statement of sense. Transfer fails. Despair fails. Quotation is not the Graphē (Chapter 66, used not retried).

**Premise 3.** Scripture is misread in five inspectable modes. The writing remains the measure. A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect (Chapter 67, used not retried).

**Premise 4.** Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution are secondary systems. They may serve. None becomes primary written authority by Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition (Chapter 68, used not retried).

**Premise 5.** When commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture, the seat of sense is occupied and the test is reversed. The writing is not broken. Service is not the event (Chapter 69, used not retried).

**Premise 6.** The writings themselves exhibit doctrinal turning aside and name its causes and mechanisms. A commanded way is left quickly by substitution of a made god, the redemption-sentence retained (Exodus 32; Deuteronomy 9). A deceived heart issues in turning and in another service; right things are refused and smooth things demanded (Deuteronomy 11:16; Isaiah 30:9–11). Churches are removed from the caller unto a different gospel that is not another of the same kind, troubled and perverted by some, bewitched and hindered from obeying a placarded truth, leavened by a little contrary (Galatians 1; 3; 5). Some swerve from the commandment’s end into vain jangling, desiring to teach what they do not understand (1 Timothy 1:3–7). Some depart from the faith by giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons (1 Timothy 4:1–2). Other-teaching refuses consent to wholesome words; a falsely named knowledge is professed, and some err concerning the faith (1 Timothy 6). Ears that will not endure sound doctrine heap teachers by lust and turn from the truth unto fables (2 Timothy 4:3–4). Empty talk increases and consumes; a false sentence about the resurrection overthrows the faith of some (2 Timothy 2:16–18). Seducers deceive and are deceived; continuance in the things learned, in the company of the scriptures, is commanded (2 Timothy 3:13–15). Human commandments and fables turn from the truth and subvert houses (Titus 1). Things heard slip when earnest heed is not given (Hebrews 2:1). An evil heart of unbelief departs from the living God; sin’s deceit hardens; the word heard does not profit when not mixed with faith (Hebrews 3–4). Joyful hearing without root falls away in temptation (Luke 8:13). Philosophy and empty deceit carry off from Christ those who have received him (Colossians 2). Perverse speech draws disciples after the speakers (Acts 20). Destructive teaching is brought in beside; the straight way is forsaken (2 Peter 2). The unlearned and unstable wrest hard things unto destruction and can be led away from their own steadfastness (2 Peter 3:16–18). A brother can err from the truth and be converted (James 5:19–20). Erring is joined to not knowing the scriptures (Matthew 22:29).

**Premise 7.** Reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions, tested rather than cited as authority, cohere where they locate wresting, bias, explaining-away, and self-interested handling in men, where they detect fallacy by what is written, where they treat dull hearing as a condition that can leave a word unheld, and where they join intellectual failure to turning among persons and among bodies that claim Christ’s name. They do not cohere, and are not adopted, where they reduce every turning to bare willfulness, where they deny hard texts or real expounding, where they install a verse-count or a dispensational grid as the method, where they treat a causal chain through aridity, accepted heresies, *apeiros*, and *spoudazō* as already finished, or where the warner’s grid is received as the cure because the warner named the disease.

**Premise 8.** Competing reductions fail: the writing’s hardness as the cause; governance as already the whole pathology; every disagreement as tergiversation; harmlessness; fate; the heart against the intellect as a forced choice; speed as proof that nothing was ever given; this file as already Chapters 71–73 or Movement X.

**Inference.** Therefore doctrinal turning aside is an inspectable movement from a truth the Graphē has given toward another object that claims its place. Its causes and mechanisms are the ones the writings name: substitution, leaven and spread, selection of teachers by appetite, transfer and withholding of heed, twist and beguilement, covert introduction, drawing-after, drift, and departure by unbelief. The intellectual failures that permit it are failures of understanding, consent, learning, stability, endurance of sound doctrine, heed, and knowing the scriptures one possesses. Those failures join unbelief, lust, deceit, and gain, and do not excuse the movement. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance, earnest heed, and conversion remain real contraries. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement IX’s fifth word.

The inference is not a leap from “hearers can err” to “every difference is a desertion.” The exhibitions supply the given, the movement, and the claimant. The inference is not a leap from “the turning is grave” to “the later pathology-files and the labour-files have been written.” Sequence forbids that leap. The inference is not a leap from “a source warned against turning” to “the source’s system is the account of turning.” Testing forbids that leap.

Thus:

> **The join is inspectable: primary writing + distinguished interpretation + catalogued misreading + ranked secondary systems + governance of meaning already exhibited + the writings’ own clauses of removal, swerving, heed transferred, ears turned, ways forsaken, and wresting = a warranted account of the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside, and of the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth, at this level and not beyond it.**

---

# 70.59 Explicit Versus Inferred

What is explicit in the writings used here includes: a quick turning out of the way commanded, and a calf assigned the exodus (Exodus 32:8); a deceived heart, a turning, and service of other gods (Deuteronomy 11:16); a demand for smooth things and a command to turn aside out of the path (Isaiah 30:10–11); removal from the caller unto a different gospel which is not another of the same kind, and a curse on another preaching (Galatians 1:6–9); bewitching, not obeying the truth, beginning in the Spirit and seeking completion by the flesh (Galatians 3:1–3); a good race hindered, a persuasion not from the caller, a little leaven (Galatians 5:7–9); swerving from the commandment’s end unto vain jangling, without understanding what is affirmed (1 Timothy 1:5–7); departure from the faith by heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons (1 Timothy 4:1); non-consent to wholesome words, and erring concerning the faith by professing a falsely named knowledge (1 Timothy 6:3–5, 20–21); non-endurance of sound doctrine, heaped teachers, itching ears, the ear turned from the truth unto fables (2 Timothy 4:3–4); empty talk increasing, a gangrenous word, the resurrection said to be past, the faith of some overthrown (2 Timothy 2:16–18); deceiving and being deceived, and the command to continue in the things learned (2 Timothy 3:13–14); commandments of men that turn from the truth (Titus 1:14); earnest heed against slipping from the things heard (Hebrews 2:1); an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God, hardening by sin’s deceit, the word not profiting when not mixed with faith (Hebrews 3:12–13; 4:2); hearing, joy, belief for a while, no root, falling away in temptation (Luke 8:13); spoiling through philosophy and vain deceit, not after Christ (Colossians 2:8); perverse speech to draw disciples after the speakers, and the word of grace able to build up (Acts 20:30–32); privy bringing-in, denial of the Master who bought them, forsaking the straight way (2 Peter 2:1–2, 15); hard things wrested by the unlearned and unstable unto destruction, and the warning against being led away and falling from steadfastness (2 Peter 3:16–17); erring from the truth and being converted (James 5:19–20); erring, not knowing the scriptures (Matthew 22:29).

What is inferred, and warranted by the join, is that these explicit relations are the causes and mechanisms the locked assignment names as tergiversation; that the intellectual failures identified are the openings those clauses describe, joined to and not substituted for unbelief, lust, and deceit; that substitution, spread, appetite, heed, twist, covert introduction, drawing-after, and drift are operations visible across more than one exhibition; that governance is a condition of disguised fidelity and not the whole cause; that the five modes can carry the movement without becoming this file; and that continuance, heed, and conversion are real contraries, so the movement is neither harmless nor fated.

What is not inferred here: that the normalization and institutional acceptance of heresy have been written; that aridity and the loss of reasonability have been written; that *apeiros* has been opened; that *spoudazō*, rightly dividing, or the First Principles have been established; that every disagreement is a turning; that every quick departure proves the prior profession empty, or that every prior profession was deep; that every teacher is a wolf; that every question is vain jangling; that every use of the word philosophy is Colossians 2:8; that a named later party is the historical moment turning began; that the Introduction’s classes are a complete psychology; that the leaflet’s chain is a finished causal law; that the leaflet’s grid is the cure or is itself adjudicated verse by verse.

The distinction between explicit and inferred is itself part of the chapter’s honesty. The writings exhibit departures, name causes, and command contraries. The chapter names those exhibitions as the account of doctrinal turning aside. The later files remain later.

Thus:

> **What the writings assign as the movement from a given truth, and as the conditions of that movement, is explicit. That those relations are this chapter’s account of tergiversation is the warranted inference. Later doctrines have not been inferred here.**

---

# 70.60 The Warranted Conclusion Stated with Full Force

The conclusion may now be stated without postponement and without inflation.

Doctrinal turning aside is the movement of a person or a people from a truth the Graphē has given toward another object that claims that truth’s place.

**The causes** the writings attach to that movement include: a deceived heart; refusal to wait on the word given and demand for a substitute; troubling and perverting speech; bewitchment and hindrance; a persuasion not from the caller; desire to teach without understanding; transfer of heed to seducing spirits and demonic doctrines; refusal to endure sound doctrine; lust that selects teachers; empty talk that increases; human commandments and fables; failure of earnest heed; an evil heart of unbelief; the deceitfulness of sin; temptation meeting a rootless reception; philosophy and empty deceit not after Christ; the aim of drawing disciples after the speaker; wages; privy introduction of destructive teaching; unlearned and unstable wresting. The list is plural because the record is plural.

**The mechanisms** by which the movement is carried include: substitution that keeps the holy sentence and reassigns it; the small contrary that leavens, consumes, and spreads; the heaping of teachers by the ear’s appetite; the transfer and the withholding of heed; the twist, the enticing word, and the true line used for a false step; the covert bringing-in beside the faith; the drawing of disciples after the speaker; the drift of things heard; the departure of unbelief in the face of a word heard. These operations are readable from the clauses. They are not a psychology invented behind the clauses.

**The intellectual failures** that permit the departure are failures of understanding what one affirms, of consent to wholesome words, of learning and stability before what is hard, of endurance of sound doctrine, of the direction of heed, and of knowing the scriptures one possesses. They permit as openings. They stand in the same paragraphs as unbelief, lust, deceit, hypocrisy, and gain. They do not excuse the turner. The unlearned wrestler goes to his own destruction. The affirm-er who does not understand is still the man who turned aside unto vain jangling.

**The truth turned from remains the measure.** The calf does not become the Lord. The different gospel does not become the received gospel. The fable does not become the truth. The slandered way remains the way. The Scripture is not broken by the leaving. A following, even of many, does not transform the departure into truth. That last sentence is the neighbour of Chapter 71, stated here only as the survival of the measure, not as the doctrine of institutional acceptance.

**Continuance is a real contrary.** Continue in the things learned. Give the more earnest heed. Take heed lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief. Beware, knowing beforehand. Grow in grace and in the knowledge of the Lord. Convert the one who errs from the truth. The word of God’s grace is able to build up. The holy scriptures are able to make wise unto salvation. “Some” depart. The some is not the all. The turning is not fate, and it is not harmless.

This continues Movement IX. It is not Chapter 69 retried. It is not Chapters 71–73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.

Thus:

> **The causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside have been examined, and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth have been identified. The turning is in force. Later questions remain later because they are different questions.**

---

# 70.61 Apply the Standard

The standard has been applied.

A movement that stands in the neighbourhood of the faith is now to be asked not only, “What voice is finishing the sense?” — Chapter 69’s question — but, “What truth was given, who or what has moved from it, and what object has claimed its place?” Was the way commanded, and has a substitute received its sentence? Was the gospel received, and has a different message kept the name? Was sound doctrine the thing to endure, and has the ear ordered fables? Was Christ received, and has a persuasive speech carried the hearer off from him? Was the straight way there, and has it been forsaken for wages? Was the writing in the hands, and has it been wrested because the handler was unlearned and unstable?

The questions are practical without becoming a tribunal’s handbook, a history of parties, or a technique of interpretation. A people who confess that Scripture is primary may still be removed from the gospel they received. A people who have run well may still be hindered. A hearer who once received the word with joy may still have no root when temptation comes. An elder may still speak perverse things to draw disciples after himself. A warning against turning may still be stapled to a grid that turns. A hard sentence may still be left hard without being twisted, and a twisted sentence may still be judged by the writing it twisted.

The standard also protects. A correction toward the writing is not a desertion. A teacher who opens the scripture and commends disciples to the word of grace is not a wolf. A question not settled by the writing is not yet a fable. A hearer who continues in the things learned is not credited with infallibility and is not accused of turning because others turned. Service remains service. Steadfastness remains a real relation to a truth that stands. The protection is the same fact as the judgment: the writing is the measure of both the continuance and the departure.

The standard is the Graphē. Tergiversation is the movement away from what it has given. The intellectual failures are openings in the hearer and the handler. The openings do not move the standard.

Thus:

> **The standard has been applied: the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside, and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth, have been identified as Movement IX’s fifth word, not announced as a slogan, and not postponed as if the turning were weak.**

---

# 70.62 From Tergiversation to Accepted Heresies

A turning, now controlled as an inspectable departure with named causes, still leaves a further question.

The turning-file is in force. Persons and peoples leave a given truth by substitution, spread, appetite, heed, twist, covert introduction, drawing-after, drift, and unbelief. Intellectual failures permit the leaving and do not excuse it. The truth remains the measure. Those sentences are the cleared ground. They are not yet the dedicated examination of how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, or of why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth.

If the turning were not stated, the next question would still be what causes departure. The turning has been stated. If this chapter were already the account of accepted heresies, the next file would be repetition. This chapter is not that account. The next question is therefore the acceptance the locked assignment names: Accepted Heresies.

“Many shall follow their pernicious ways” has been read as a following. A following can thicken into a normal doctrine, a test of membership, a teaching that no longer has to be brought in beside because it has become the house’s own voice. The thickening is not yet examined. A little leaven leavens the lump. The leavened lump, received as the faith and defended as the faith, is a further object. The present file had to establish the leaven as a mechanism of turning. It must not steal the account of acceptance in order to make the turning sound like a sociology of institutions. The next file must not steal this turning as if the causes had not been stated.

That is the proper open of the next chapter. The turning was never meant to be a slogan that finishes Movement IX, and it was never meant to deny that a departure can become the ordinary doctrine of a body. It was meant to be the naming of the movement and of the failures that permit it, sufficient to justify taking the next question, which is the question the movement itself forces once acceptance, and not only departure, is the object: how do erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why does institutional acceptance not transform error into truth?

The next file must not treat this turning as if the causes had not been described. This file must not treat that acceptance as if Chapter 71 were already written. Naming the neighbourhood is not performing the examination.

---

# What Has Been Established

This chapter has established:

1. **Tergiversation, in this argument, is doctrinal turning aside: the movement of a person or a people from a truth the Graphē has given, toward another object that claims that truth’s place.**
2. **The biblical acts collected under that name include *sur*, *ektrepō*, *apostrephō*, *aphistēmi*, *metatithēmi*, *pararreō*, *astocheō*, and *strebloō*. The words stay distinct. The assigned object is one.**
3. **A cause is a condition the writings attach to the departure. A mechanism is an operation by which the departure is carried. Both are read from the clauses.**
4. **An intellectual failure is a failure of understanding, consent, learning, stability, endurance of sound doctrine, heed, or knowing the scriptures, which permits departure as an opening and does not excuse it.**
5. **Departure from truth leaves what the writing has given as the case. Retained vocabulary is a disguise of the leaving, not a proof that the leaving did not occur.**
6. **The truth turned from remains the measure. The turning does not break it and does not become it.**
7. **The causes and mechanisms are named in the writings, so the turning is inspectable. Forewarning is possible because the departure is describable in advance.**
8. **Continuance in what was learned, earnest heed, beware, and conversion of the one who errs are real contraries. Turning is not fate.**
9. **First hearing, correction toward the writing, service under the writing, and the hardness of some sentences are not themselves tergiversation.**
10. **Exodus 32 and Deuteronomy 9 exhibit a quick substitution: the commanded way left, the exodus-sentence reassigned to a made god, the making concealed in the report.**
11. **Deuteronomy 11:16 orders deceived heart, turning aside, and service of other gods. Isaiah 30:9–11 exhibits hearers demanding smooth things and commanding the path to be abandoned.**
12. **Galatians 1:6–9 exhibits removal from the caller unto a different gospel that keeps the name and is denied the identity. Troublers pervert. The received gospel measures. The curse weighs. Speed does not erase the prior call.**
13. **Galatians 3:1–3 and 5:7–9 exhibit bewitchment, hindrance of a good race, a persuasion not from the caller, and leaven. The truth had been placarded. Non-obedience is the failure.**
14. **First Timothy 1:3–7 exhibits a swerve from the commandment’s end into vain jangling by men who desire to teach and do not understand what they affirm.**
15. **First Timothy 4:1–2 exhibits departure from the faith by a transfer of heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons, with hypocrisy and a seared conscience. “Some” refuses fate. Express speech refuses mystery.**
16. **First Timothy 6 exhibits non-consent to wholesome words and a professed, falsely named knowledge by which some err concerning the faith. The deposit remains keepable.**
17. **Second Timothy 4:3–4 exhibits the ear’s mechanism in order: non-endurance of sound doctrine, teachers heaped by lust, itching ears, the ear turned from the truth, the person turned unto fables.**
18. **Second Timothy 2:16–18 exhibits empty talk increasing, a false sentence about the resurrection, a gangrenous spread, and the overthrow of the faith of some.**
19. **Second Timothy 3:13–14 exhibits deceiving and being deceived, and commands continuance in the things learned, in the company of the scriptures able to make wise unto salvation.**
20. **Titus 1:10–14 exhibits human commandments and fables that turn from the truth and subvert houses. Soundness in the faith is the contrary. Household subversion is not yet the normalization-file.**
21. **Hebrews 2:1 exhibits drift: the things heard slip when the more earnest heed is not given. The loss can be quiet. The obligation shows it is not trivial and not fated.**
22. **Hebrews 3:12–4:2 exhibits departing from the living God by an evil heart of unbelief, hardening by sin’s deceit, and a heard word that does not profit when not mixed with faith. Duration of exposure is not heed.**
23. **Luke 8:13 exhibits joyful hearing, belief for a while, no root, and falling away in temptation. The prior reception and the fall are both in the text.**
24. **Colossians 2:4–8 exhibits beguiling speech and a carrying off through philosophy and empty deceit after men and after the world’s rudiments, not after Christ. Fullness in him is the reason the supplement is a turning.**
25. **Acts 20:28–32 exhibits distorted speech aimed at drawing disciples after the speakers, from outside or from among the elders. The word of God’s grace is able to build up.**
26. **Second Peter 2:1–2 and 2:15 exhibit privy bringing-in, denial of the Master who bought them, a following, and the forsaking of the straight way for the way of wages. The way of truth remains the way while it is slandered. Acceptance as a doctrine of a body remains Chapter 71.**
27. **Second Peter 3:16–18 exhibits the intellectual failure of the unlearned and unstable who wrest hard things unto destruction, and the danger of being led away and falling from one’s own steadfastness. Hardness is not the verb’s subject. Growth in the knowledge of Christ is the contrary.**
28. **James 5:19–20 exhibits erring from the truth among brethren and conversion back. Return is intelligible because the truth remains.**
29. **Matthew 22:29 joins erring to not knowing the scriptures and the power of God. The failure is culpable. It is not the only cause the rest of the canon names.**
30. **The intellectual failures identified are: not understanding what one affirms; not consenting to wholesome words; unlearned instability before what is hard; not enduring sound doctrine; heed withheld or transferred; not knowing the scriptures one possesses.**
31. **Those failures permit departure and do not pardon it. They stand with unbelief, lust, deceit, and gain.**
32. **Substitution keeps a holy sentence, name, or reverence and assigns it to another object.**
33. **A little contrary spreads: leaven, gangrene, privy cargo, subverted houses.**
34. **Teachers are heaped by the ear that will not endure sound doctrine, and speakers distort speech to become the disciples’ destination.**
35. **Heed is the hinge: transferred, it departs; withheld, it drifts.**
36. **Twist, enticing speech, and a true line used for a false step carry turning in people who have not thrown the writing away.**
37. **Governance of meaning is a condition under which departure can be called fidelity. It is not the whole cause.**
38. **The five modes of misreading can carry a turning. They are instruments, not a second catalog, and not the definition of the turning.**
39. **The reconstructible Introduction account of wresting, bias, explaining-away, and self-interested handling is received as coherence. A total willfulness that erases hinderers is not adopted. A simplicity that erases hard texts and expounding is not adopted.**
40. **“As it is written” is received as the direction by which a turning is detected. A mechanical count of verses is not adopted as the detector.**
41. **Dull hearing can leave a delivered word unheld. That coherence is received. Aridity, *apeiros*, and the first principles are not thereby written.**
42. **The reconstructible Aletheia chain is received where intellectual failure is joined to turning among persons and among bodies that claim Christ’s name. It is not adopted as a finished sequence through aridity, accepted heresies, unskillfulness, and *spoudazō*.**
43. **A warning against tergiversation does not certify the warner’s grid. The grid is refused the offices of cause-list and of cure. Each sentence meets the writing.**
44. **“The writing is hard, therefore the writing causes the turning” fails.**
45. **“Governance is already the whole cause” fails.**
46. **“Every disagreement is tergiversation” fails.**
47. **“The turning is harmless because the truth still stands” fails.**
48. **“The turning is fate, and the commands are rhetoric” fails.**
49. **“Only the heart” and “only the intellect” both fail.**
50. **“Speed proves there was never a truth to leave” fails.**
51. **Treating this chapter as already Chapters 71–73 or Movement X fails.**
52. **What is explicit has been distinguished from what is inferred, and later doctrines have not been inferred here.**
53. **The turning attaches to a movement from a given truth. It does not confiscate correction, service, or continuance, and it does not confer truth on the object turned unto.**
54. **This chapter continues Movement IX because its assigned word has been stated.**
55. **This chapter opens Chapter 71 by naming the next necessary question without answering it.**
56. **What is reserved is Chapters 71–73; entire Movement X (Chapters 74–85); the First Principles themselves; and σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*) as a dedicated chapter.**

---

# Chapter Summary

> **The chapter’s central conclusion:** Doctrinal turning aside is the movement of a person or a people from a truth the Graphē has given toward another object that claims its place. Because the writing is the primary written authority already earned; because that authority has been distinguished from the authority of interpretation; because the record does not fail and the Scripture cannot be broken; because misreading has been catalogued without making the writing obscure; because secondary systems have been ranked as servants; and because governance of meaning has been shown as occupation of the seat of sense without being allowed to pose as the whole pathology — the causes and mechanisms of the turning can be read from the writings themselves. Substitution, spread, appetite, heed, twist, covert introduction, drawing-after, drift, and unbelief carry the movement. Failures of understanding, consent, learning, stability, endurance of sound doctrine, heed, and knowing the scriptures permit it, together with lust, deceit, and gain, and without excusing it. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance, earnest heed, and conversion remain real contraries. Competing reductions fail: hardness as the writing’s fault; governance as the whole cause; every disagreement as desertion; harmlessness; fate; the heart against the intellect; speed as retroactive emptiness; this chapter as already Chapters 71–73 or Movement X. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement IX’s fifth word. The turning is in force. Chapter 71 remains later because it is a later question. Movement IX continues.

The essential architecture is:

> **Governance of meaning already stated → tergiversation defined → biblical acts distinguished → causes and mechanisms defined → one clean account of sequence and limits → three members of positive warrant → exhibitions of turning examined → intellectual failures identified → mechanisms joined → governance kept as condition → modes kept as instruments → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested → reductions refused → turning warranted → sequence to accepted heresies.**

The governing distinctions are:

- **The turning** is not **a second account of governance.**
- **A cause** is not **an excuse.**
- **An intellectual failure** is not **the absence of the heart’s unbelief, lust, and deceit.**
- **Retained vocabulary** is not **retained truth.**
- **The truth’s survival** is not **the turning’s harmlessness.**
- **Hardness** is not **wresting.**
- **Speed** is not **proof that nothing was given.**
- **“Some”** is not **“all.”**
- **A little leaven** is not **already the normalization-file.**
- **The itching ear** is not **already aridity.**
- **Not-understanding** is not **already *apeiros*.**
- **Earnest heed** is not **already *spoudazō*.**
- **Correction toward the writing** is not **desertion.**
- **Service** is not **turning.**
- **Every disagreement** is not **tergiversation.**
- **The warner’s grid** is not **the cure.**
- **This file** is not **Chapter 69 retried.**
- **This file** is not **Chapters 71–73.**
- **This file** is not **Movement X or the First Principles.**
- **Using Chapters 57, 65, 66, 67, 68, and 69** is not **reprinting them.**
- **Limits** are **the shape of the doctrine**, not **delayed doubt.**
- **Sequence** is **not hesitation about this level.**

The decisive principle is:

> **Examine the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside, and identify the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth, claiming what the writings’ own exhibitions and the preceding premises warrant and not more: the movement is inspectable, the openings are named, the truth remains the measure, and continuance is a real contrary — before examining how erroneous doctrines become accepted. Draw the conclusion the premises support. Do not draw the conclusions that still require later premises. Then ask how error becomes the ordinary doctrine of a body, and why acceptance does not make it true.**

---

# Transition to Chapter 71

Movement IX continues. Its fifth word has been stated.

The Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The writing is the decisive written measure. That gate is in force. The authority of that writing has been distinguished from the authority claimed for a later statement of what the writing means. Transfer fails. Despair fails. How that later act fails has been examined: poor perception, deficient understanding, faulty inference, context failure, improper handling. The writing remains the measure of those operations. Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution have been examined as secondary systems toward that writing. They may serve under it. None becomes primary authority merely by claiming Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition. What happens when commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it has been examined. The seat of sense is occupied. The test is reversed. The writing is not broken. Service is not the event. The causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside have now been examined, and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth have been identified. The movement is inspectable. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance is a real contrary. Movement IX’s fifth word is in force.

The writings that judge that movement do not leave unused the further question of acceptance. Turning has been stated as turning. Stated turning still leaves the dedicated examination of how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and of why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. A people can leave a truth, and the account of how the leaving becomes the house’s ordinary doctrine can remain a different question. The next necessary question is therefore not a new curiosity. It is the question the locked assignment names:

> **How do erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, now that doctrinal turning aside has been shown in its causes and mechanisms, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that acceptance rather than a second turning-file, and rather than aridity or unskillfulness?**

That is the subject of:

# Chapter 71 — Accepted Heresies

> **Examine how erroneous doctrines can become normalized or institutionalized and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth.**

The investigation now moves from:

> **tergiversation and doctrinal turning aside**
>
> to:
>
> **accepted heresies.**

# End of Chapter 70

chapters.title: Accepted Heresies
chapters.body:
> **Movement IX — When Authoritative Truth Is Mishandled**

> **Central objective:** Examine how erroneous doctrines can become normalized or institutionalized, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth, so that a turning already shown in its causes is now shown in its settlement — the erroneous doctrine become the ordinary teaching of a body, or installed in that body’s places, offices, calendar, penalties, and public rule — and so that the body’s reception is refused the power to make the error true. This continues Movement IX. It uses Chapters 57, 62–63, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, and 70 as premises. It is not a second turning-file, not aridity, and not *apeiros*, and not Movement X or the First Principles written in advance.

---

## Chapter Assignment

Chapter 70 established Movement IX’s fifth word. Doctrinal turning aside is the movement of a person or a people from a truth the Graphē has given toward another object that claims that truth’s place. The causes and mechanisms are inspectable in the writings. Intellectual failures of understanding, consent, learning, stability, endurance of sound doctrine, heed, and knowing the scriptures permit the departure and do not excuse it. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance, earnest heed, and conversion remain real contraries. The turning-file is in force.

Chapter 70 ended by naming the next necessary question, not a new curiosity:

> **How do erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, now that doctrinal turning aside has been shown in its causes and mechanisms, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that acceptance rather than a second turning-file, and rather than aridity or unskillfulness?**

That is this chapter’s assignment.

The locked Table of Contents states the work in one sentence:

> **Examine how erroneous doctrines can become normalized or institutionalized and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth.**

The locked knowledge-flow places this examination after the turning and before the dedicated examination of aridity and unskillfulness. Turning has been stated as turning. Stated turning still leaves the settlement in which an erroneous doctrine ceases to be a departure someone must smuggle and becomes the ordinary teaching, the manner of the fathers, the chapel’s word, the doctrine a church holds, or the rule a council commands. A movement away from a given truth is one object. A body that now teaches the error as its doctrine, and offers its own reception as though reception were truth, is a further object. The present file is that object, at the level the premises warrant, and not beyond it.

The present file does not re-narrate the causes and mechanisms of departure. It cites Chapter 70 as established. It does not re-describe the occupation of the seat of sense. It cites Chapter 69 as established. It does not re-rank theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution. It cites Chapter 68 as established. It does not re-catalog how Scripture is misread. It cites Chapter 67 as established. It does not re-draw the distinction between the authority of the text and the authority of interpretation. It cites Chapter 66 as established. It does not re-prove that the Graphē is the primary written authority. It cites Chapter 65 as established. It does not re-answer why the Scripture cannot be broken, or why the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. It cites Chapters 62–63 and 57 as established. It does not write aridity or *apeiros* as dedicated files. It does not write Movement X. It does not enter the First Principles. It examines the normalization and institutionalization of erroneous doctrine, and the refusal of reception as a transforming act, without which Movement IX would possess a turning and still lack the earned account of how the turning becomes the house’s own voice.

A departure, now distinguished from governance and from a mere disagreement, still leaves a further question. If persons and peoples can leave a truth the writing has given, how does the thing they left toward become what a body calls its doctrine, its manner, its feast, its priesthood, its command? If the settlement were already the turning restated, the fifth word would be reprinted as the sixth. If the settlement were already the dryness of judgment or the diagnosis of the unskillful, the later files would be closed inside this one. If the examination stopped at the warning “error is still error when many hold it,” the how of acceptance would be a slogan, and the why of non-transformation would be an assertion Chapters 1–3 had already made and this file had not applied. The present file is the acceptance, at the level the writings and the locked assignment require, and not beyond it.

The remaining question of the book’s sequence follows. Sequence continues the investigation. It does not convert the present line into hesitation.

## Central Objective

> **To examine, from the biblical record and from premises already in force, how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth, so that Movement IX’s sixth word is one inspectable verdict: an accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine that a body has received as its ordinary teaching or installed in the forms by which it orders belief and life; the writings exhibit the operations of that reception; and the reception — by multitude, by fathers, by office, by chapel, by penalty, by age, by a sign that comes to pass, by a flattering name, or by the word “doctrine” itself — does not make the error conform to reality. The truth the writing has given remains the measure of the settled teaching, as it remained the measure of the turning. A remnant, a contrary word, and a book found in the house remain real refusals of the accepted state. The account keeps this settlement distinct from a second narrative of turning, from the loss of reasonability, from unskillfulness as a dedicated diagnosis, and from the labour-files. It refuses the reductions that treat consensus, antiquity, office, survival, or religious show as creators of truth; that treat the truth’s survival as the acceptance’s harmlessness; that treat every sect-name as an accepted heresy or every minority as fidelity; that treat Chapters 68 and 69 as already this file; and that treat this file as already Chapter 70, Chapters 72–73, or Movement X. It refuses both under-claim and over-claim.**

The governing movement is:

> **Turning aside already stated → question of accepted heresies → acceptance defined → normalization and institutionalization distinguished → biblical words collected → objects distinguished → premises already in force used, not retried → one clean account of sequence and limits → positive warrant from the non-transforming character of reception, from the writings’ exhibition of settlement, and from the real possibility of refusal → each exhibition examined with biblical record → operations of acceptance joined → non-transformation stated from the exhibitions → reconstructible Introduction and Aletheia propositions tested as coherence → competing reductions refused → inspectable inference → warranted conclusion → sequence to aridity.**

The chapter’s conclusion is affirmative:

> **An accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine that has become the ordinary teaching of a body, or that has been installed in that body’s places, priesthood, calendar, official mouth, school, penalty, or suffered teaching office, so that the error is now what the body holds, teaches, commands, or will not depart from. The writings exhibit how that settlement happens: by installation that imitates an authorized feast; by a court that speaks with one mouth; by appeal to the king’s chapel; by a people who love to have it so; by a claim to possess the law while the word is rejected; by the manner of the fathers; by teaching the commandments of men as doctrines and teaching men to break the commandment; by the named doctrine of a school; by an agreement to expel confessors; by an assembly’s command; by words that travel under a sending the senders did not give; by the carrying-away of respected men into one public walk; by the following of many and the slander of the way of truth; by a church that holds a doctrine and suffers a teacher; by ordinances that have a show of wisdom; by prohibitions taught as the rule; by a letter that wears an apostolic name; by a common report the body glories in. Institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth. A multitude is forbidden as a measure. A sign that comes to pass does not license the other gods. A sin successors will not depart from remains a sin. A chapel does not make a cult the Lord’s house. Fathers who did not hearken are the ground of wrath, not of legitimacy. Vain worship is worship that teaches human commandments as doctrines. The way of truth remains the way of truth while many follow the heresies and speak evil of the way. Christ hates the doctrine the church suffers. The creature remains good while a doctrine forbids it. What a hostile body calls heresy may be the way that believes all that is written, and what a body calls the faith may be the error. Names do not settle the case. Truth remains conformity to reality. The Graphē remains the primary written authority. The Scripture is not broken by a kingdom’s continuance in a sin, by a council’s command, or by a church’s toleration. Refusal remains possible: the multitude may be disobeyed; the book found in the house judges the fathers’ way; one prophet may speak what the Lord says against four hundred; the rest in a church may not have the doctrine; God is to be obeyed rather than men. This continues Movement IX. It is not Chapter 70 retried. It is not Chapters 72–73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.**

The remaining questions follow by sequence. The verdict is already in force as a warranted account of accepted heresies, not as postponed guesswork.

# 71.1 The Question Created by the Preceding Chapter

Movement IX is open. Its first word has been stated. The authority of the Graphē and the authority claimed for a later statement of sense are two objects. Transfer fails. Despair fails. Its second word has been stated. The later act fails in inspectable modes: poor perception, deficient understanding, faulty inference, context failure, and improper handling. The writing remains the measure. A correct reading remains possible. An incorrect reading remains incorrect. Its third word has been stated. Theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution are secondary systems. They may serve under the writing. None becomes the primary written authority merely by claiming Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition. Its fourth word has been stated. When commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it, the secondary source occupies the seat of sense and the test is reversed. The writing is not broken. Service is not the event. Its fifth word has been stated. Doctrinal turning aside is an inspectable movement from a truth the Graphē has given, carried by causes and mechanisms the writings name, permitted by intellectual failures that do not excuse it. The truth left remains the measure. Continuance is a real contrary. The distinction-file is in force. The catalog is in force. The rank is in force. The displacement-file is in force. The turning-file is in force.

Chapter 70 established the movement of departure. That conclusion is a premise here. A stated turning still leaves a further question: how does the erroneous doctrine become normalized or institutionalized, and why does the body’s acceptance fail to transform the error into truth?

A people can receive the turning-file as a piety — “we know men can leave the truth” — and still walk in the sin a king installed, still love the arrangement in which prophets prophesy falsely and priests bear rule by their means, still hold a doctrine Christ hates, still suffer a teacher who calls herself a prophetess, still treat the chapel’s word as the faith because the chapel is the king’s. They can quote Chapter 70’s refusal of harmlessness and still offer the following of many as if the following had ended the question. The turning has named the movement. The settlement of the error as the ordinary doctrine is a further object.

The question is therefore not:

> **What are the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside?**

That question has been answered.

The question is:

> **How do erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized, and why does institutional acceptance not transform error into truth?**

If Movement IX proceeded from the turning to aridity without examining acceptance, it would skip the locked step. If it treated this file as already Chapter 70, it would convert an acceptance-file into a second turning-file. If it treated this file as already Chapters 72–73 or Movement X, it would close the movement’s later questions inside its sixth word. The present file is the dedicated examination of accepted heresies.

That is a different operation from a repeated warning that error is error. It is the operation this chapter must perform.

# 71.2 What This Chapter Does Not Repeat

Chapters 1–3 established truth as conformity to reality, distinct from belief, popularity, institutional consensus, and sincerity as a determinant of truth. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening ontology of truth. It uses truth as already defined, now as the reality an accepted doctrine either conforms to or does not, and as the reality no reception can redefine.

Chapters 4–7 established knowledge, evidence, reason, and rational warrant as inspectable operations. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening epistemology. It uses reason as already defined, now as the operation by which a doctrine a body has received is tested against what the writing gave.

Chapter 13 established knowing God as revelation rather than speculation. Chapter 14 established that human accounts about God are themselves to be tested. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write them. It uses them as the ground on which a received human doctrine about God can be named as received without being mistaken for revelation because a house teaches it.

Chapters 20–22 established γραφή (*graphē*, G1124) as writing that, in biblical usage, designates Holy Writ / Scripture. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the lexical files of the writing. It uses them: the measure of an accepted doctrine, where the doctrine claims to be the faith, is the writing.

Chapters 51–53 established the scriptural corpus, recognition as reception rather than creation, and prophetic and apostolic authority. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the canon-file. It uses the distinction already earned: a body’s reception of a book does not create the book’s authority. The same logic now meets a body’s reception of a doctrine. Reception is not creation. The canon-argument is not reprinted. It is applied to a different object, the doctrine a body calls its own.

Chapter 57 established that the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates, and that this non-failure is not the infallibility of the interpreter, the church as church, or every later tradition. Chapters 62–63 established that the Scripture cannot be broken. Chapter 65 established the Graphē as the primary written authority. Chapter 66 distinguished that standing from the standing claimed for a later statement of sense, and already refused both transfer and despair. Chapter 67 examined how the later act fails, and already established that a correct reading remains possible and an incorrect reading remains incorrect. Chapter 68 ranked the four systems and refused them primary standing by identity, academy, antiquity, or recognition. Chapter 69 examined what happens when secondary sources govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it. Chapter 70 examined the causes and mechanisms of doctrinal turning aside and the intellectual failures that permit departure from truth. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try them. It performs the examination of accepted heresies that Chapter 70 reserved.

This chapter does not recatalogue the calf of Exodus 32, the removal of Galatians 1, the itching ear of 2 Timothy 4, or the privy bringing-in of 2 Peter 2:1 as if the turning were still in doubt. It may use passages those chapters have already handled when the new function is the settlement of an erroneous doctrine as a body’s ordinary or official teaching, and the failure of that settlement to transform error into truth. The new function is this:

> **To examine how erroneous doctrines become normalized or institutionalized; to show why institutional acceptance does not transform error into truth; and to leave aridity, *apeiros*, labour, and the First Principles in their assigned files.**

# 71.3 Define the Question: Accepted Heresies

**Accepted heresy**, in this chapter, is an erroneous doctrine that a body has received as its ordinary teaching, or has installed in the forms by which it orders what is believed, taught, and enforced, so that the error presents itself as the doctrine, the manner, the faith, or the rule.

The English phrase is not a biblical hapax to be imported as a new revelation. It is the locked assignment’s name for a settlement the writings already exhibit. “Heresy” in later controversy often means a chosen doctrine formally contrary to a defined rule of a communion, held with persistence. That later technical sense is not the premise of this chapter, and it is not silently installed as the meaning of every Greek line below. The argumentative force of the assignment is narrower and prior: an error in doctrine has become what a body treats as normal, or what a body has built into its public order, and the question is how that happens and why the happening does not make the error true.

The phrase is easily abused. In ordinary speech “accepted” may be heard as any teaching a Christian may hold without suspicion, so that every received truth is already on trial as a heresy. “Heresy” may be heard as a sneer at every party one does not belong to, so that the opponent’s name is already the verdict. “Institutional” may be heard as a sneer at every ordered body, so that a church, a school, or a household is guilty by existing. None of those senses is this chapter’s object.

Four elements belong to the definition.

First, **an erroneous doctrine**. The object is a teaching, a διδαχή (*didachē*, G1322), a commandment taught as doctrine, a required account of what saves, a prohibition taught as the faith, a sentence about God and his worship that does not conform to the reality the writing has given. A custom with no doctrinal claim is not yet this object. A moral disorder the body also fails to mourn can exhibit the same structure of normalization, and one exhibition below uses that structure. The assigned object remains the doctrine. Error has already been distinguished from truth. This chapter does not re-open that distinction. It asks what happens when the error is the thing a body now teaches.

Second, **received by a body as ordinary, or installed in the body’s order**. Normalization is the error’s becoming the usual teaching: the way of the people, the manner of the fathers, the path many follow, the doctrine held, the thing loved, the report no longer mourned. Institutionalization is the error’s installation in the forms of a public order: a place of worship, a priesthood, a calendar, an official mouth, a school’s doctrine, a penalty of expulsion, a command of an assembly, a teaching office the church suffers to continue. The two are modes of one acceptance. A doctrine can be normal in a people’s love before it has a chapel. A doctrine can be installed in a chapel while some in the assembly have not received it. The chapter does not require both modes in every case. It does require that the error have become the body’s teaching or the body’s rule, and not merely a motion in one hearer that Chapter 70 already judged.

Third, **the reception offered as though it settled truth**. The theological force of the file is not only that bodies adopt errors. It is that the adoption is then treated as the reason the doctrine should be believed: because the people went, because the prophets speak with one mouth, because this is the king’s chapel, because our fathers walked in it, because we did not depart from it, because the synagogue has agreed, because she calls herself a prophetess, because we are wise and the law is with us, because many follow. The assignment’s second clause is the refusal of that offer. Acceptance is a historical and social fact. It is not an ontological act.

Fourth, **not those other claims**. The definition excludes, as not this object: a retry of Chapter 70’s causes and mechanisms of turning; aridity as the loss of reasonability; *apeiros* as unskillfulness in the Word; Movement X’s labour-files; the First Principles as this file’s achievement; a history of post-apostolic parties as the premise; a polity of councils as the cure. Those exclusions are part of the definition. They are not a later apology.

Thus:

> **The question of this chapter is not what causes a turning, and not yet how reasonability is lost or how skill is gained. Those questions have been examined or remain later. The question is how an erroneous doctrine becomes the ordinary or official teaching of a body, and why that body’s acceptance does not make the error true.**

---

# 71.4 Normalized and Institutionalized

The assignment names two operations. They are distinguished here so that a chapel is not required before an error can be the ordinary doctrine, and so that a vague mood of “everyone thinks so” is not treated as an institution.

**Normalized.** An erroneous doctrine is normalized when it has become the unremarkable teaching of a body: what the people love to have, what the fathers did, what many follow, what is held as “the doctrine,” what is commonly reported and gloried in, what the prophet of this people says because this people will have him. The mark is ordinariness. The error no longer has to be brought in beside the faith as a stranger. It is the house’s voice. Chapter 70 reserved this thickening. “Many shall follow their pernicious ways” was read there as a following. The following, become the path one does not apologize for, is this mode.

**Institutionalized.** An erroneous doctrine is institutionalized when it has been set into the ordering forms of a body: altars and houses of high places; priests made from those who are not the priests of the writing; a feast in a month devised of a king’s heart; a court of prophets who answer with one mouth; a sanctuary called the king’s chapel; a seat from which burdens are bound; an agreement that confession will be punished by expulsion from the assembly; a command of the council; a man who casts out of the church those who would receive the brethren; a teacher the church suffers to teach. The mark is installation. The error has furniture, office, calendar, or sanction.

The relation between the modes is exhibited, not theorized in the abstract. Jeroboam’s calves are installed, and then the people go, and then the thing becomes a sin, and then later kings depart not from it. Installation and normalization confirm one another in that narrative. They are still distinguishable. The devising of the feast is the king’s act. The not-departing of successors is the continuance of a people and a dynasty in what was devised. Thyatira suffers a teacher, which is institutional permission, and some have the doctrine while the rest have not, which shows that institutional permission and universal inward consent are not the same fact. A doctrine can be the church’s tolerated teaching while a remnant has not received it. The remnant’s existence does not make the toleration unreal. The toleration’s existence does not make the remnant’s refusal a second doctrine of equal truth. The writing addresses both.

Thus:

> **Normalization is the error become ordinary teaching. Institutionalization is the error installed in a body’s ordering forms. Accepted heresy is the name of the settlement either mode, or both, produces. Neither mode is the transformation of the error into truth.**

---

# 71.5 The Biblical Words the Name Collects

The writings do not use one Greek word for every settled error. The chapter collects the words that bear on choosing, holding, teaching, and suffering a doctrine, and it keeps them distinct so that a lexicon is not mistaken for the argument.

**αἵρεσις (*hairesis*, G139).** From αἱρέω, to take or choose. In the Acts passages the word names a party: the sect of the Sadducees (Acts 5:17), the sect of the Pharisees (Acts 15:5; 26:5), the sect of the Nazarenes as Tertullus calls it (Acts 24:5), “this sect” as the Roman Jews have heard it spoken against (Acts 28:22), and “the way which they call heresy” (Acts 24:14). In those lines the word is a party-designation. It does not, by itself, decide that the party’s doctrine is false. Paul uses the opponents’ word and then states the actual relation: he worships the God of the fathers, believing all things written in the law and the prophets. In 1 Corinthians 11:19, Galatians 5:20, and 2 Peter 2:1 the word names a chosen line that divides. Galatians lists it among the works of the flesh, beside seditions. First Corinthians says there must be heresies among the church, that the approved may be made manifest. Second Peter speaks of αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, heresies of destruction, privily brought in, which deny the Master who bought them. Chapter 70 took the privy bringing-in as a mechanism of turning. This chapter takes the word’s force as a chosen teaching that can be the thing a body follows, calls a sect, or suffers as doctrine. The party-name and the destructive choice are not one lexeme-use. Collapsing them would make every sect-label an accepted heresy, which Acts 24:14 forbids, or would empty 2 Peter 2:1 of the doctrines that destroy.

**αἱρετικός (*hairetikos*, G141).** Titus 3:10 only in the New Testament. The factious man, the man who chooses a line of his own. After a first and a second admonition, he is to be rejected. The admonitions mark settlement. The choice has been addressed and has remained his. He is subverted, he sins, and he is self-condemned. The word names a person whose chosen line has become his standing position. It does not name a vote by which a church creates truth or creates falsehood.

**διδαχή (*didachē*, G1322) and the verbs of holding and permitting.** Matthew 16:12 identifies the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees as their doctrine. Revelation 2:14 speaks of those who hold (ἔχω) the doctrine of Balaam. Revelation 2:15 speaks of those who hold (κρατέω, G2902) the doctrine of the Nicolaitans. Revelation 2:24 speaks of the rest who have not this doctrine. The doctrine is a distinguishable teaching some have and some have not. Revelation 2:20 uses ἀφίημι: thou sufferest, thou permittest, that woman Jezebel to teach. Permission to teach is the institutional act. The doctrine held is the content. Christ’s “which thing I hate” is the verdict the permission does not revise.

**δόγμα (*dogma*, G1378) and δογματίζω (*dogmatizō*, G1379).** Colossians 2:20 asks why, if the readers have died with Christ from the rudiments of the world, they are subjected to ordinances — touch not, taste not, handle not — after the commandments and doctrines of men. The ordinances have a show of wisdom. The show is relevant because show is one way a human doctrine becomes acceptable as a rule. The verb of subjection names the body’s coming under the rule. It does not name the rule’s truth.

These words are one assignment because each can mark an erroneous teaching that a body chooses, holds, teaches, suffers, or submits to. They are not one lexeme. A sect-name used by an accuser, a fleshly party, a destructive teaching many follow, a factious man who will not be admonished off his line, a school’s doctrine, a doctrine held in a church, and a set of ordinances with a religious show are exhibitions of acceptance in different courts. Collapsing the words into a single technical term of later controversy would hide the exhibitions. Leaving them unjoined would hide the assignment.

Thus:

> **Accepted heresy, in this argument, is the erroneous doctrine the writings exhibit as chosen, held, taught, suffered, or submitted to by a body. *Hairesis* keeps its range: party-name, fleshly faction, destructive choice. *Hairetikos* names the settled chooser. *Didachē* names the teaching held or not held. *Dogma* names the ordinance a body comes under. The words stay distinct. The object they serve in this file is one.**

---

# 71.6 Distinguish Objects That Must Not Be Collapsed

The investigation fails at the first step if it treats different objects as one.

**This acceptance and Chapter 70’s turning.** This chapter examines settlement. Chapter 70 examined departure. A turning can thicken into a normal doctrine. The thickening is not the departure restated, and the departure is not unstated because the thickening has its own file. A person can turn and still meet a body that has not made the error its doctrine. A body can hold an erroneous doctrine as its ordinary teaching long after the first movers are dead, so that the present members do not experience themselves as turning at all. They experience themselves as faithful to the chapel, the fathers, the school, or the feast. That experience is the reason this file exists. To treat this chapter as Chapter 70 retried would hide the settlement inside another account of the leaving. To omit the settlement in order to protect the turning-file would leave the turning unjoined to the sixth word Movement IX assigns.

**Acceptance and the governance of meaning.** Chapter 69 examined what happens when a secondary source occupies the seat of sense. A governor can be the condition under which an error is called the sense of the writing. The condition does not make the accepted doctrine a reprint of the occupation. A doctrine can become the ordinary teaching of a people by a feast, a priesthood, a loved arrangement, and a following, and the question of this file is the doctrine’s reception, not a second description of the seat. A court can be tempted to govern and still teach what the writing gives. Governance is a standing premise. It is not the whole of acceptance, and acceptance is not the proof that Chapter 69 was incomplete.

**Acceptance and the rank of institutions.** Chapter 68 refused theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution the office of primary written authority by Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or recognition. That rank is in force. This chapter does not re-argue it. The new object is the erroneous doctrine’s becoming the body’s teaching. An institution can be secondary and still teach the truth under the writing. An institution can be secondary and teach an error it has come to call the faith. The rank explains why the institution’s recognition cannot save the error. It does not itself narrate how the error became the teaching. Narrating that settlement is this file.

**The body’s reception of a truth and the body’s reception of an error.** A church can hold the doctrine it was taught. Acts 2:42 speaks of continuing stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine. Second Thessalonians 2:15 commands holding the traditions taught by the apostle’s word or epistle. That holding is reception of a given truth. It does not create the truth, and it is not an accepted heresy. The hostile name “heresy” can be laid on that holding, as Acts 24:14 records. The name fails. Despair, already refused in Chapter 66, is refused again if someone infers from this chapter that every body is an accepted heresy by being a body. The object is the erroneous doctrine received, not the existence of reception.

**A question not closed by the writing and an accepted heresy.** Chapter 70 refused the reduction that every disagreement is tergiversation. The same refusal holds here. A question the writings have not closed is not, by the mere fact that a school answers it one way and another school another way, an accepted heresy of the school one dislikes. The error in this file is error relative to truth the writing has given: another god assigned the exodus, a human commandment taught as God’s, a condition of salvation the apostles did not command, a denial of the Master, a doctrine Christ names and hates, a prohibition of what God created to be received. Where the writing has not settled the question, this chapter does not appoint the louder school’s doctrine as heresy or as orthodoxy.

**Acceptance and the truth’s survival.** Men can receive an error as the faith of their house for generations. They cannot, by receiving it, make it conform to reality. The calves remain a sin while Israel walks in them and departs not. The way of truth remains the way of truth while it is evil spoken of. The Scripture is not broken by the reception. The reception succeeds as the settlement of a body’s teaching. It fails as an ontological correction of God.

**This chapter and later files.** Aridity, *apeiros*, scholarly labour, *spoudazō*, and the First Principles remain later. A body that holds an error may also be dry of judgment and unskillful in the word. Appearance is not those files written now. The intellectual failures Chapter 70 identified remain premises of how departure is permitted. They are not re-diagnosed here as the loss of reasonability. The next chapter will examine that loss. This chapter examines the settlement the loss does not have to be fully described in order for the settlement to be judged.

Thus:

> **Accepted heresy is an erroneous doctrine received as a body’s ordinary teaching or installed in its order. It is not the turning retried, not the displacement retried, not the rank-file retried, not every reception, not every open question, not the abolition of the truth, and not the later files under another name.**
