This principle is headed by the Greek terms μετάνοια (metanoia, G3341) and νεκρῶν ἔργων (nekrōn ergōn): repentance from dead works.

Hebrews 6:1 has already named the foundation: repentance from dead works. Μετάνοια (metanoia) is the change of mind. Νεκρῶν ἔργων (nekrōn ergōn) names the dead works. You will not flatten either term into a mood.

Μετάνοια (metanoia, G3341) is a real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, not merely the consequences of it. The governing verses here are Matthew 3:8, Matthew 3:11, Matthew 9:13, and Luke 24:47. They will be quoted in full in section II. Hear the definition first, then the verses, then the distinction from μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai, G3338).

Metanoia specifies compunction (remorse) for guilt including reformation: regeneration, quickening, recreation — “new creature.” A real change of mind and attitude over sin and the cause. All things are become new.

It is not a mood. It is not a tear without a turn. It includes reformation because the man in Christ is a new creature. Compunction without reformation is not the metanoia named here. Reformation without blood is still a dead work; section VI will not let you make self-reformation the way. Hold both.

2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

Who writes? Paul. To whom? The church at Corinth, a people he must still reason with about ministry and reconciliation. Why here? This verse is used four ways in one principle: new creature, change, old things deceased, in-Christ location. If any man be in Christ — the location is Christ, not a course enrolment. He is a new creature — recreation, not a repaired mood. Old things are passed away — section IV will name two kinds. Behold, all things are become new — “all things are become new” is not a slogan for a new year. It is the state of the man in Christ.

B. Νεκρῶν ἔργων

Νεκρῶν ἔργων (nekrōn ergōn) — dead works — are the works of the old man: the spirit and nature of the devil (Ephesians 4:22); old things (2 Corinthians 5:17); the old nature (Ephesians 2:1 — trespasses, a deviation from moral equity, and sins). The wages thereof is death (Romans 6:23).

The phrase is not an eighth word and not a second doctrine. Dead works are works of the old man and works of the old nature.

Ephesians 4:22 — “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;”

Ephesians 2:1 — “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;”

Trespasses, in Ephesians 2:1, are deviation from moral equity, and sins. Dead works are not “things I did that felt empty.” A man may call a boring task a dead work because it bored him. Scripture calls a work dead because it is of the old man and the old nature. Do not confuse them.

Romans 6:23 will be opened in section V. Hear its clause now so the wage is not a surprise: the wages of sin is death. Dead works earn that wage. The conscience is later purged from them by blood (Hebrews 9:14). That purge is not this heading. This heading is the change of mind over the works and over the cause that produced them.

C. Reversal of another’s decision

By implication the word also carries reversal of another’s decision. Do not flatten that into a technique. Keep this: repentance is not less than a change of mind. A change of mind can reverse what a man had decided, and what he had followed in another’s decision. It is still a change of mind over sin and its cause. It is not a method for managing rooms.

D. Distinction, principle, charge

Distinction: μετάνοια (metanoia) as real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, including reformation and the new creature, versus a tear without a turn versus a mood versus a regret of consequences only. Dead works are works of the old man and old nature, not tasks that bored you.

Principle: the first stone is μετάνοια from νεκρῶν ἔργων: repentance from dead works. The man in Christ is a new creature. Old things pass. The wage of the old things is death.

Reasoning: if μετάνοια were a feeling, 2 Corinthians 5:17 would be a feeling. If dead works were boredom, Hebrews 9:14 would purge boredom. If reformation could be detached from the new creature, this school would not name regeneration, quickening, recreation in one breath with “new creature.”

Application: name one work you have called “dead” because it bored you, and one the Scripture would call a dead work because it is of the old man. Do not submit the first as if it were the second.

Charge: write Hebrews 6:1 and 2 Corinthians 5:17. Then write ten lines: what μετάνοια (metanoia) is, what νεκρῶν ἔργων (nekrōn ergōn) are, and where you have treated a tear as if it were a new creature.

II. SEVEN ORIGINAL WORDS FOR REPENT

Metanoia is one of the original words for repentance. The authorized list for this school is seven. We will not invent an eighth. We will not pad the list with a seminary word the house did not send.

Hold each word as the list uses it. Quote the verse. Set the context. Do not merge 6 and 7.

A. Hebrew nacham (H5162)

Nacham: to sigh, breathe strongly, to be sorry. The addresses: Genesis 6:6; Exodus 13:17; Job 42:6; Jonah 3:10.

Genesis 6:6 — “And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.”

The LORD, over man’s wickedness. Nacham here is grief and being sorry, a strong breathing of sorrow. It is not Matthew 27:3. It is the word the list gives you first: sigh, breathe strongly, be sorry.

Exodus 13:17 — “And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:”

The people, of the way out, when they see war. Nacham here can name a sorry that is not yet holiness.

Job 42:6 — “Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Job, after the LORD had spoken. Nacham here is sorrow in the dust. Do not make Job’s dust the whole foundation. The foundation in Hebrews is metanoia from dead works, in Christ.

Jonah 3:10 — “And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.”

Nineveh turned. God saw their works and repented of the evil He had said He would do. Nacham here is being sorry, a relenting. Hold the word: sigh, breathe strongly, be sorry.

B. Hebrew shuwb (H7725)

Shuwb: to turn back. The addresses: 1 Kings 8:47; Ezekiel 14:6.

1 Kings 8:47 — “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;”

Solomon, at the dedication, concerning captives. They must bethink themselves, repent, make supplication, name the sin. Shuwb is the turn back. A man can be sorry and not turn.

Ezekiel 14:6 — “Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations.”

The Lord GOD to Israel, idols in the heart. Shuwb is commanded: turn from idols and abominations. The turn has an object. It is not a mood in the room.

C. Hebrew nocham (H5164)

Nocham: regret. The address: Hosea 13:14.

Hosea 13:14 — “I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.”

The LORD, concerning Ephraim. Repentance — nocham, regret — shall be hid from His eyes. Learn the word as regret. It is not metanoia. It is not an eighth.

D. Hebrew nichuwm (H5150)

Nichuwm: compassion. The address: Hosea 11:8.

Hosea 11:8 — “How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together.”

The LORD over Ephraim. His repentings — nichuwm, compassion — are kindled. Hold it as compassion. Do not merge it with metanoia to make a softer gospel.

E. Greek metanoeō (G3340)

Metanoeō: to change the mind for the better morally; to change the attitude toward sin. The address: Luke 13:3.

Luke 13:3 — “I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.”

Read the verse in its place. Some told Jesus of the Galilaeans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. He asked if those Galilaeans were sinners above all Galilaeans because they suffered such things. He said, Nay. Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. He added the eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and said the same.

Luke 13:4 — “Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?”

Luke 13:5 — “I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.”

Who speaks? The Lord. To whom? Dwellers who wanted a ranking of sinners by disaster. Why? Because they were reading consequence as if it were the measure of cause, and He turned them to their own need of a changed mind.

Metanoeō here is a change of mind toward sin, not a regret that the tower fell on someone else. If you treat disaster as the definition of repentance, you have not heard Luke 13. If you treat another man’s ruin as your repentance, you have not changed your mind.

F. Greek μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai) (G3338)

Metamellomai: to regret consequences of sin, not the cause. The addresses: Matthew 27:3; 2 Corinthians 7:8. Judas is the teaching case. Consequences only.

Matthew 27:3 — “Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,”

Matthew 27:4 — “Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.”

Matthew 27:5 — “And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.”

Who? Judas, which had betrayed Him. When? When he saw that He was condemned. What did he do? Repented himself — μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai) — brought again the silver, said he had sinned in betraying innocent blood, cast the silver down, went and hanged himself.

He regretted the consequence. He saw the condemnation. He felt the weight of the silver. He used the word “sinned.” He did not come to a new mind over sin and its cause. He did not become a new creature. He did not receive the One he betrayed. He went and hanged himself.

If you treat Judas’s remorse as if it were metanoia, you have not laid this foundation. You have laid a feeling. A man can say “I have sinned,” return money, and still perish in the cause. Metamellomai can go as far as suicide and still not be the first stone.

2 Corinthians 7:8 — “For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.”

Who writes? Paul, concerning a severe letter. Metamellomai here is his own regret about the sorrow the letter produced — a regret of a consequence — and then his refusal to remain in that regret. The list places this verse with consequences, not the cause. Do not turn Paul’s sentence into an eighth word. Do not turn it into Judas. Use it as the list uses it: μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai) can name regret of a result.

G. Greek metanoia (G3341)

Metanoia: a real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, not merely the consequences. The addresses: Matthew 3:8, 11; 9:13; Luke 24:47.

Matthew 3:8 — “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:”

Who speaks? John the Baptist, to Pharisees and Sadducees who came to his baptism. Why? Because they were fleeing wrath as a consequence and needed to be told that repentance has fruit. Metanoia that has no fruit is not the change the word names. Reformation is in the definition. Fruit is in the verse.

Matthew 3:11 — “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:”

John’s water is unto repentance. The Mightier baptizes with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Course 3 will open baptisms. Here the verse stands as a metanoia address: the change of mind is not a private tear. It is the repentance John’s baptism pointed to, and it is not yet the whole of what the Mightier does.

Matthew 9:13 — “But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

Who speaks? Jesus, to those who asked why He ate with publicans and sinners. Why? Because they thought the righteous were the company, and He came to call sinners to metanoia. The change of mind is for sinners, over sin and its cause. A man who will not take the name sinner will not take this stone.

Luke 24:47 — “And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.”

Who speaks? The risen Lord, opening their understanding, sending them. What is to be preached? Repentance and remission of sins in His name, among all nations. Metanoia is not a private Jewish mood. It is preached in His name. Section VI will not let you put another name in that place. Section VII will not let you postpone receiving Him until a later course.

H. Hold 6 and 7 until you can teach the difference in your sleep

Metamellomai regrets consequences of sin, not the cause. Metanoia is a real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, not merely the consequences.

Judas is 6. Luke 13:3 is 5, the verb of changed mind. Matthew 3:8 is 7, fruit meet for the noun. If you cannot keep those three files apart, you cannot teach this principle.

I. Charge

Write the seven words with one verse each, in full, KJV. Then write ten lines: where have you treated regret as if it were metanoia? Name Judas if you have used his remorse as a pattern. Name the tower if you have used another man’s ruin as your repentance. Do not invent an eighth word to make the page look fuller.

III. CAUSE, NOT CONSEQUENCE

Hell is a consequence. It is not the definition of repentance.

Matthew 16 is not this narrative. This school teaches Luke 16:19-31. With Revelation 20:10-15 as the final lake. Do not teach Matthew 16 as the rich man and Lazarus. Do not teach Matthew 16 as the lake of fire.

A. Luke 16:19-31 — the narrative of the consequence

Luke 16:19 — “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:”

Luke 16:20 — “And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,”

Luke 16:21 — “And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.”

Luke 16:22 — “And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;”

Luke 16:23 — “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.”

Luke 16:24 — “And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.”

Luke 16:25 — “But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.”

Luke 16:26 — “And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

Luke 16:27 — “Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house:”

Luke 16:28 — “For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

Luke 16:29 — “Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.”

Luke 16:30 — “And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.”

Luke 16:31 — “And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

The Lord is speaking. The living already have Moses and the prophets. A great gulf is fixed. No crossing. No extra witness from the dead. That narrative is the consequence: torment, flame, gulf.

The rich man, already in the flame, wants his brothers not to come there. That wish is Hell-avoidance. It is not metanoia in the brothers, and it is not metanoia in him. A man may fear that fire and still love the cause of his death.

Chapter 7 will open Paradise, Hell, and the emptying of the righteous. Here you will not turn Luke 16 into the five prisons. Fear of torment is not yet the first stone.

B. Revelation 20:10-15 — the end of the consequence

Revelation 20:10 — “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.”

Revelation 20:11 — “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.”

Revelation 20:12 — “And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

Revelation 20:13 — “And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.”

Revelation 20:14 — “And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.”

Revelation 20:15 — “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

That is the end of the consequence. The lake of fire. The second death. Chapter 7 will open the book, the blotting, the three deaths, and the five prisons. Here the point is narrower: if your “repentance” is only the wish not to go there, you have not yet changed your mind over sin and its cause. A man can study the lake and remain in love with the cause.

C. Distinction, principle, charge

Distinction: repentance over sin and its cause versus Hell-avoidance versus Judas’s regret of condemnation versus the rich man’s wish that his brothers not come into torment.

Principle: Hell is a consequence. Luke 16:19-31 shows it. Revelation 20:10-15 ends it. Metanoia is not defined by that fear.

Reasoning: if Hell-avoidance were metanoia, the rich man’s request for his brothers would be the first stone. Abraham would have sent Lazarus. The Lord would not have said they have Moses and the prophets. If Matthew 16 were this narrative, this school would teach Matthew 16. That reference was an error. We will not repeat it.

Application: where have you treated Hell-avoidance as if it were metanoia? Where have you preached the flame and omitted the cause? Where have you used fear as if it were a new creature?

Charge: write Luke 16:27-31 in your own hand. What did Abraham refuse? Why were Moses and the prophets enough? Then write Revelation 20:15. Then write one paragraph that does not mention the lake until it has named sin and its cause.

IV. TWO OLD THINGS THAT MUST PASS

2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

Repentance from dead works delineates two kinds of “old things” deceased — passed away.

These two old things are not one pile labelled “sin” so that you can hide the old man behind a list of acts, or hide the acts behind a theory of nature. Both must pass. In Christ they are passed away.

A. Old thing 1 — the old man

The spirit, nature, and power of sin — the old man: nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience.

Do not reduce the old man to a bad habit. This teaching will not let you. The old man is the spirit and nature of the devil in the disobedient. Nothing more nor less. That sentence stands. Do not soften it into a personality type.

John 8:44 — “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

Jesus, to men who claimed Abraham and God as father while they sought to kill Him. You cannot teach this verse as a bad habit.

Ephesians 2:2 — “Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:”

The old man is not an unused costume. The spirit worketh. Disobedience has children. The prince has a course.

2 Corinthians 4:4 — “In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.”

Chapter 3 will open image. Here the verse sits in the old-man Scripture set: a blinding power, minds held from the gospel. That is not a habit.

1 John 3:8 — “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.”

1 John 3:9 — “Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.”

Hold 3:8 and 3:9. Do not soften this Scripture set. Do not invent a third nature this school does not name. The old man is of the devil. The born of God is another creature. That is why old things pass.

1 John 5:18 — “We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.”

Sinneth not. Keepeth himself. The wicked one toucheth him not. The old-man file ends, in this Scripture set, with a man the wicked one does not touch — not because the man is careful in a slogan, but because he is begotten of God.

Ephesians 4:22 — “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;”

Ephesians 4:23 — “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;”

Ephesians 4:24 — “And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

The former conversation is not a list of quirks. It is the walk of the old man. Do not use 4:22 to hide the list of acts, and do not use the list to hide 4:22.

Scripture set held: John 8:44; Ephesians 2:2; 2 Corinthians 4:4; 1 John 3:8-9; 1 John 5:18; Ephesians 4:22. One old thing. Spirit, nature, and power of sin. Nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience.

Charge on old thing 1: can you teach John 8:44, Ephesians 2:2, and 1 John 3:8-9 as one Scripture set without calling the old man “a bad habit”? Write the teaching in one page. If you are on The Walk, one tight page. If you are on The Intensive, one page that walks each verse and then the Scripture set.

B. Old thing 2 — outward sin

Outward sin is the second old thing. It has its own Scripture file. It is not another name for the old man.

Galatians 5:19 — “Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,”

Galatians 5:20 — “Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,”

Galatians 5:21 — “Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.”

This is not a curiosity. This is outward sin named. Walk the list without calling it “the old man.” The old man produces works. The works are the second old thing. Both must pass.

1 John 3:4 — “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is the transgression of the law. Outward sin has a definition. It is not a vibe. It is transgression.

Romans 4:15 — “Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.”

The law worketh wrath. Where no law is, there is no transgression. Hold this with 1 John 3:4. Transgression is not an invention of mood. Wrath is not an invention of preachers. The second old thing sits under law and wrath.

James 1:13 — “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:”

James 1:14 — “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.”

James 1:15 — “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.”

The second old thing has a genealogy: lust, conception, sin, death. Do not blame God for the line. Do not stop the line at a private lust and pretend the child was never born.

Mark 7:20 — “And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.”

Mark 7:21 — “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,”

Mark 7:22 — “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:”

Mark 7:23 — “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

This teaching places Mark 7:19-21. The account you must teach is 7:20-23. Outward sin is not a stain that fell on a clean man from a dirty world. It proceeds. It defiles.

Romans 1:18 — “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;”

Romans 1:19 — “Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.”

Romans 1:20 — “For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:”

Romans 1:21 — “Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.”

Romans 1:22 — “Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,”

Romans 1:23 — “And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.”

Romans 1:24 — “Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:”

Romans 1:25 — “Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.”

Romans 1:26 — “For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:”

Romans 1:27 — “And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.”

Romans 1:28 — “And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;”

Romans 1:29 — “Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,”

Romans 1:30 — “Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,”

Romans 1:31 — “Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:”

Romans 1:32 — “Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.”

The catalogue is not a curiosity. It is outward sin named. Without excuse. Given up. Given over. Worthy of death. This teaching cited 1:18-32. This school teaches 1:18-32.

C. Both, not one pile

You cannot hide the old man behind a list of acts. You cannot hide the acts behind a theory of nature. Walk Galatians 5:19-21 and Mark 7:20-23 without calling them “the old man.” Then state what must pass besides the list: the spirit and nature of the devil working in the disobedient.

In Christ they are passed away. That is 2 Corinthians 5:17. If they have not passed, you are not finished with this stone because you have named the lists. Naming is not passing. Passing is in Christ.

D. Charge

What old thing has not passed? Which of the two kinds is it? Write the name. Write the verses. Do not write “sin” as a pile. If you cannot separate the two files, you have not laid this part of the stone.

V. THE WAGES

Romans 6:23 — “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Read the verse in Romans 6. You were the servants of sin. You are to be the servants of righteousness. Death is the wage of the old things. Eternal life is the gift of God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Romans 6:16 — “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?”

Romans 6:17 — “But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.”

Romans 6:18 — “Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.”

Romans 6:19 — “I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.”

Romans 6:20 — “For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.”

Romans 6:21 — “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.”

Romans 6:22 — “But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.”

Romans 6:23 — “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

They yield to a master. The old master pays death. God gives eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Wage versus gift. Do not build a repentance that wants to keep the cause and escape the wage.

Hold the line: salvation from sin is exclusively the only salvation you need, sin being the cause of all death and depravity. Not salvation from boredom. Not salvation from a small life. Not salvation from other people’s opinions. Salvation from sin. Sin is the cause of all death and depravity. If you have put another “salvation” in that place, you have moved the stone.

Death in this book is not only the stopping of breath. Chapter 7 will open three kinds of death. Here it is enough to refuse a repentance that wants to keep the cause and escape the wage.

Principle: the wages of sin is death. The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Salvation from sin is the salvation you need.

Charge: what other “salvation” have you put in the place of salvation from sin? Write Romans 6:23, then write the clause that names the gift. Then write Romans 6:21 and name the fruit you were ashamed of, without calling the wage a metaphor.

VI. THE ONLY WAY

The only way out of sin unto true repentance is Christ Jesus.

A. Blood and the conscience

Hebrews 9:14 — “How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?”

The phrase is Hebrews’ own phrase: dead works. The conscience is purged from them by blood, to serve the living God. Self-reformation without that blood is still a dead work.

Hebrews 9:13 — “For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:”

The lesser blood purified the flesh. How much more the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works. Water will be taught in its chapter as a sign after one is saved. It is not this stone.

How does blood purge the conscience from dead works? Answer from the verse. The blood of Christ. He offered Himself without spot. Through the eternal Spirit. To God. The conscience is purged. The aim is service of the living God.

B. Quickened with Christ

Ephesians 2:1 — “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;”

Ephesians 2:2 — “Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:”

Ephesians 2:3 — “Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.”

Ephesians 2:4 — “But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,”

Ephesians 2:5 — “Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)”

The turn is real. The quickening is God’s, with Christ, by grace. Dead works belong to the dead. The living God is served by those whose conscience is purged and whose life is quickened.

C. In Christ, a new creature

2 Corinthians 5:17 again. If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature. Old things are passed away. All things are become new. The location is in Christ. The creature is new. The old things — both kinds — are passed. There is no new creature outside of Him. There is no “all things new” as a slogan over an old man still working.

D. No other name

Acts 4:10 — “Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him doth this man stand here before you whole.”

Acts 4:11 — “This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.”

Acts 4:12 — “Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.”

Peter, before rulers: Jesus Christ of Nazareth, crucified, whom God raised. There is no second saviour. There is no rite that takes His place. Water is a sign after one is saved. It is not this stone. A course enrolment is not this name. The Power of Salvation is a companion, not another name.

E. Distinction, principle, charge

Distinction: Christ the way versus self-reformation as the way versus another name versus a sign treated as the object versus a course treated as the new creature.

Principle: the only way out of sin unto true repentance is Christ Jesus. His blood purges the conscience from dead works. There is none other name.

Charge: how does blood purge the conscience from dead works? Answer from Hebrews 9:14 in a paragraph a babe could follow. Then write Acts 4:12. Then write one sentence you will not say again if it puts another name in that place.

VII. RECEIVE HIM

The charge is not a later illustration. Receive Him today.

A. Power to become the sons of God

John 1:11 — “He came unto his own, and his own received him not.”

John 1:12 — “But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:”

John 1:13 — “Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.”

Reception is how one enters the new creature. Sonship language begins here. Course 2 will open faith, image, justification, and the heir. Course 3 will open the Spirit’s witness of that sonship. You do not wait for those chapters to receive Him.

Born not of blood: pedigree will not do it. Not of the will of the flesh: appetite will not do it. Not of the will of man: a house, a school, a nation will not do it. Of God. Power to become the sons of God is given, not earned as a wage. The wage was death. This is gift and power.

B. The word nigh thee

Romans 10:8 — “But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;”

Romans 10:9 — “That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.”

Romans 10:10 — “For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.”

The word is nigh. You do not fetch Christ down. You confess the Lord Jesus. You believe God raised Him. You shall be saved.

Have you received Him? Write the confession Romans 10:9 actually asks. The Lord Jesus. Raised from the dead. Mouth and heart. If you have, write what “power to become the sons of God” means from John 1:12-13, not from a slogan. If you have not, the charge stands: Receive Him today. A course enrolment is not the new creature.

C. Distinction, principle, charge

Distinction: receiving Him versus enrolling in a course versus being born of blood, of the will of the flesh, or of the will of man versus waiting for Course 2 or Course 3 to become a son.

Principle: as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God. Confess the Lord Jesus; believe God raised Him; thou shalt be saved.

Charge: have you received Him? Write John 1:12-13 and Romans 10:8-10. Write the confession the text asks. Then you are ready to be taught faith toward God — not as a feeling, but as the state of sons.

VIII. WHAT THIS CHAPTER WILL NOT DO

It will not treat Hell-avoidance as metanoia.

It will not treat Judas’s regret as the foundation.

It will not invent an eighth repent-word.

It will not teach Matthew 16 as Luke 16.

It will not merge the old man and outward sin into one vague confession.

It will not offer another name.

It will not tell you that a course enrolment is the new creature.

It will not treat self-reformation without blood as the purge of the conscience.

It will not treat water as this stone, or The Power of Salvation as a seventh course, or this chapter as Chapter 7.

The new creature is in Christ. The foundation is laid when a man has changed his mind over sin and its cause, and has received the One whose blood purges the conscience from dead works.

IX. FURTHER READING

The Power of Salvation — directed reading when that volume is in your hand. It is a companion, not a seventh course, and not a substitute for this chapter.

When that volume is assigned, you will read named sections for the week. You will not be required to finish the whole book to complete this course or the year. Buying the school does not grant that book. Buying that book does not grant this course.

X. WORD DRILL LABOUR

Write Hebrews 6:1. Write 2 Corinthians 5:17. Write Matthew 27:3-5. Write Luke 13:3. Write Hebrews 9:14. Write Acts 4:12. Write John 1:12-13. Write Romans 10:9-10. Write Romans 6:23.

Reason metanoia: change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, including reformation, new creature.

Reason μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai): regret of consequences, not the cause. Judas. The silver. The hanging.

Reason nekros ergon: dead works of the old man and the old nature. Not boredom.

Reason old man: nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience.

Reason outward sin: the second old thing, with its own file.

Reason wages: death. Reason gift: eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Reason blood: purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

Reason name: none other under heaven.

Reason receive: as many as received Him. Power to become the sons of God. Born of God.

If you cannot reason those words without a slogan, you have recited this chapter. Recitation is not the stone.

Seven words. Not eight. Luke 16. Not Matthew 16. Two old things. Not one pile. Christ the only way. Receive Him today.

XI. LABOUR FOR THE WALK AND THE INTENSIVE

Same doctrine. Same first stone. Different hours. Course 1 occupies nine of the fifty-two weeks. This chapter is the weight of those weeks, with Chapter 1 as the gate.

The Walk — about three hours a week. Read this chapter in sittings you can finish without skimming the lists. Write the seven words with one verse each. Write ten lines on metanoia versus μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai). Name the two old things. Write Romans 6:23 and Acts 4:12 and Romans 10:9. Confess the Lord Jesus if you have not. Write the eight examination points below as eight tight paragraphs.

Intensive — about eight hours a week. Read until you can teach. Write the seven words with their full verses and a sentence of context each. Write a full page on Judas that does not treat his remorse as the stone. Write Luke 16:27-31 and say what Abraham refused. Write one page on the old-man Scripture set without the word “basically.” Walk Galatians 5 and Mark 7 without calling them the old man. Write Hebrews 9:14 as a paragraph a babe could follow. Write the eight examination points as eight full pages.

Both: same exams. Same certificate when a certificate is issued. No second curriculum. A certificate later will ask more than a click. Mastery is not completion of activities.

XII. EXAMINATION OF THE PRINCIPLE

This section is not a new doctrine. It is the examination of the stone.

You should now be able to teach, from Scripture:

1. Graphē over religious substitute — Chapter 1, still in force.
2. Babe versus teacher; ἄπειρος (apeiros); νήπιος (nēpios); two marks — Chapter 1, still in force.
3. Spoudazō as labour — Chapter 1, still in force.
4. The seven words; metanoia versus μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai).
5. Cause versus consequence (Luke 16:19-31; Revelation 20:10-15).
6. Two old things.
7. Wages and the only salvation you need.
8. Christ the only way; no other name; receive Him.

Write the principle as you would teach it to a babe, then as you would stand behind it before a teacher. Name the two old things. Name the difference between metanoia and μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai). Do not submit a feeling in the place of the Scripture set.

Then you are ready to be taught faith toward God — not as a feeling, but as the state of sons. Chapter 3 will open that stone. Do not carry an unlaid first stone into it and call the carrying growth.

chapters.title: Faith toward God
chapters.body:
Hebrews 6:1 — “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God.”

Repentance received you into the new creature. Faith names the state you are in. Do not treat this chapter as a mood. Treat it as the second stone.

This is the textbook of Foundation School, Aletheia Publications, under Dr. Coach Achu Gustave. Holy Scripture is the authority. What follows opens the second principle until you can teach it.

The writer of Hebrews will not let you lay this stone again as a lifestyle. He will also not let you skip it. You leave a foundation after it is laid. You do not leave a heading you never understood.

Faith toward God is not the second feeling after the first tear. It is credence. It defines your state as a child. If you make it a temperature, you have not heard πίστις (pistis).

I. PISTIS — CREDENCE THAT DEFINES SONS

Faith essentially defines our state as children of God. Greek πίστις (pistis): credence. In effect it defines our acceptance — true nature — and our espousal: adoption as sons of God.

Credence is not a shiver. Credence is the mind’s agreement with what God has said and done. You credit the record. You do not wait to feel like a son before you will be named one.

Galatians 4:1-3 — “Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world.”

The heir can be lord of all and still live like a servant while he is a child. Bondage under elements is not the last word. The father’s appointed time is.

Galatians 4:4-7 — “But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.”

Read the order as written. God sent forth His Son. The Son was made of a woman, made under the law. He redeemed them that were under the law. The purpose of that redemption, in this sentence, is that we might receive the adoption of sons.

Because ye are sons — not in order to become sons — God hath sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. The cry follows the sonship. The Spirit does not invent a child. He cries in a child.

Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son. And if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Son is not a compliment. Heir follows son as the next name in the same breath.

Romans 8:14-16 — “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God.”

You have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear. Again. The old bondage is not the gift. The gift is the Spirit of adoption. The cry is Abba, Father. The witness is that you are the children of God — present tense.

Romans 8:17 — “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

If children, then heirs. The “if” is not a doubt about whether children exist. It is the logic of the household. Children inherit. Heirs of God. Joint-heirs with Christ. Suffering with Him is named in the same verse as glorified together. Do not cut the verse in half to keep only the inheritance and refuse the fellowship of His sufferings. Do not cut it in half the other way and keep only the pain as if there were no heir.

Ephesians 1:3-5 — “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.”

Adoption here is not an emergency repair God thought of after Adam fell. He predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will. The will is His. The pleasure is His. The adoption is by Jesus Christ.

Pistis is not a feeling you work up in a meeting. It is credence that agrees with what God has done and who you are by that doing. Servant is not the name. Son is the name. Heir follows son.

Hold the distinction until you can teach it without a slogan. A man may tremble and still be a servant in his mind. A man may be quiet and still be a son. The state is not measured by the noise of the room.

Course 1 received Him. John 1:12 already said that as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God. This chapter does not invent a second reception. It names the credence of the son that reception made.

Charge of this section. Write, from Galatians 4:5-7 and Romans 8:15-17, whether you are a servant or a son. Do not write a mood. Write the names the text gives. If a son, then an heir. Say what follows.

II. ’ĔLŌHÎM — IMAGE AND LIKENESS

This acceptance or approval is on the basis of our true nature from creation with respect to God.

Genesis 1:26 — “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.”

God, in the Hebrew of this verse, is ’ĕlōhîm. This teaching reads ’ĕlōhîm as plural: Trinity. “Let us make” is not a committee of angels inventing a lesser thing. God speaks as God. The “us” and the “our” are the speech of God concerning God. Man is made in that image, after that likeness.

Do not send the plurality to a courtroom of created beings. The Maker is speaking. The thing made is man.

Image. Likeness. Dominion. Those are not ornaments. They are the design. Man is who he is by how he was designed and by Who designed him.

Genesis 1:27 — “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”

The Living Bible (TLB) gloss, kept as a gloss beside the KJV, not as a rival Bible: “So God made man like his Maker. Like God did God make man; Man and maid did he make them.”

Like his Maker. That is the use of the gloss. Mark it TLB. Keep the KJV as the text you teach. The gloss is there so you will not miss the sentence: God made man like his Maker.

Genesis 1:28 — “And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.”

He blessed them. He spoke to them. Fruitful. Multiply. Replenish. Subdue. Have dominion. The blessing and the charge are one speech. You will not be allowed, in this school, to keep “image” as a pious word and throw away dominion as if it were optional poetry.

This school will not put a softer sentence in the place of Genesis 1:26-28. Teach the verses as written. Man is who he is by design and by Who designed him.

This chapter keeps a Scripture set with these verses. You will not detach the Scripture set. You will not use the Scripture set to empty the verses. You will hold them together.

John 14:12 — “Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.”

He that believeth on Me. The works that I do shall he do also. Greater works than these shall he do. Because I go unto My Father. The going of the Son is the reason the believer is not left as a spectator of works he can never touch. Do not reduce the verse to a fundraising slogan. Do not empty it because you are afraid of it. Teach it as written, with Genesis 1:26-28.

1 John 4:17 — “Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.”

As He is, so are we in this world. Not as He will be, so we hope to be after we die. In this world. The love is made perfect toward boldness in the day of judgment on that ground. Do not turn the sentence into a compliment you pay yourself. Do not refuse the sentence because it is large. It is written.

Psalm 82:6 — “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

Romans 8:17 you have already heard: if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.

John 17:20-23 will be opened in its own section. It belongs in this Scripture set now as the prayer of oneness and of glory given. Hold the address. Do not wait until section IX to admit that the prayer exists.

This is the image-and-likeness file. You will not be taught a hedge that undoes Genesis 1:26-28. You will be taught the writing.

If you came to this chapter hoping the school would apologize for the text, you came to the wrong house. If you came hoping the school would invent a title the Scripture set does not grant, you also came to the wrong house. The text is enough. Reason from it.

Further reading at this knot, directed, not as a seventh course: The Doctrine of Man. Why Men Die.

III. PSALM 82 WITH JOHN 10 — DO NOT EMPTY THE VERSE

Psalm 82:1-5 — “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods. How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked? Selah. Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy. Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked. They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.”

The psalm is a judgment scene. God stands. He judges among the gods. The charge is unjust judgment, respect of wicked persons, failure to defend the poor and fatherless. They know not. They walk on in darkness. The foundations of the earth are out of course.

Out of course. Remember that phrase when this chapter reaches δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē). Equity is conformity with the nature of God. Original: back on course.

Psalm 82:6-8 — “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes. Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

I have said. The saying is God’s. Ye are gods. And all of you are children of the most High. The next breath is not a cancellation invented by a frightened teacher. It is the psalm’s own next line: But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.

Teach 82:6 with 82:7. Do not detach 82:6 from the writing to make a slogan. Do not empty 82:6 by using 82:7 as if the first sentence never stood. Both sentences are in the psalm. Both are Holy Writ.

John 10:30-33 — “I and my Father are one. Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him. Jesus answered them, Many good works have I shewed you from my Father; for which of those works do ye stone me? The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.”

The charge against the Lord is blasphemy: being a man, He makes Himself God. He does not flee the writing. He appeals to it.

John 10:34-36 — “Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?”

Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If He called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken. The same Lord who will not let the scripture be broken will not let you empty the verse He just quoted.

John 10:37-38 — “If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him.”

The works are the Father’s works. The knowing is that the Father is in Him and He in the Father. That oneness will return in John 17. Do not pretend John 10 is a different religion from Genesis 1 and from the prayer.

The Scripture set is Psalm 82:6 with 82:7 and with John 10:34-35. Course 1 already used John 10:35 for the authority of the graphē: the scripture cannot be broken. That authority governs this psalm as it governs every other writing.

Charge. Write Psalm 82:6 and 82:7 in one paragraph, then write John 10:34-35 under them. Do not add a slogan. Do not subtract a clause. Say what the three verses force when they are left together.

IV. TRUE NATURE — PARTAKERS

2 Peter 1:2-3 — “Grace and peace be multiplied unto you through the knowledge of God, and of Jesus our Lord, According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue.”

Knowledge again. Course 1 defined knowledge as perception, learning, and reasoning. Grace and peace are multiplied through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord. Divine power has given all things that pertain unto life and godliness. The call is to glory and virtue.

2 Peter 1:4 — “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.”

Partakers of the divine nature. The promises are the means. Escape from the corruption that is in the world through lust is named in the same sentence. You are not being invited to invent another nature. You are being made partaker of the nature Genesis already named, having escaped the corruption.

This teaching places this verse with man’s true nature and with the glory he came short of through sin. Dikaiosynē, later in this chapter, is equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God — original: back on course.

Back on course. Psalm 82:5 said the foundations of the earth are out of course. Romans 3 will say all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. 2 Peter 1:4 is not a new species. It is participation in the nature from which man came short, by the promises, in escape from corruption.

2 Peter 1:5-8 — “And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity. For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Faith is the first named in the adding. Virtue. Knowledge. Temperance. Patience. Godliness. Brotherly kindness. Charity. The partaker is not a man who quotes 1:4 and refuses 1:5. Diligence belongs here as it belonged to σπουδάζω (spoudazō) in Chapter 1.

You are not being invited to invent another nature. You are being returned to the one Genesis named, in Christ.

Charge. Define true nature from Genesis 1:26-28 and 2 Peter 1:4 in one Scripture set. What is partaken? What is escaped? What is not invented?

V. WHY DID JESUS COME?

Romans 3:21-22 — “But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference.”

The righteousness of God is manifested. It is witnessed by the law and the prophets. It is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe. There is no difference.

Romans 3:23-24 — “For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.”

Why did Jesus come? This teaching sets the question on these verses. All have sinned. All have come short of the glory of God. Being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

The glory come short is deviation from true nature. That is the gloss. Glory here is not a vague heaven someday. Glory here is the nature Genesis named and the image 1 Corinthians 11:7 will name.

1 Corinthians 11:7 — “For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.”

The immediate context is headship and covering in the assembly. This school will not skip the clause because the chapter is contested. This teaching cites the identity clause: man is the image and glory of God. That is the glory named in Romans 3:23.

Teach the clause. He is the image and glory of God. Come short of the glory is come short of that. Jesus came because that glory was come short. He did not come to invent a different creature. He came that the man made in the image might be justified freely and set back on course.

Romans 3:25-26 — “Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”

God set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in His blood. The declaration is His righteousness. He is just. He is the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. The justifier does not become unjust in order to justify. The blood declares righteousness. The believer is the one justified.

Charge. Answer the question: Why did Jesus come? Answer in terms of glory and true nature from Romans 3:23-24 and 1 Corinthians 11:7. Do not answer with a slogan that never names the glory.

VI. DIKAIOŌ — JUSTIFIED FREELY

Justified: Greek δικαιόω (dikaioō) — render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt. It is a derivative of δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē): righteousness, justification. Equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God (2 Peter 1:4). Original: back on course.

Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. Through Greek apolutrōsis — redemption; ransom in full.

Romans 3:24 again: being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Freely. By His grace. Through the redemption. The redemption is in Christ Jesus.

There is no unpaid remainder on that ransom. Apolutrōsis is ransom in full. Do not preach a justification you must finish by labour. Labour belongs to study (Chapter 1). Innocence before God is free in Christ.

Dikaioō is not a project you complete on a good week. It is a rendering. God renders just. God renders innocent. Free from evil or guilt. The agent is grace. The means is the ransom in full.

If you add a fee to a ransom in full, you have not understood the word. If you postpone innocence until you have suffered enough to deserve it, you have not heard “freely.”

Romans 3:27-28 — “Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.”

Boasting is excluded. The law of faith excludes it. A man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. Pistis again. Credence. Not a wage.

The distinction is sharp. Free justification is not earned innocence. Earned innocence is not this principle. A man who is still trying to buy what apolutrōsis already paid is not yet standing on this stone. He may be busy. He is not crediting the ransom.

Charge. Has man been justified? Write the answer: Yes, and freely. Show apolutrōsis in Romans 3:24. Name what you will not add to a ransom in full.

VII. YOU ARE THE DIKAIOSYNĒ OF GOD NOW

2 Corinthians 5:17-19 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation; To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.”

Course 1 already taught the new creature and the two old things that pass. This chapter does not relay that stone. It opens the next sentence of the same passage.

God has reconciled us to Himself by Jesus Christ. God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them. The word of reconciliation is committed unto us.

2 Corinthians 5:20-21 — “Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God. For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.”

He hath made Him to be sin for us, who knew no sin. That we might be made the righteousness of God in Him. present tense stands: so right now, you are the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God in Christ.

Dikaiosynē: righteousness, justification. Equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God. Original: back on course. You are that, in Him, now.

This is not an aspiration you visit on a good day. It is the state πίστις (pistis) credits. Course 1 laid the new creature. This chapter names the righteousness of that creature.

Do not say “I am becoming the righteousness of God” as if 2 Corinthians 5:21 were a ladder you have not finished. The verse is not a ladder. He made Him to be sin. The purpose clause is that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him. This teaching will not let you postpone the name.

Do not say “I am the righteousness of God” as a boastful claim that has dropped “in Him.” The location is in Him. The new creature is in Christ. The δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) is in Him.

Charge. Write 2 Corinthians 5:21 in full. Then write, in the present tense, what you are in Christ. Do not write a future you hope to earn. Do not write a title you invented. Write the verse.

VIII. HEBREWS 1:8 — WHAT DOES THAT MAKE YOU?

Hebrews 1:1-2 — “God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.”

God has spoken by His Son. The Son is appointed heir of all things. By Him He made the worlds. Heir language is already in the opening of the book. You will meet heir again from Galatians 4. Do not forget that the Son is first named heir of all things here.

Hebrews 1:3-4 — “Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high; Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.”

The Son is the brightness of His glory and the express image of His person. He upholds all things by the word of His power. He purged our sins by Himself. He sat down. He is so much better than the angels. He has by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.

Express image. Genesis 1 already used image. 2 Corinthians 4 will use image of God for Christ. Hebrews 1:3 names the Son the express image of His person. Hold the word. Do not invent a second image that is not this one.

Hebrews 1:5-7 — “For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son? And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him. And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.”

The angels are not addressed as Son. The firstbegotten is worshipped by angels. The distinction is the writer’s. Do not flatten Son and angel into one rank.

Hebrews 1:8 — “But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.”

Unto the Son He saith. Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever. A sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of Thy kingdom. The Father addresses the Son as God. The sceptre is righteousness — δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) in the thought of this chapter.

After 2 Corinthians 5:21, the question is: according to Hebrews 1:8, what does that make you? It does not print the answer.

This school will not invent a title the Scripture set does not grant. You will reason from the Scripture set. You are the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God in Christ. The Son is the brightness of His glory and the express image of His person. The Father addresses the Son as God. The sceptre of His kingdom is righteousness. Genesis 1:26-28 has already named image, likeness, and dominion. 1 John 4:17 has said, as He is, so are we in this world.

Write what the Scripture set forces. Do not write what a slogan wants. Do not write a name the Scripture set does not grant. The charge is the question. The labour is the reasoning.

If you invent a title to sound mature, you have become a babe with a louder word. If you refuse to reason because you are afraid of the Scripture set, you have also become a babe. Dull of hearing is still dull when it is cautious.

Charge. Answer the question from the Scripture set: 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 1:3; Hebrews 1:8; Genesis 1:26-28; 1 John 4:17. Do not invent a title. Do not leave the question blank. Reason.

IX. WHO IS HEIR? WHAT IS AN HEIR?

This teaching asks two questions and points you to Galatians 4:5-7. Who is heir of God? What is the meaning of “heir”?

Galatians 4:1 already told you that the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all. The child-heir can live like a hired man. That is not because he is a hired man. It is because he is still under tutors until the time appointed.

Galatians 4:7 — “Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.”

Who is heir of God? The son. The one who is no more a servant. The one of whom it is said, if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

What is an heir? An heir is not a hired man hoping for a wage. An heir is the one to whom the father’s estate belongs by sonship. The estate is not a tip for good work. It is the portion of the child.

Romans 8:17 again: heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ. Joint-heirs. Not a junior partner who might be cut out if the week goes badly. With Christ.

Do not make heir a metaphor for “someone who likes church.” Do not make heir a career in ministry. Do not make heir a feeling of belonging. Answer from the adoption Scripture set.

The distinction is the household. A servant receives orders and a wage, if he receives anything. A son receives the name and the portion. Course 3 will return to this when the Spirit cries Abba and you are not a slave. Do not wait for that chapter to refuse the hired-man gospel.

Application. If you pray as a servant trying to be hired, you have not credited Galatians 4:7. If you idle as if an heir had no charge, you have not credited Romans 8:17’s “if so be that we suffer with him.” The heir is not a hired man. The heir is also not a tourist.

Charge. Who is heir of God? What is the meaning of heir? Write both answers from Galatians 4:5-7 and Romans 8:17. Name one way you have treated yourself as a hired man. Put it down.

X. LIKEN JOHN 17:20-23

John 17:1 — “These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee.”

This is the hour. The Son asks to be glorified that He may glorify the Father. The prayer that follows is not a conference agenda. It is the Son speaking to the Father.

John 17:18-19 — “As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world. And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.”

As Thou hast sent Me, even so have I sent them. For their sakes He sanctifies Himself, that they might be sanctified through the truth. The “they” of this stretch is first the men given Him. The next verses open the prayer beyond them.

John 17:20-23 — “Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.”

This teaching asks: How would you liken the prayer of oneness with the Father by Jesus in John 17:20-23?

Liken. The word is liken. You are not asked to invent a new doctrine. You are asked to set this prayer beside what you have already been taught and to say what the words themselves force.

Do not reduce it to an organizational merger. A merger of ministries can be signed by men who are not one as the Father is in the Son. Do not empty it into a feeling of togetherness. A feeling can be warm in a room that has never heard “I in them, and thou in me.”

The measure in the text is “as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.” That is the “as.” Not as a team agrees. As the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father.

That they also may be one in us. The location of the oneness is in the Father and the Son. That the world may believe that Thou hast sent Me. The world’s believing is tied to this oneness, not to a better logo.

And the glory which Thou gavest Me I have given them. Glory given. The same glory-file this chapter opened at Romans 3:23 and 1 Corinthians 11:7. He has given them the glory the Father gave Him. The purpose clause is that they may be one, even as We are one.

I in them, and Thou in Me, that they may be made perfect in one. Perfect in one. Course 1 already told you maturity is perfection, the second movement after first principles. This prayer does not wait for Chapter 6 to use the word. Made perfect in one. And that the world may know that Thou hast sent Me, and hast loved them, as Thou hast loved Me.

As Thou hast loved Me. The love the Father has for the Son is the measure of the love the world is to know toward them. Do not shrink that “as.”

Liken from the words. You have been made in the image, after the likeness. You are the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God in Christ. As He is, so are we in this world. The Son is the express image. The Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father. The glory given to the Son is given to those who believe. I in them. Thou in Me.

Write the likeness from those words. Course 3 will open the Spirit who shews “Mine.” Do not wait for that course to refuse a cheap oneness.

Charge. How would you liken John 17:20-23? Write the likeness from the words of the prayer. Name one reduction you will refuse: organizational merger, or a feeling of togetherness without “as thou, Father, art in me.”

XI. THE IMAGE IN THE FACE OF JESUS CHRIST

2 Corinthians 4:1-2 — “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.”

This ministry. Received mercy. Renounced hidden things of dishonesty. Not handling the word of God deceitfully. Manifestation of the truth. Conscience. In the sight of God. Faith toward God will not handle the word deceitfully to make this chapter safer than it is.

2 Corinthians 4:3-4 — “But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.”

If our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost. The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not. Lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.

Christ is the image of God. The gospel is glorious. The light is that gospel. The blinding is lest that light should shine. Course 1 already used 2 Corinthians 4:4 in the old-man Scripture set: the god of this world blinds minds. The same verse now sits in the faith Scripture set because the thing blinded against is the image.

That blindness is not a small inconvenience. It is the old opposition to the image. The lost are not merely uninformed. Their minds are blinded lest the image shine.

2 Corinthians 4:5-6 — “For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.”

We preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord. God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness — Genesis 1 again — hath shined in our hearts. The purpose: to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

The glory of God is known in His face. The same God who said “Let there be light” has shined in our hearts. Knowledge of the glory. Face of Jesus Christ. Image of God.

Faith toward God is credence of this light, this image, this sonship, this free justification. It is not a leap into the dark. The god of this world wants the leap into the dark. The gospel shines.

If you treat faith as a jump without a face, you have not heard 2 Corinthians 4:6. If you treat the face as a picture you admire without becoming the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God in Him, you have not heard 2 Corinthians 5:21. Hold both.

Charge. Write 2 Corinthians 4:4 and 4:6 as one Scripture set. Who is the image of God? Where is the light of the knowledge of the glory of God given? What blinds a mind against that light?

XII. THE SECOND STONE LAID — REASONING AND APPLICATION

You have now walked the second principle. Pistis. Adoption. Image and likeness. Psalm 82 with John 10. Partakers. Glory come short. Dikaioō freely. Apolutrōsis in full. You are the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God now. Hebrews 1:8 asked. Heir named. John 17 likened. The face of Christ shone.

Reasoning is not optional decoration. Chapter 1 told you knowledge is perception, learning, and reasoning. This chapter has asked the questions this school asks. A man who can recite the headings and cannot answer the questions is still a babe in the word of righteousness.

Application is not a fourth gospel. It is the credence lived. If you are a son, you will not keep the servant’s name for humility’s sake. That is not humility. That is unbelief wearing manners. If you are the δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosynē) of God in Christ, you will not postpone innocence until you have paid what the ransom already paid. If you are made in the image, after the likeness, you will not apologize for Genesis 1:26-28.

You will also not boastful claim past the Scripture set. Joint-heirs suffer with Him. Partakers have escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. The psalm that says Ye are gods also says ye shall die like men if you walk on in darkness and judge unjustly. John 17’s oneness is as the Father in the Son, not as a crowd in a brand.

The next chapter will baptize the son this chapter named: into Christ, then in water as a sign, then in the Spirit as witness. Do not carry a hired man’s mind into that chapter. Do not carry a slogan’s title either.

XIII. FURTHER READING

The Doctrine of Man — already in the house.
Why Men Die.
True Nature of God — if you know God’s nature, then you are as Him, unlimited, because you are made in His image (Genesis 1:26).
Who’s Jesus to You?

These are companions, not a seventh course. Directed sections when the volumes are in your hand. Completing this course does not require finishing every page of the library.

Do not wander the back-list as if a title on a catalogue page were a Year-1 assignment. The four named above are the companions this principle directs. Presence of Sons is not this chapter’s book. Spirit Witness is not this chapter’s book. Those names belong later, and even then as their own books.

The next chapter opens the doctrine of baptisms: the son this chapter named is baptized into Christ, then in water as a sign, then in the Spirit as witness.

chapters.title: The Doctrine of Baptisms
chapters.body:
