Hebrews 6:2 — “Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.”

Hebrews 6:2 is baptisms, plural. This school will not flatten the plural. There are seven in Scripture. Three are essential for believers. Only one of those three saves the soul.

Course 2 named the son. This chapter baptizes that son: into Christ, then in water as a sign, then in the Spirit as witness.

This is the textbook of Foundation School, Aletheia Publications, under Dr. Coach Achu Gustave. Holy Scripture is the authority. You will learn the word, then the seven, then the three, then the agents, then the distinctions that keep the tank from becoming a second saviour.

I. BAPTISMOS — WASHING

Baptismos: ablution. Ritual washing of a priest’s hands or of sacred vessels.

Do not make the word a font before you have heard what it washes. This teaching opens the principle with washing, not with a tank.

Hebrews 6:2 names a doctrine of baptisms. The first word under that heading is washing. Hold it.

Ablution is not a metaphor you may ignore. It is the sense of the word. Something is washed. Someone is washed. The question this chapter must answer is: by what agency, into what, in what element, by which agent, and to what end.

If you begin at the river, you have begun late. Begin at βαπτισμός (baptismos). Washing. Then it takes you to the Word.

A priest’s hands were washed because the priest was to handle holy things. Sacred vessels were washed because they were to bear what was set apart. The washing is not the priesthood. The washing serves a holiness already named.

The washing will not invent the son Course 2 named. It will not replace the new creature Course 1 received. It will be understood: first as the Word’s agency at new birth, then as the seven, then as the three for believers.

Charge. Before you argue immersion or pouring, write the word βαπτισμός (baptismos) as ablution. What is washed? You do not yet answer with a tank. You answer with washing.

II. THE AGENCY OF THE WORD

Ephesians 5:25-27 — “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.”

Christ loved the church and gave Himself for it. The purpose clauses follow that giving. That He might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word. That He might present it to Himself a glorious church.

The washing of water here is by the word. The water in this verse is not the power. The Word is the agency. Sanctify. Cleanse. Present. Glorious. No spot. No wrinkle. Holy. Without blemish. The font did not love the church. Christ did. The Word washes.

1 Peter 1:23-25 — “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever. For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away: But the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you.”

Born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever. The agency of new birth in this sentence is the Word. Flesh is grass. The glory of man falls. The word of the Lord endureth. This is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you.

You were not born again of a tank. You were born again of incorruptible seed, by the word of God. If you make the tank the seed, you have left 1 Peter 1:23.

John 3:3-5 — “Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born? Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.”

Nicodemus hears “born” and thinks a womb. The Lord answers with water and the Spirit. This teaching places John 3:5 with Ephesians 5:26 and 1 Peter 1:23: the washing signifies the agency of the Word at new birth.

John 3:6-8 — “That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again. The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.”

Flesh begets flesh. Spirit begets spirit. Ye must be born again. The washing of the Word and the birth of the Spirit are not a second womb. They are the entrance the Lord named.

The washing signifies the agency of the Word at new birth. That is the premiere of the three essential baptisms. You do not begin this principle at a river. You begin it where the Word washes.

Charge. Write Ephesians 5:26, 1 Peter 1:23, and John 3:5 as one Scripture set. What is the agency? What is not the power? Where does this principle begin?

III. SEVEN IN SCRIPTURE — NO EIGHTH

This teaching said seven mentioned in the Scriptures for believers, and named only three. The authorized list is seven. We will not invent an eighth. We will not pretend the Bible has only three.

You must be able to name all seven, and which three are essential for believers, and in what doctrinal order. A man who can name three and cannot name seven has flattened the plural. A man who invents an eighth has left the file.

1. John’s baptism in water.

Matthew 3:1-3 — “In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

Matthew 3:5-6 — “Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.”

Matthew 3:11 — “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.”

John baptized with water unto repentance. He is not the one who baptizes with the Holy Ghost. He says so. This is the first of the seven. It is in Scripture. It is not the baptism that saves your soul now.

Acts 19:3-4 — “And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.”

John’s baptism pointed to the One coming after. It was not a rival saviour. When men at Ephesus had only John’s baptism, Paul did not leave them there.

2. Christ’s baptism in water.

Matthew 3:13-15 — “Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me? And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.”

Matthew 3:16-17 — “And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

The Lord was baptized in water. John forbade Him. The Lord said it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. The Spirit descended. The Father spoke. This is the second of the seven. It is Christ’s own baptism in water. It is not your saving. It is in the file.

John 1:31-33 will return when we name the agent of Spirit baptism. Hold the address.

3. Baptism in suffering.

Luke 12:50 — “But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!”

The Lord has a baptism still to be baptized with after Jordan. He is straitened till it be accomplished. The element here is not water. Baptizō will be shown to name overwhelming and burying regardless of element. This is the baptism of His suffering.

Matthew 20:22-23 — “But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able. And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.”

Cup and baptism together. The sons of Zebedee did not know what they asked. He told them they would drink and be baptized with that baptism. This is the third of the seven. Do not make it an eighth later by renaming it. It is already numbered.

4. Baptism in the cloud and in the sea.

1 Corinthians 10:1-2 — “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.”

All our fathers. Under the cloud. Through the sea. Baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea. The elements are cloud and sea. The baptism is unto Moses. This is the fourth of the seven. It is Israel’s passage, written for our admonition. It is not the font in your meeting.

The baptism unto Moses does not cancel Christ. It is a type in the file. 1 Corinthians 10:4 — “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

5. Christian baptism in water.

Matthew 28:18-20 — “And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.”

This is the water baptism of the nations taught, after they are made disciples. The agent, as the owner locked it, is the minister. This is the fifth of the seven. It is essential for believers as a sign after one is saved. It is not the one baptism that saves the soul.

6. Baptism into Christ and into His body.

This is the premiere of the three essential. It happens at repentance and new birth. It is “one baptism” (Ephesians 4:5). It is the only baptism that saves the soul. The agent is the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:13). Sections IV through VI will open it.

7. Baptism in the Holy Spirit.

Witness of sonship and enduement of power for service. The agent is Christ (Matthew 3:11; John 1:31-33). Prerequisite: new birth. Sections XI through XV will open it.

Those are the seven. No eighth. John’s water is not Christian water. Christ’s water is not your water. Suffering is not the tank. Cloud and sea are not the tank. Into Christ is not the tank. The Spirit is not the tank. Keep the names.

Charge. Write the seven in order, with one text for each. Do not invent an eighth. Do not pretend the Bible has only three.

IV. THREE FOR BELIEVERS; THREE AGENTS; THE WORD BAPTIZŌ

Three for believers, in doctrinal order: 6, then 5, then 7.

Into Christ at repentance and new birth.
Water after one is saved.
Spirit — witness of sonship and enduement of power for service.

Doctrinal order is not a law that the Spirit may not fall before a man reaches the river. The Spirit may be given before water (Acts 10:44-48) or after it (Acts 1:4-8; 2:1-11; 8:12-21; 19:1-7). Do not make one sequence a law the Acts will not carry. The doctrine still names 6, then 5, then 7 as the order of what the three are: saving baptism, then sign, then witness and enduement.

Three agents:

The Holy Spirit baptizes into Christ and into His body (1 Corinthians 12:13).
Christ baptizes in the Holy Spirit (Matthew 3:11; John 1:31-33).
The minister baptizes into water (Matthew 28:19).

Do not assign the wrong agent to the wrong baptism. The minister does not baptize you into Christ. The Spirit does. Christ does not send you to the minister to be baptized in the Spirit. Christ baptizes in the Spirit. The Spirit does not replace the minister at the water. The minister baptizes in water.

John 1:31-33 — “And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water. And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him. And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost.”

John baptizes with water. The Same who sent him said: the One on whom the Spirit descends and remains is He which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost. Christ is that baptizer. Hold the agent.

Baptizō (G907) is from baptō (G911): to dip; to overwhelm with suffering; to bury into — regardless of the element. The element does not invent the word. The word names what is done in the element.

Baptō is to dip. Luke 16:24 — the rich man asks that Lazarus dip the tip of his finger in water. John 13:26 — He it is to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. Revelation 19:13 — a vesture dipped in blood. The root is dip.

Baptizō takes that root and names the act: to dip; to overwhelm with suffering (Matthew 20:22-23; Luke 12:50); to bury into (Romans 6:3-7; Colossians 2:12). Water, Spirit, suffering, cloud, sea — the word does not change its sense because the element changed. You are dipped, overwhelmed, buried into.

Baptizō at Galatians 3:27 is: to make whelmed — fully wet; overpowered / overwhelmed; submerged / drowned. Hold that for the next section.

Charge. Name the three for believers in doctrinal order. Name the three agents with one text each. Define baptizō from baptō without making the tank the word.

V. INTO CHRIST — THE ONE BAPTISM THAT SAVES

Ephesians 4:4-6 — “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

One body. One Spirit. One hope. One Lord. One faith. One baptism. One God and Father of all. The “one baptism” sits in that heptad. It is not a slogan for a denomination’s tank. It is not a slogan against water. It is not a slogan against the Spirit.

This one baptism is baptism into Christ and His body at repentance and new birth — fellowship of the saints. It is the only baptism that saves the soul.

“One baptism” does not cancel water. It does not cancel the Spirit. It names the baptism that brings a man into Christ and into the body. The other two for believers remain. They are not this one.

If you treat the tank as this one, you have not heard Ephesians 4:5. If you treat a second experience as this one, you have not heard it either. The saving is into Christ. The agent is the Spirit. The time is repentance and new birth.

Course 1 received Him. Course 2 named the son. This baptism is that receiving named as baptism: into Christ, into His body, fellowship of the saints.

Charge. Why does “one baptism” not cancel water and Spirit as this school teaches them? Answer from Ephesians 4:5 with the three-for-believers file. Do not invent a fourth option in which nothing but the tank is one, or nothing but a feeling is one.

VI. BAPTIZŌ — WHELMED; PUT ON CHRIST

Galatians 3:27 — “For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.”

Baptizō: to make whelmed — fully wet; overpowered / overwhelmed; submerged / drowned. Baptized into Christ is not a damp confession. It is put on Christ.

You do not put Him on as a garment you take off at the door. You are whelmed into Him. As many as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. The “as many as” is not a maybe. Those baptized into Christ have put Him on.

This is baptism 1 of the three essential — number 6 in the seven. It happens at repentance and new birth. Course 1 received Him. This chapter names what that receiving is as baptism: into Christ.

Do not move Galatians 3:27 to the font as if the minister whelmed you into Christ. The minister whelms you in water after you are saved. The Spirit baptizes into Christ. Put on Christ is the fruit of that baptism.

Galatians 3:26 will be held with 3:27 in one paragraph in section X. Do not read 3:27 yet as if 3:26 were not there. Children by faith. Baptized into Christ, put on Christ. One life.

Charge. What does baptizō mean at Galatians 3:27? What have you put on if you have been baptized into Christ? What have you not put on if you have only been wet?

VII. BURIED, RAISED, ONE BODY

Romans 6:3-7 — “Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin. For he that is dead is freed from sin.”

Baptized into Jesus Christ. Baptized into His death. Buried with Him by baptism into death. Raised — like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father — to walk in newness of life. Planted together in the likeness of His death; also in the likeness of His resurrection. The old man Course 1 named is crucified with Him. The body of sin destroyed. Henceforth we should not serve sin. He that is dead is freed from sin.

This is not a later improvement on salvation. This is what baptism into Christ is. Death. Burial. Resurrection. Newness of life. The old man crucified. Freed from sin.

Romans 6:8-11 — “Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him. For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God. Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Reckon. Dead indeed unto sin. Alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. The reckoning is πίστις (pistis) at work on this baptism. You do not reckon a thing that has not happened. You reckon what baptism into His death already is.

Colossians 2:11-12 — “In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.”

Circumcision made without hands. Putting off the body of the sins of the flesh. Buried with Him in baptism. Risen with Him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised Him from the dead. Faith of the operation of God. Not faith in the tank. Faith in the God who raised Christ.

1 Corinthians 12:12-13 — “For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.”

The body is one. So also is Christ. By one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. Jews or Gentiles. Bond or free. All made to drink into one Spirit. The agent of this baptism is the Spirit. Buried. Raised. One body.

Water will later figure what this baptism already is. Water does not create it. If you wait for the river to crucify the old man, you have not heard Romans 6. If you refuse the river because Romans 6 already buried you, you have confused the object with the sign. The next sections will hold that distinction.

Charge. Who baptizes into one body? Into whose death are you baptized? What walks in newness of life? What does water not create?

VIII. WATER AFTER ONE IS SAVED — THE FIGURE

Water baptizō after one is saved.

It symbolizes the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ already elucidated in baptism 1. It is a figure. A sign points to a location. It is not the object.

The agent is the minister (Matthew 28:19). The minister does not save the soul by the act. He baptizes a person who has already been baptized into Christ.

Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them. Teaching first in the sense of the commission: make disciples, baptize, teach them to observe. The nations are not saved by the baptizing. They are baptized as those who have been taught and have received Christ.

Do not refuse the sign because it is not the object.
Do not worship the sign as if it were the object.

A man who refuses water because “I was baptized into Christ already” has told a truth and then used it to disobey the sign the Lord attached to the nations taught. A man who runs to water to get saved has made the sign the object. Both have left the file.

Christian water is number 5 in the seven. It is the second of the three for believers. It is after one is saved. It is significant only for those who have received Christ. This teaching will say that again when 1 Corinthians 1 is opened.

Charge. When is water baptizō? What does it symbolize? Who is the agent? What two errors will you refuse: refusing the sign, and worshipping the sign?

IX. IS IT THE WATER THAT SAVES?

1 Peter 3:18-20 — “For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.”

Christ suffered once for sins. The just for the unjust. That He might bring us to God. Put to death in the flesh. Quickened by the Spirit. Eight souls were saved by water in Noah’s day. The ark. The flood. The longsuffering of God waited.

1 Peter 3:21-22 — “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ: Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.”

The like figure. Figure. Baptism doth also now save us — and the verse itself refuses the filth of the flesh as the saving. Not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God, by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

The question is: is it the water that saves us, or the thing that it is a figure or symbol of?

Faith in the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ saves the soul, not the sign.

Just as a sign or symbol points you to a location of the object of the subject represented by the sign. The sign is not the city. The water is not the resurrection. The conscience answers toward God by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

Answer from the verse. Do not invent a third option in which the water becomes a second saviour. Do not invent a fourth in which the figure is nothing.

Eight souls were saved by water. The like figure. The figure now saves — not as filth removed from skin, but as the answer of a good conscience, by the resurrection. If you make the flood the gospel, you have not heard “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.” If you make the verse a denial that baptism is even a figure, you have not heard “the like figure.”

Charge. Is it the water that saves us, or the thing that it is a figure of? Answer from 1 Peter 3:21 and, in the next section, 1 Corinthians 1:17-18 together.

X. THE CROSS, NOT WATER, IS POWER — GALATIANS 3:26 WITH 3:27

1 Corinthians 1:17 — “For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect.”

Christ sent Paul not to baptize, but to preach the gospel. Not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect. If the tank were the power, Paul was sent to the wrong work. He was sent to preach. The danger named is making the cross of none effect.

1 Corinthians 1:18 — “For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God.”

The preaching of the cross — not water baptism — is the power of God unto us which are saved. To them that perish it is foolishness. The divide is not who got wet. The divide is the cross preached.

1 Corinthians 1:21-24 — “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness; But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. Jews require a sign. Greeks seek wisdom. We preach Christ crucified. Unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.

Water baptism does not save the soul from sin. It is a symbol significant only for those who have received Christ. The preaching of the cross, not water baptism, is God’s power to save.

Paul was not sent to make the tank the mission. He was sent to preach the gospel.

Galatians 3:26 — “For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.”

Galatians 3:27 — “For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.”

Hold both verses in one paragraph. Children by faith. Baptized into Christ, put on Christ. Faith in Christ Jesus saves the soul, not water baptism. That is the line, and 3:26 is the verse for it. 3:27 is baptism into Christ, not the font as the saviour. If you read 3:26 and throw away 3:27, you have faith with no putting-on. If you read 3:27 and throw away 3:26, you have a baptism that is no longer by faith. They are one life. Course 2 already forbade two gospels. Do not make two here.

Charge. Write Galatians 3:26 and 3:27 as one paragraph. Then write why the preaching of the cross, not water, is the power of God. Use 1 Corinthians 1:17-18 and 1:24.

XI. SPIRIT BAPTISM — WITNESS OF SONSHIP AND ENDUEMENT OF POWER

Baptism in the Holy Spirit is your natural or hereditary witness of sonship — heir of God.

Galatians 4:6-7 — “And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.”

Because ye are sons. God hath sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. No more a servant, but a son. If a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

Prerequisite: becoming God’s son — new birth / salvation. The Spirit is not sent into a man who has not been made a son. Course 1 and Course 2 are not optional prefaces. A man asking for the Spirit as a substitute for repentance has not heard the prerequisite.

The Holy Spirit witnesses (informant) a Father–Son relationship (ensuant) as a consequence of sonship. He does not invent the son. He cries Abba because you are a son. Informant. Ensuant. The witness follows the sonship as a consequence.

This witness stays. With it this school also teaches the enduement of power for service. Not instead of the witness. With it. Christ is the agent (Matthew 3:11; John 1:31-33). The sequence with water is not one locked order.

Acts 1:4-5 — “And, being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye have heard of me. For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.”

Acts 1:8 — “But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.”

Power after the Holy Ghost is come upon you. Witnesses unto Me. This is enduement for service. It is not a replacement of Abba. It is with Abba.

Acts 2:1-4 — “And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

They waited as He commanded, then they were filled. Acts 8 and Acts 19 show the Spirit after water in other companies. Acts 10 shows the Spirit before water.

Acts 10:44-48 — “While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter, Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.”

The Holy Ghost fell while Peter yet spake. They heard the word. The gift was poured out. Then Peter asks: can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? Water after the Spirit in this house. The sign is not refused because the Spirit came first. The Spirit is not denied because water had not yet been applied.

Acts 8:14-17 and Acts 19:5-6 will return under laying on of hands in the next chapter. Here they stand as Spirit after water. Do not make Acts 10 a law against Acts 2. Do not make Acts 2 a law against Acts 10.

Charge. Who is the Spirit sent into, according to Galatians 4:6? What two things does this school teach together, not instead? Name one account of the Spirit before water and one after.

XII. WITHOUT MEASURE — HOLD THE VERSE AND THE SOURCE

John 7:37-39 — “In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)”

If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, and drink. He that believeth on Me. Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. This spake He of the Spirit, which they that believe on Him should receive. The Holy Ghost was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.

Rivers. Not a teaspoon. They that believe. The giving waits on His glorification. You do not invent a Spirit the Lord had not yet given. You also do not, after He is glorified, preach a trickle the verse did not name.

John 3:34 — “For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.”

The verse, in its own sentence, is unto Him — Christ. He whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God. God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto Him.

This teaching applies “the measure Christ experienced” and says: the Spirit not by measure unto you.

Hold the verse. Hold the use given here. Do not empty John 3:34 to protect a stingy second-blessing slogan. Do not invent a measure this school refuses. Do not pretend the grammar of John 3:34 is about you in the first instance. It is unto Him. Then hold this: that measure, not by measure, unto you.

Both. The sentence is Christ’s. The application is given here. A babe will drop one to keep the other. You will hold both.

Charge. Whose sentence is John 3:34 in its own grammar? What does this school apply unto you? Why must you hold both?

XIII. FULLNESS

Colossians 1:19 — “For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell.”

In Him should all fulness dwell. It pleased the Father. The fullness is not a human achievement. It pleased the Father that it dwell in the Son.

Colossians 2:9-10 — “For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power.”

In Him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in Him. Complete. In Him. He is the head of all principality and power. You are not complete in a meeting. You are complete in Him.

1 Corinthians 1:24 — “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God. The same verse that forbade making water the power now sits in the fullness file. Power and wisdom are a Person.

1 Corinthians 12:27 — “Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.”

Ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular. The body into which the Spirit baptized you is not a club. It is His body. Members in particular. You are not a spare part in a warehouse. You are a member.

Galatians 2:20 — “I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.”

Crucified with Christ. Nevertheless I live. Yet not I, but Christ liveth in me. The life now lived in the flesh is by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me. Fullness is not a second man sitting beside the old man. Christ liveth in me.

2 Corinthians 2:14-16 — “Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place. For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?”

Always causeth us to triumph in Christ. The savour of His knowledge by us in every place. Sweet savour of Christ. To the one, death unto death. To the other, life unto life. Who is sufficient? The fullness file does not make you sufficient of yourself. It makes you a savour of Christ.

Ephesians 4:13 — “Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.”

Till we all come. Unity of the faith. Knowledge of the Son of God. Unto a perfect man. Unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ. Course 1’s maturity is not a different religion from this verse. Perfect man. Measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.

Fullness. Complete in Him. The Spirit not by measure unto you. This is not a slogan for a meeting. It is the son, whelmed, witnessing, complete.

Charge. Write the fullness Scripture set as one teaching: Colossians 1:19; 2:9-10; 1 Corinthians 1:24; 12:27; Galatians 2:20; 2 Corinthians 2:14-16; Ephesians 4:13. What does “complete in Him” refuse? What does it not turn into?

XIV. NOT SLAVES — YOU ARE THE FEAR AND DREAD

Not slaves. Not timidity.

2 Timothy 1:7 — “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

God hath not given us the spirit of fear. He has given the spirit of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. The three stand in one breath. Power without love is not this gift. Love without a sound mind is not this gift. A sound mind without power is not this gift.

It is not possible for you to fear. You rather are the fear and dread of the world: thieves and all wickedness alike, demons and Satan inclusive.

Genesis 9:1-2 — “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth. And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.”

God blessed Noah and his sons. Be fruitful, multiply, replenish — Genesis 1:28 heard again after the flood. And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast, every fowl, all that moveth, all the fishes. Into your hand are they delivered.

Deuteronomy 11:22-25 — “For if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; Then will the LORD drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves. Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be. There shall no man be able to stand before you: for the LORD your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.”

The LORD your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon. No man shall be able to stand before you. As He hath said unto you.

This school will not teach James 2:9 as this Scripture set. James 2:9 is respect of persons. It is not the fear-and-dread file. The owner locked Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. Also Romans 8:17; Genesis 1:26-28; Psalm 139:14.

Romans 8:17 you have: heirs of God, joint-heirs with Christ.

Genesis 1:26-28 you have: image, likeness, dominion.

Psalm 139:14 — “I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.”

Fearfully and wonderfully made. Heir. Image. Fearfully made. The charge is exact. It is not possible for you to fear. You are the fear and dread.

This school will not soften that charge for babes. Further reading: Why We’re Beyond — its own book, not Fearfully Made.

Do not turn the charge into boastful claim without the Scripture set. Power, love, and a sound mind stand in the same breath. An heir who has dropped love and a sound mind is not preaching 2 Timothy 1:7. He is performing. Genesis 9 and Deuteronomy 11 sit with Romans 8:17 and Genesis 1:26-28 and Psalm 139:14. The Scripture set is the guard. The charge is not withdrawn because someone might boastful claim. The boastful claim is refused because it dropped the Scripture set.

Charge. Teach 2 Timothy 1:7 with Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. Add Romans 8:17, Genesis 1:26-28, and Psalm 139:14. Do not soften for babes. Do not boastful claim without the Scripture set. Do not use James 2:9 here.

XV. ANANGELLŌ — HE SHALL SHEW YOU MINE

John 16:13-15 — “Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you. All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall shew it unto you.”

When He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will guide you into all truth. He shall not speak of Himself. Whatsoever He shall hear, that shall He speak. He will shew you things to come. He shall glorify Me. He shall receive of Mine, and shall shew it unto you. All things that the Father hath are Mine. Therefore said I, that He shall take of Mine, and shall shew it unto you.

Anangellō: to announce in detail — declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell.

Mine: the express image of God, announced unto you — express image and likeness of Me. Genesis 1:26-28.

The Spirit of truth does not invent another image. He shews what Course 2 already named: man made in the image, after the likeness, given dominion. He glorifies the Son. He does not speak of Himself.

Guide into all truth. Not into a private religion. All truth. He shall not speak of Himself. A spirit that advertises itself is not this Spirit. He takes of Mine. He announces in detail. Rehearse. Report. Show.

What is Mine? The tie is not vague property. Mine is the express image of God, announced unto you as express image and likeness of Me. Genesis 1:26-28. The Spirit who cries Abba is the Spirit who shews the image. Sonship and image are one household.

Course 3 depends on Courses 1 and 2. You cannot have Spirit witness of sonship without a son. You cannot have Mine announced as image if you emptied Genesis 1:26-28. The Spirit will not shew a different man than the one God made and Christ restored.

Charge. What is “Mine” in John 16:14-15 as Genesis 1:26-28 holds it? What does anangellō mean? What will the Spirit not do: speak of Himself, or invent another image?

XVI. FURTHER READING

Spirit Witness — its own book. Not a volume of Presence of Sons 1–4. If a catalogue once set the titles near each other, that proximity is bibliographic, not a series assignment.

Why We’re Beyond — its own book. Not Fearfully Made.

These are companions, not a seventh course. Directed sections when the volumes are in your hand. Completing this course does not require finishing every page of the library.

The next chapter opens laying on of hands: nine occasions, resultant, not a substitute for the three stones already named.

chapters.title: Laying on of Hands
chapters.body:
Hebrews 6:2 — “Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.”

When?

This teaching answers with nine occasions. Not a tenth. Not a vague practice called “immissions.” Nine accounts. Each its own text.

This principle is among the first principles. It is also the one this school will not let you treat as the foundation. It is viable only as you actualize the more grounding fundaments — repentance, faith toward God, the doctrine of baptisms. It plays a more resultant role, not substantively to the believer.

Do not skip the nine because they are resultant.
Do not make the nine a substitute for the three stones already laid.

This is the textbook of Foundation School, Aletheia Publications, under Dr. Coach Achu Gustave. Holy Scripture is the authority. The heading is “When?” and then nine occasions with their texts. You will learn each occasion as itself. You will not invent a tenth to make the file feel complete. The nine are complete.

This school names no required companion here. Directed reading later, if a volume is assigned. Completing this chapter does not wait on a book this school does not name.

I. RESULTANT — NOT THE FOUNDATION

Hands do not invent the son.
Hands do not replace metanoia.
Hands do not replace πίστις (pistis).
Hands do not replace baptism into Christ, water as figure, or the Spirit as witness.

A man who has not laid those stones and then treats hands as if they were the house has not heard “when?”

Hebrews 6:1-2 names repentance from dead works, faith toward God, the doctrine of baptisms, and then laying on of hands. The order is the writer’s. You do not begin the year at hands. You do not make hands the proof that the year has begun.

Hebrews 6:2 names this among the six. The same verse is cited again under imparting gifts. The principle is real. The role is resultant.

Resultant means what follows from what is already true. A result is not a root. If you treat a result as a root, you will baptize unrepentant men with hands, bless children as if hands were new birth, and sell the gift as Simon tried to buy it.

Viable only as you actualize the more grounding things. Actualize is not a slogan. Course 1: metanoia from dead works; the new creature; Christ the only way. Course 2: πίστις (pistis); son; heir; image; free justification. Course 3: into Christ; water as sign; Spirit as witness and enduement. Then hands.

It plays a more resultant role, not substantively to the believer. Substantively is the three stones. Resultant is this lesson. Both are in Hebrews 6:2. One is not the other.

When? After the grounding things are actualized. That is not a date on a calendar. It is an order in the man.

Charge of this section. Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? All three that stand before this one in Hebrews 6:1-2. Name them. Do not name a mood.

II. BLESSING MEN — GENESIS 48:14

Genesis 48:8-10 — “And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who are these? And Joseph said unto his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them. Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.”

Israel is old. His eyes are dim. He asks who these are. Joseph answers: my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. Bring them, I will bless them. He kisses them. He embraces them. The blessing is not a technique performed on strangers to prove a gift. These are Joseph’s sons, brought to the patriarch to be blessed.

Genesis 48:11-13 — “And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed. And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth. And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near unto him.”

Joseph arranges them for the custom: Manasseh the firstborn toward Israel’s right hand, Ephraim the younger toward Israel’s left. The right hand is the honour. Joseph knows the order of birth. He bows himself with his face to the earth.

Genesis 48:14 — “And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn.”

Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly. Wittingly. The dim eyes do not make the hands accidental. He guides them. The younger receives the right hand.

Genesis 48:15-16 — “And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.”

The blessing is spoken. God, before whom Abraham and Isaac walked. The God which fed me all my life long. The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads. Let my name be named on them. Let them grow into a multitude. The hands are laid. The mouth blesses. The God of the fathers is named.

Genesis 48:17-20 — “And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head unto Manasseh’s head. And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head. And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.”

Joseph objects. He holds up his father’s hand to uncross them. Not so, my father. This is the firstborn. Israel refuses. I know it, my son, I know it. The younger shall be greater. He set Ephraim before Manasseh. The occasion is blessing men. The hands are guided. The blessing is not Joseph’s arrangement. It is Israel’s, under God.

The account is a blessing of men, not a technique you copy without the God who spoke to the patriarch. Do not turn crossing hands into a method. Do not skip the spoken blessing as if the contact were the power. Read the chapter. The blessing is spoken. The hands are laid. Joseph objects. Israel will not uncross them.

Distinction. This is not ordaining. This is not healing. This is not imparting the Spirit. This is blessing men — Joseph’s sons — by a patriarch who names the God of Abraham and Isaac.

Charge. Write Genesis 48:14 in its place in 48:8-20. Who is blessed? Which hand goes where, and why wittingly? What will you not copy as a method without the God who spoke?

III. OFFERINGS — NUMBERS 8:10

Numbers 8:5-7 — “And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them. And thus shalt thou do unto them, to cleanse them: Sprinkle water of purifying upon them, and let them shave all their flesh, and let them wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean.”

The LORD speaks. Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them. Water of purifying. Shave. Wash. The offering of the Levites does not begin as a private ritual in a meeting. It begins as the LORD’s command to Moses.

Numbers 8:9-11 — “And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt gather the whole assembly of the children of Israel together: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites: And Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD for an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD.”

Bring the Levites before the tabernacle. Gather the whole assembly. Bring the Levites before the LORD. The children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites. Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD for an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD.

Numbers 8:10: “And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites.”

The congregation put their hands upon them. This is making offerings — identification and presentation — not a private ritual invented in a meeting. The hands of Israel on the Levites say: these are our offering before the LORD. Aaron offers them. They execute the service of the LORD.

Numbers 8:12-14 — “And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the heads of the bullocks: and thou shalt offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, unto the LORD, to make an atonement for the Levites. And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them for an offering unto the LORD. Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine.”

The Levites lay their hands upon the bullocks. Sin offering. Burnt offering. Atonement for the Levites. Set them before Aaron and his sons. Separate them. The Levites shall be Mine. The hands serve the offering God commanded. They do not invent a priesthood.

Numbers 8:19, 21-22 — “And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel: that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary. And the Levites were purified, and they washed their clothes; and Aaron offered them as an offering before the LORD; and Aaron made an atonement for them to cleanse them. And after that went the Levites in to do their service in the tabernacle of the congregation before Aaron, and before his sons: as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so did they unto them.”

Given as a gift. To do the service. After that they went in to do their service. As the LORD commanded Moses, so did they. The hands did not invent the service. The command did. The hands identified and presented.

Distinction. This is not blessing Joseph’s sons. This is not ordaining Joshua. This is making offerings. The children of Israel put their hands upon the Levites. The Levites are offered. Do not invent a priesthood by copying the gesture without the command.

Charge. What are the hands doing in Numbers 8:10? Who puts them on whom? Before whom? What do the hands not invent?

IV. ORDAINING — NUMBERS 27:18, 23

Numbers 27:15-17 — “And Moses spake unto the LORD, saying, Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the LORD be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

Moses is going to die. He asks the LORD to set a man over the congregation, that they be not as sheep which have no shepherd. The request is the LORD’s man, not Moses’ favourite.

Numbers 27:18-20 — “And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him; And set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight. And thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient.”

Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. A man in whom is the spirit already. Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation. Give him a charge in their sight. Put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation may be obedient.

Joshua is already a man in whom is the spirit. Moses lays his hand and gives him a charge. Ordaining here is not creating the Spirit in the man. It is charge, before the priest, before all the congregation, as the LORD commanded.

Numbers 27:21-23 — “And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation. And Moses did as the LORD commanded him: and he took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation: And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.”

He laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses. The charge is as commanded. The hands are as commanded. The man already has the spirit.

Do not make ordination a substitute for the Spirit already in the man. The text will not let you. A meeting that lays hands to create what God has not put in the man is not Numbers 27. A meeting that refuses to charge a man in whom the spirit already is, because it wants a more dramatic creation, has also left the text.

Hold this next to Deuteronomy 34:9. Do not flatten the two texts into one slogan. Numbers 27: the man in whom is the spirit; charge; hands. Deuteronomy 34: full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Two occasions in the file. One Joshua. Two texts. The next section will not let you merge them.

Distinction. Ordaining is not blessing men. It is not making offerings. It is not imparting Spirit as Deuteronomy 34 names it. It is charge upon a man in whom is the spirit already.

Charge. Write Numbers 27:18 and 27:23. What is already in Joshua before the hands? What do the hands and the charge do? What will you not make ordination into?

V. IMPARTING THE SPIRIT — DEUTERONOMY 34:9

Deuteronomy 34:5-8 — “So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD. And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.”

Moses dies. The servant of the LORD. According to the word of the LORD. Israel weeps thirty days. The days of weeping end. The next verse is not a funeral feeling. It is Joshua.

Deuteronomy 34:9-12 — “And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses. And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face, In all the signs and the wonders, which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land, And in all that mighty hand, and in all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.”

Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. The children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

The occasion is imparting Spirit. Full of the spirit of wisdom — for Moses had laid his hands upon him. The “for” is in the verse. This school will not erase it to protect a slogan from Numbers 27. This school will not erase Numbers 27 to make Deuteronomy 34 the only text.

Hold them beside each other. Do not flatten. Joshua was a man in whom is the spirit before the charge. He is full of the spirit of wisdom after the hands. Do not invent a tenth occasion to explain them. The teaching already has two occasions here: ordaining and imparting Spirit.

Israel hearkened. The fruit of the occasion is not a feeling in Moses. It is a people who hear the man charged, and do as the LORD commanded Moses. Hearkening is the test you can see. A man may claim impartation and have no people who will hear the word as the LORD commanded.

Moses is not the source of the Spirit. The LORD is. Moses laid his hands. Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom. The “for” stands. The flattening is refused.

Distinction. Imparting Spirit in Deuteronomy 34:9 is not the ninth occasion (imparting Spirit baptism in Acts). It is not Numbers 27’s ordaining flattened. It is its own text. Full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him.

Charge. Write Deuteronomy 34:9 next to Numbers 27:18 and 27:23. What does each text force? What tenth explanation will you refuse? What did Israel do after the hands?

VI. BLESSING CHILDREN — MATTHEW 19:13-15

Matthew 19:13-15 — “Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.”

Matthew 19:13-15 is the passage. Verse 15 closes the account. Then were there brought unto Him little children, that He should put His hands on them, and pray. The disciples rebuked them. Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto Me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And He laid His hands on them, and departed thence.

They were brought that He should put His hands on them, and pray. Hands and prayer. The disciples rebuked the bringing. The Lord would not. Suffer. Forbid them not. Of such is the kingdom of heaven. He laid His hands on them. He departed.

This is blessing children — not a dedication invented to replace new birth, and not a small thing you skip because the children are small.

Course 1 already told you new birth is in Christ, by receiving Him, by the word. Little children are not saved by a hand on the head in the place of that birth. The Lord did not say the hands were the womb. He said, Suffer them. Forbid them not. Of such is the kingdom. He laid His hands on them.

Do not make this occasion a replacement for repentance and faith. Do not refuse the occasion because you have learned that hands are resultant. Resultant is not worthless. The Lord laid His hands on them. The disciples were the ones who rebuked. Do not take the disciples’ part against the Lord and call it doctrine.

He departed thence. The blessing is not a long programme. He laid His hands on them, and departed. The kingdom word remains: of such is the kingdom of heaven.

Distinction. Blessing children is not blessing men as Genesis 48. It is not healing. It is not new birth. It is the Lord putting His hands on little children and praying, against the rebuke of His own disciples.

Charge. Write Matthew 19:13-15 in full. What did the disciples do? What did the Lord do? What will you not make this occasion into: a replacement for new birth, or a thing too small to teach?

VII. HEALING — MARK 6:2, 5; 16:18; ACTS 5:12

Mark 6:1-3 — “And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him. And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands? Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.”

He came into His own country. He taught in the synagogue. They were astonished. From whence hath this man these things? What wisdom is this which is given unto Him, that even such mighty works are wrought by His hands? Then they named the carpenter, the family, the sisters. They were offended at Him.

Mark 6:2 is in the file because of the hands: mighty works wrought by His hands. The astonishment turns to offence. Familiarity is not faith.

Mark 6:4-6 — “But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.”

He could there do no mighty work, save that He laid His hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. Nazareth limited what unbelief would receive. A few sick were still healed by His hands. He marvelled because of their unbelief. He went round about the villages, teaching.

Unbelief does not erase the occasion. It narrows what is received. The few are still in the verse. The hands are still on the sick. The healing is still done. Do not use Mark 6:5 to say hands do nothing. Do not use it to say unbelief is a small thing. He could there do no mighty work, save… He marvelled because of their unbelief.

Mark 16:15-18 — “And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned. And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.”

Go. Preach the gospel to every creature. He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved. Course 3 already taught you which baptism saves the soul, and what water is. Do not drag Mark 16:16 back into a tank-saviour. Signs shall follow them that believe. They shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

The risen Lord’s word to those who believe includes laying hands on the sick. This is not a substitute for preaching the gospel. The gospel is commanded first. The signs follow them that believe. Hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

Acts 5:12-16 — “And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people; (and they were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch. And of the rest durst no man join himself to them: but the people magnified them. And believers were the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women.) Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.”

By the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people. Believers were added to the Lord. The sick were brought. They were healed every one. The occasion this school names is healing — Mark 6:2, 5; 16:18; Acts 5:12. The shadow in Acts 5:15 is in the narrative. It is not a tenth occasion. The file says healing, and it names the hands texts.

This is not a substitute for repentance, faith, or baptism into Christ. It is an occasion in the file. Teach the texts. Do not invent a tenth healing system beside them.

Distinction. Healing is not blessing children. It is not miracles as Acts 19:11 names them in the next occasion. It is the sick recovered by hands, in the Lord’s own works, in His word to believers, and in the apostles’ hands.

Charge. Write Mark 6:2, Mark 6:5, Mark 16:18, and Acts 5:12. What did unbelief do at Nazareth? What did the risen Lord say them that believe shall do? What tenth healing system will you refuse?

VIII. MIRACLES — ACTS 19:11

Acts 19:8-10 — “And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God. But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus. And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.”

Paul is at Ephesus. Three months in the synagogue. Hardened. Believed not. He separates the disciples. Two years in the school of Tyrannus. All they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus. The word is first. The miracles are not a substitute for the word heard.

Acts 19:11-12 — “And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.”

God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul. God wrought. By the hands of Paul. The next verse tells of cloths from his body; the diseases departed; the evil spirits went out.

The occasion this school names is performing miracles — by the hands. Acts 19:11.

Do not make Paul the source. God wrought. Do not make the cloth a tenth occasion. The file says miracles, Acts 19:11. The cloths are in verse 12. They are how, in that narrative, the sick were reached. They are not a tenth item in the When? list.

Acts 19:13-17 will show men who treat the Name as a technique without the Lord. The seven sons of Sceva. The evil spirit answers. Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye? The man leaps on them. The Name is magnified. That narrative is a warning, not a tenth occasion. Hands and miracles in this lesson remain God’s work by Paul’s hands.

Distinction. Miracles in Acts 19:11 are not the healing teaching flattened. This chapter separates healing and miracles. Healing has its texts. Miracles has Acts 19:11. God wrought. By the hands of Paul. No tenth from the cloth.

Charge. Who wrought the special miracles? By whose hands? Why is the cloth not a tenth occasion? What happens if you make Paul the source?

IX. IMPARTING GIFTS — 1 TIMOTHY 4:14; 2 TIMOTHY 1:6; HEBREWS 6:2

1 Timothy 4:12-16 — “Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity. Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all. Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.”

Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. The gift is in him. It was given by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. Reading. Exhortation. Doctrine. Meditate. Give thyself wholly. Take heed unto thyself and unto the doctrine.

The hands of the presbytery sit with prophecy and with a gift not to be neglected. They do not sit in the place of doctrine. Take heed unto the doctrine. Continue in them.

2 Timothy 1:5-7 — “When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

Unfeigned faith first — grandmother, mother, and Timothy. Then: stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. The gift is in him. By the putting on of Paul’s hands. Stir it up. God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

Course 3 already taught 2 Timothy 1:7 with the fear-and-dread Scripture set. Here the verse sits next to the gift in him by the putting on of hands. Do not drop power, love, and a sound mind when you teach the gift. Do not drop the gift when you teach the spirit God has given.

Hebrews 6:2 names laying on of hands among the first principles, and that same verse is cited again under this occasion. The principle and the gift-occasion are not two religions. One file.

The gift is not to be neglected. It is to be stirred. Hands of the presbytery. Hands of Paul. Prophecy with the laying on.

Do not treat a gift as if it were the foundation. Do not treat the foundation as if it forbade gifts. A man who makes the gift the house has not heard resultant. A man who forbids the gift because he has learned repentance, faith, and baptisms has not heard Hebrews 6:2 twice — as principle and as this occasion.

Distinction. Imparting gifts is not imparting Spirit baptism. It is not ordaining flattened. It is the gift in thee, by prophecy, with the hands of the presbytery; the gift of God in thee by the putting on of Paul’s hands; and the same Hebrews 6:2 that named the principle.

Charge. Write 1 Timothy 4:14, 2 Timothy 1:6, and Hebrews 6:2. What is not to be neglected? What is to be stirred? Why is Hebrews 6:2 in this occasion as well as in the heading of the chapter?

X. IMPARTING SPIRIT BAPTISM — ACTS 8:17-24; 9:17; 19:6

Acts 8:14-17 — “Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.”

Samaria had received the word of God. They were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them. Peter and John prayed. Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

Course 3 already taught that water is after one is saved, and that the Spirit may be after water. This is that sequence in Samaria. The hands are in the account. The receiving is in the account.

Acts 8:18-24 — “And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity. Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.”

Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, and offered money. Give me also this power. Peter said the gift of God cannot be purchased. Thy money perish with thee. Thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Neither part nor lot. Heart not right. Repent. Gall of bitterness. Bond of iniquity.

This occasion includes the refusal of Simon. Do not teach the hands and skip the rebuke. The ninth account has a man who wanted the power without the heart. The answer is not a price. It is perish with thy money, and repent.

Acts 9:17-18 — “And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.”

Ananias putting his hands on Saul: Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. The Lord sent. Sight. Filled with the Holy Ghost. He arose, and was baptized. Hands, filling, then water in this house — as Course 3 already allowed. Ananias is not the baptizer in the Spirit as Course 3 named the agent. Christ is that baptizer. Ananias is sent. He puts his hands on him. Saul is filled.

Acts 19:1-6 — “And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost. And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus. When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.”

Certain disciples. Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost. Unto John’s baptism. Paul points them to Christ. They were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

John’s baptism is not Christian water and not Spirit. Course 3 numbered it first among the seven. Here men who had only that baptism hear of Christ, are baptized in His name, and the Holy Ghost comes when Paul lays hands.

Course 3 already taught that Christ baptizes in the Spirit, and that the Spirit may be given before water or after it. This occasion is imparting Spirit baptism by hands in these accounts. It does not cancel the agent Course 3 named. It does not make hands the foundation. It is the ninth in the file.

Christ remains the baptizer in the Spirit (Matthew 3:11; John 1:31-33). Acts 10 still stands: the Spirit fell while Peter yet spake, before water, without this chapter’s hands as the law. The ninth occasion does not cancel the tenth-not-invented, and it does not cancel the agent. Hands in Acts 8, 9, and 19 are in the file. They are resultant. They are not a second Christ.

Distinction. Imparting Spirit baptism is not imparting gifts. It is not Deuteronomy 34’s imparting Spirit flattened into Acts. It is Acts 8:17-24 with Simon refused, Acts 9:17, and Acts 19:6. Christ remains the Spirit-baptizer.

Charge. Write the three accounts. What did Simon want, and what did Peter say? Who sent Ananias? What came on the men at Ephesus when Paul laid hands? What agent will you not cancel?

XI. THE NINE AS ONE FILE

Write them until you can teach them without a tenth:

1. Blessing men — Genesis 48:14.
2. Making offerings — Numbers 8:10.
3. Ordaining — Numbers 27:18, 23.
4. Imparting Spirit — Deuteronomy 34:9.
5. Blessing children — Matthew 19:13-15.
6. Healing the sick — Mark 6:2, 5; 16:18; Acts 5:12.
7. Performing miracles — Acts 19:11.
8. Imparting gifts — 1 Timothy 4:14; 2 Timothy 1:6; Hebrews 6:2.
9. Imparting Spirit baptism — Acts 8:17-24; 9:17; 19:6.

All these attest a record across Holy Scripture. No invented tenth. Each occasion remains itself. Blessing children is not healing. Ordaining is not buying the gift. Simon is in the ninth account so that you will not make the ninth a market.

Hold ordaining beside imparting Spirit. A man in whom is the spirit already; then full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Two texts. One Joshua. No tenth invented to reconcile them.

Hold healing beside miracles. Healing has its Scripture set. Miracles has Acts 19:11. God wrought. The cloth is not a tenth.

Hold imparting gifts beside imparting Spirit baptism. A gift stirred is not the Holy Ghost purchased. Timothy is not Simon. The presbytery’s hands and Paul’s hands are not Simon’s money.

Hold the little-children passage beside Course 1. The Lord laid His hands on little children. He did not make the hands a second womb. Suffer them. Forbid them not.

Hold the whole nine beside Courses 1–3. Resultant. Not the house.

A vague practice called immissions is not this lesson. Nine accounts. Each its own text. If you cannot write the nine without looking, you are not ready to teach “when?”

Charge. Write the nine with their texts from memory. If you added a tenth, put it down. If you merged two, separate them. If you skipped Simon, write Acts 8:18-24.

XII. WHEN — THE CHARGE OF THIS CHAPTER

When? After the more grounding things are actualized.

Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? All three that stand before this one in Hebrews 6:1-2.

A man who has not turned from dead works, who has not faith toward God, who has not been baptized into Christ, is not ready to make hands the house. He may be busy with hands. He is not standing on the foundation.

Name one practice you will not treat as a foundation. If the practice is one of these nine, keep it resultant. If it is a tenth you invented, put it down.

You have walked nine occasions. Blessing men. Offerings. Ordaining. Imparting Spirit. Blessing children. Healing. Miracles. Gifts. Spirit baptism. Each with full writing. Each with a distinction. Each with a charge.
