The principle is among the first principles. The role is resultant. Viable as you actualize repentance, faith toward God, and the doctrine of baptisms. Not substantively to the believer as a substitute for those three.

Do not skip the nine because they are resultant.
Do not make the nine a substitute for the three stones already laid.
Do not invent a tenth.
Do not sell the ninth.
Do not flatten Joshua’s two texts.
Do not make the cloth a tenth.
Do not replace new birth with hands on a child.
Do not cancel Christ as Spirit-baptizer.

No required companion is named. No required companion is named here. This school will not invent a book to fill the mark. Completing this chapter does not wait on a volume this school does not name.

The next chapter opens resurrection of the dead: spiritual and material — two kinds, not one slogan. Spiritual resurrection is the new birth you already received, in this life only. Material resurrection is the body. You will not flatten them. You will not postpone new birth past death. You will learn the two issues, the thousand years, and the companies in their time.

Hands were never the last word. They were the fourth stone, resultant, named, limited, and taught. Lay them where Hebrews laid them. Then go on.

chapters.title: Resurrection of the Dead
chapters.body:
Hebrews 6:2 — “Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.”

This teaching opens this principle with two kinds. Not one slogan. Not a mood about “going to heaven.” Two kinds. Then two material issues a thousand years apart. Then five companies inside the first of those issues. Then a core sentence you will not flatten.

Hands were resultant. This stone is not a feeling after hands. It is the raising the writing already named: first the man from death in trespasses, in this life only; then the body from the grave, in its hour, in its company, in its issue.

You will not be given one rapture that swallows five. You will not be given a second advent that is rapture 2. You will not be given a Millennium that is the last judgment. You will not raise the wicked before the thousand years. You will not offer new birth after death.

Sit under this chapter. The chronology is dense. This chapter opens it until you can recite it without rewriting it into another school.

I. TWO KINDS

There are two main kinds of resurrection: spiritual and material.

Kind is the first sentence under the heading. Kind is not a decoration. Kind is the first cut. If you mix the kinds, every later hour will lie.

Spiritual resurrection is the new birth: being quickened — revived — from dead in trespasses and sins, renewed in the glorious likeness of God. It is now. It is this life. It is the man, not the corpse.

Material resurrection is the resurrection of the body, not spirit. The graves. The voice. Two issues. A thousand years between them.

Hold the Scripture set already. Ephesians 2:1-6; Ephesians 4:21-24; Colossians 3:10; 1 John 3:9 name the spiritual kind. John 5:28-29 names the material kind. Revelation 20 times the two material issues. Daniel 12 stands with them. The Scripture facts grounds the hope of the flesh. The five companies complete the first material rising. The core sentence keeps the order from collapsing.

Distinction. Spiritual is not a poetic name for the body’s rising. Material is not a late name for new birth. A man may be quickened now and still wait for the grave to give his body. A corpse may be raised later who was never quickened here. The kinds do not trade places.

Principle. Hebrews 6:2 names resurrection of the dead among the first principles. This teaching will not let you treat that name as one event. Two kinds first. Then, inside the material kind, two issues. Then, inside the first issue, five companies.

Reasoning. If you call every rising “the resurrection,” you will preach new birth as if it were a future grave, and you will preach the grave as if it were another chance to be born. The writing will not carry that mixture. Course 1 already quickened you, if you have received Him. This chapter does not invent a second new birth. It names that quickening as spiritual resurrection, and then it opens the body.

Application. When you hear “resurrection” this year, you will ask: which kind? If spiritual, you will stay in this life. If material, you will ask: which issue — life or damnation? If the first issue, you will ask: which company? You will not answer with a slogan.

Charge of this section. Write the two kinds as they are set here. Spiritual: what rises, when, which texts. Material: what rises, when the two issues fall, which texts. Do not write a third kind. Do not write one kind with two nicknames.

II. SPIRITUAL — EPHESIANS 2:1-6

Ephesians 2:1 — “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;”

Ephesians 2:2 — “Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:”

Ephesians 2:3 — “Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.”

Ephesians 2:4 — “But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,”

Ephesians 2:5 — “Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)”

Ephesians 2:6 — “And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:”

Who speaks? Paul, to saints, and to you if you are in that same Christ. To whom? Men dead in trespasses and sins — not the graves of John 5:28. Why? To name what God has already done: quickened, raised up together, seated in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.

Quickened is revived. The raising here is together with Him, now — not the later hour when all that are in the graves hear His voice.

Context. Course 1 already opened this Scripture set as the only way. The same verses return under another name. Spiritual resurrection is that new birth. It is not a second conversion invented for a later course.

Scripture set. Ephesians 2:1-6 with Ephesians 4:21-24, Colossians 3:10, and 1 John 3:9. This six opens the death and the quickening. The three open likeness.

Distinction. Ephesians 2:6 is not John 5:28. Seated in heavenly places is not all graves coming forth. If you preach Ephesians 2 as if your body had put on immortality, you have left this teaching. If you preach John 5 as a new attitude only, you have left it the other way.

Principle. Spiritual resurrection is the new birth. You hath He quickened. The verb is His.

Reasoning. If you were dead, you did not raise yourself. Grace is in the parenthesis because the quickening is not wages. The seat is not a later prize for men who remain dead.

Application. You will not wait for a funeral to become alive to God. If you are still dead in trespasses, this life is the hour. Section IV will shut the door after death.

Charge. Write Ephesians 2:1-6 in full. Mark the death, the quickening, the together, the seat. Write one sentence you will not say: that this passage is the graves of John 5.

III. LIKENESS — EPHESIANS 4, COLOSSIANS 3, FIRST JOHN 3:9

This teaching does not leave spiritual resurrection as a rescue from wrath only. It is renewed in the glorious likeness of God.

Ephesians 4:21 — “If so be that ye have heard him, and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus:”

Ephesians 4:22 — “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;”

Ephesians 4:23 — “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;”

Ephesians 4:24 — “And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

After God. That is likeness. Course 2 already named image and likeness from Genesis 1:26-28. The new man is created after God. Righteousness. True holiness. Not a costume.

Colossians 3:10 — “And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:”

Ye have put on the new man, renewed in knowledge after the image of Him that created him. The rising is not ignorance decorated with a testimony.

1 John 3:9 — “Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.”

Born of God. Seed remaineth. This teaching sets this in the spiritual-resurrection Scripture set, not as a later slogan you may empty. The birth is the rising.

Scripture set. Ephesians 4:21-24; Colossians 3:10; 1 John 3:9 with Ephesians 2:1-6. Quickened men put on what God created.

Distinction. Likeness restored in new birth is not the immortal body of 1 Corinthians 15. Do not steal Paul’s later chapter to explain John’s new birth. Do not steal John’s new birth to cancel Paul’s later body.

Principle. Spiritual resurrection renews you in the glorious likeness of God.

Reasoning. If the new man is created after God, you do not design him. If His seed remaineth, the birth is not a meeting you forget by Thursday.

Application. Read Genesis 1:26-28 beside these verses. Do not treat spiritual resurrection as a ticket that leaves the image untouched. Do not postpone holiness until the grave opens.

Charge. Write the three likeness texts in full. What is put off? What is put on? After whose image?

IV. THIS LIFE ONLY

Spiritual resurrection takes place only in this life.

When you leave this life, or world, all possibilities of new birth salvation or spiritual resurrection have passed, and are forfeited if you are not yet born again.

The window is locked to two writings. Not a third. Not a verse Paul used for another argument.

Hebrews 9:27 — “And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:”

Appointed. Once to die. After this the judgment. The appointment is not a rumour. The once is not a cycle of second births. After death the writing does not open a mourner’s bench. It opens judgment.

Revelation 22:11 — “He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still.”

Unjust still. Filthy still. Righteous still. Holy still. The still is not encouragement to delay. It is the fixing of the man as he is. You will not preach a new birth on the far side of that still.

Scripture set. Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11. That is the forfeiture file. Two verses. Use them as a unit. Do not add a proverb the school has dropped. Do not drag 1 Corinthians 15:19 across this door.

1 Corinthians 15:19 will be taught in the Scripture facts and in the hope of the body, where Paul set it. Hear the warning now so you do not misuse it later.

1 Corinthians 15:19 — “If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.”

Paul is not defining new birth. He is proving material resurrection. If there is no resurrection of the dead, Christ is not raised; preaching and faith are vain; the dead in Christ are perished. If hope in Christ were limited to this present life only — no bodily rising — we would be the most miserable of men.

This teaching places 15:19 beside “only in this life” for the spiritual kind. This school will not make that print teach the opposite of Paul’s argument. Forfeiture stands on Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11. Bodily hope stands on 15:12-19. 15:19 stays there.

Distinction. This-life window for new birth is not this-life-only hope in Christ. Do not preach 15:19 as “no new birth after death.” Do not preach Hebrews 9:27 as if it cancelled the body’s rising.

Principle. Spiritual resurrection is this life only. After death, if you are not born again, the possibility is forfeited.

Reasoning. Once to die, after this the judgment: metanoia in the grave breaks the appointment. Unjust still: no second birth to the dead. 15:19 proves the body, not the forfeiture.

Application. You will not wait. Course 1 is still the door. You will also not become a man with spiritual life and no bodily hope. That inversion is the misery Paul named.

Charge. Why can new birth not be postponed past death? Write Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11 as a unit. Write 15:19 in 15:12-19, and say what you will not make it prove.

V. MATERIAL — JOHN 5:28-29

Material resurrection is the resurrection of the body, not spirit.

John 5:25 — “Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.”

John 5:28 — “Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice,”

John 5:29 — “And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.”

Hear the two hours. Verse 25: the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and they that hear shall live. That now is sits with the spiritual kind you have already learned — the dead in trespasses hearing and living. Verse 28: marvel not at this. Another hour is coming. All that are in the graves shall hear His voice. They shall come forth. Two issues: life, and damnation.

This teaching prints 5:28-29 as the material text. The graves. The coming forth. Body, not spirit. All. Two destinies.

Who speaks? The Son, who has life in Himself and authority to execute judgment because He is the Son of man. The voice that quickens now will empty graves later.

Scripture set. John 5:28-29 with Daniel 12 and Revelation 20. Two issues, not one morning. Revelation 20 will set the thousand years between them.

Distinction. “Now is” in 5:25 is not “the graves” in 5:28. Material resurrection is not a ghost. The graves hear. They come forth. Bodies.

The soul and spirit of man is immortal. Course 6 will open the prisons. This chapter’s material word is already fixed: resurrection of the dead refers to the bodies which die and will be raised from dust again.

Principle. Material resurrection is the body. All in the graves come forth — to life or to damnation.

Reasoning. If all come forth, the wicked are not left as unbodied shades. If there are two issues, there is not one general rising on one morning.

Application. Marvel not. Do not reduce the call to a metaphor, or the two issues to one funeral sermon.

Charge. Who comes forth? To what two resurrections? Write John 5:28-29 in full. Write what 5:25’s “now is” is not.

VI. TWO ISSUES — REVELATION 20

There are two physical, bodily issues: first, the righteous to life before the Millennium; and the wicked — unsaved, unregenerate — to damnation, the lake of fire, after the Millennium. A thousand years between the two.

John 5 named the two issues. Revelation 20 times them. Daniel 12 stands in the same Scripture set. That is the doctrine’s carrying Scripture set. You will not build the two-resurrection doctrine from Revelation 10.

Daniel 12:2 — “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Daniel 12:3 — “And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

Sleep in the dust. Awake. Some to everlasting life. Some to shame and everlasting contempt. This teaching places 12:3 with this lesson. 12:2 is the waking the 12:3 shining assumes. Dust is body. Awake is material. Two issues again.

Revelation 20:4 — “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

Revelation 20:5 — “But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.”

Revelation 20:6 — “Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.”

The correct reference is Revelation 20:4-6. Chapter 20 has no verse 46. You will teach 20:4-6. All who have part in the first resurrection rule with Christ from the Millennium.

Revelation 20:10 — “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.”

Revelation 20:11 — “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.”

Revelation 20:12 — “And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

Revelation 20:13 — “And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.”

Revelation 20:14 — “And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.”

Revelation 20:15 — “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

This is the resurrection of damnation timed. The wicked are raised together after the Millennium, judged, and cast into the lake of fire, forever. They are not raised before the thousand years. The rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.

The Millennium is not the last judgment. The last judgment in this lesson is the great white throne after the thousand years.

Do not place the two bodily resurrections in Revelation 10. The thousand years between them is Revelation 20:4-6, sitting with Daniel 12:3 and John 5:28-29.

Revelation chapter 10 has eleven verses. There is no 10:12. There is no 10:15. “10:4-6, 11-15” is not a real range. You will not invent verses to save a typesetting. You will not move the two-resurrection doctrine into chapter 10.

Teach Revelation 10:4-6 as what it is: the seven thunders, and the oath that there should be time no longer.

VII. THE CORE ORDER

The Millennium is the one thousand years period after the tribulation: the tribulation is seven years after rapture 2, and rapture 2 is not the second advent; the second advent — coming of Christ with the saints — is after tribulation, ushering the Millennium: Revelation 6–19.

That sentence is the core of this chapter. You will learn it as a doctrinal order, not as a slogan you may rearrange.

Millennium is the one thousand years after the tribulation. It is not a present metaphor for a successful church. It is not the last judgment. It is the period in which they that have part in the first resurrection live and reign with Christ, as 20:4-6 already said.

Tribulation here is seven years after rapture 2. The seven is the number. The after is the order. You will not invert it to make tribulation the waiting room from which rapture 2 collects the church.

Rapture 2 is not the second advent. The page says so in the same breath. If you make them one coming, the order collapses, Company 4 has no “come back with,” and “with the saints” becomes the same motion as “receive you unto Myself.”

Second advent is the coming of Christ with the saints, after tribulation, ushering the Millennium. The range the page gives for that span of judgment-and-return is Revelation 6–19. The appearing that closes the span is 19:11-21. You will open that appearing in section IX. You will not call 19:11 rapture 2.

Order, as the page builds it, not as another school prefers it:

Company 1 past — first resurrection begins. This age — spiritual resurrection this life only. Company 2 — rapture 2 — before the tribulation. Then seven years: Company 3, first half; Company 4 after rapture 2, in time to return; Company 5, two witnesses, first resurrection ends. Then advent with the saints, ushering the Millennium. Then the thousand years; the rest of the dead wait. Then the rest live again. Great white throne. Lake of fire.

Distinction. Rapture 2 starts the seven. Advent ends the seven and ushers the thousand. Millennium is after tribulation, not a name for the throne.

Principle. The order is fixed. Millennium after tribulation. Tribulation seven years after rapture 2. Rapture 2 is not the second advent. Advent with the saints after tribulation ushers the Millennium. Range: Revelation 6–19.

Reasoning. If rapture 2 were the advent, the tribulation could not be seven years after rapture 2 while the advent is after tribulation. Receive unto Himself before. With the saints after.

Application. Recite the order before you recite a favourite preacher. Do not ask only “rapture or tribulation first?” Five companies hang on this sentence. Revelation 20 hangs after it.

Charge. Write the order from memory. If you merged rapture 2 and the advent, separate them. If you made the Millennium the throne, put the throne after the thousand years.

Company 3: the hundred and forty and four thousand Jews, saved in the first half of the tribulation. Still first resurrection. Not rapture 2. Not the advent.

The assigned reference listed Revelation 7:18. Chapter 7 has seventeen verses. The course uses the text: Revelation 7:1-8 only for this company. You will not teach 7:18. You will not make 7:9-17 the hundred forty and four thousand. 7:9-17 is a great multitude of all nations — that teaching belongs with Company 4, not with the sealing of Israel’s tribes.

Revelation 7:1 — “And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.”

Revelation 7:2 — “And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea,”

Revelation 7:3 — “Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

Revelation 7:4 — “And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

Revelation 7:5 — “Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Reuben were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Gad were sealed twelve thousand.”

Revelation 7:6 — “Of the tribe of Aser were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Nepthalim were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand.”

Revelation 7:7 — “Of the tribe of Simeon were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Levi were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand.”

Revelation 7:8 — “Of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Benjamin were sealed twelve thousand.”

First half of the tribulation. After rapture 2. Still first resurrection — another sheaf, not the wicked.

Distinction. 7:1-8 is not 7:9-17. Revelation 7 has no verse 18; use Revelation 7:1-8 for this point.

Principle. Company 3 is 144,000 Jews, first half, Revelation 7:1-8 only.

Reasoning. Sealed after the seven has begun: not Company 2. Israel’s tribes as numbered: not a Gentile slogan. 7:9 says “after this”: not the same company.

Application. Read 7:1-8 as 7:1-8. Let Company 4 have the multitude.

Charge. Write Revelation 7:1-8 in full. Who is sealed? What verse will you not cite?

XVI. COMPANY 4 — THE GREAT MULTITUDE AFTER RAPTURE 2

Company 4: the great multitude of tribulation saints after rapture 2. Revelation 6:1–19:21. All in time to come back with Christ for the Millennium. Revelation 19:11-21.

They exist so that “with the saints” is not an empty phrase. Rapture 2 has already received a company. The seven still saves. Those saved in the seven are first-resurrection people, not leftovers for the lake. They must be gathered in time to return with Him when heaven opens.

Revelation 7:9 — “After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;”

Revelation 7:13 — “And one of the elders answered, saying unto me, What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?”

Revelation 7:14 — “And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.”

Came out of great tribulation. Washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. All nations. No man could number. This multitude is not the 144,000. It sits in the Company 4 file as the page’s “great multitude of tribulation saints after rapture 2.” The full span is 6:1–19:21 — seals, trumpets, vials, Babylon, then the return.

You will not teach every plague here as if this chapter were a commentary on all of Revelation 6–18. You will know the span. You will know they are after rapture 2. You will know they return with Him.

Revelation 19:14 you have: the armies which were in heaven followed Him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. In time to come back. That is the purpose-clause for this company.

Distinction. After rapture 2 is not instead of rapture 2. During the seven is not before the seven. Return with Christ is not receive unto Myself. First resurrection still — they are not the rest of the dead. They are not raised after the Millennium to the lake.

Principle. Company 4: tribulation saints after rapture 2, in the span of Revelation 6:1–19:21, in time to come back with Christ, 19:11-21, for the Millennium.

Reasoning. If no one were added in the seven, the advent “with the saints” would be only Company 2 returning, and the page would not have named a fourth company. If they were the wicked, they would wait until 20:5b. They do not. They follow Him in linen.

Application. You will not preach a seven in which God has no first-resurrection people. You will not preach a return with nobody behind Him. You will not collapse 4 into 2 because both are “saints.”

Charge. Name Company 4: who, when, span, purpose. Write 7:9 and 7:14. Write what “in time to come back” forbids you to do with the advent.

XVII. COMPANY 5 — THE TWO WITNESSES

Company 5: the rapture of the two witnesses. The first resurrection ends — the same first resurrection that began with Christ.

Revelation 11:7 — “And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.”

Revelation 11:8 — “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

Revelation 11:9 — “And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and an half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves.”

Revelation 11:10 — “And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.”

Revelation 11:11 — “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Revelation 11:12 — “And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.”

This is material. Bodies stood and ascended. Come up hither. Late in the seven. The first resurrection ends here. It began with Christ. Beginning and ending are not the same hour.

Distinction. Company 5 ends the first resurrection. It does not replace Company 2. It does not raise the wicked.

Principle. Two witnesses, Revelation 11:7-12. First resurrection ends. It began with Christ.

Reasoning. If you start and stop the first resurrection at Company 2, you have erased both the beginning and the ending the page named.

Application. Do not call Company 5 “the rapture.” Do not extend the first resurrection to the rest of the dead. 20:5 has forbidden that.

Charge. Name Company 5: who, when, texts. What begins with Christ? What ends here? Who is still not raised?

XVIII. CHARGE, AND MILLENNIUM AS COMPANION

Recite.

Two kinds. Spiritual: new birth, quickened from trespasses, renewed in likeness, this life only. Ephesians 2:1-6; Ephesians 4:21-24; Colossians 3:10; 1 John 3:9. Forfeiture: Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11. Not 1 Corinthians 15:19 as that proof.

Material: body, not spirit. John 5:28-29. Two issues, a thousand years: righteous to life before the Millennium; wicked after, to the lake, Revelation 20:10-15. Doctrine carried by John 5, Revelation 20:4-6, Revelation 20:11-15, Daniel 12. Revelation 10:4-6 is thunders and time no longer. Not the two-resurrection chapter. The correct reference is Revelation 20:4-6.

Core order. Millennium: one thousand years after tribulation. Tribulation: seven years after rapture 2. Rapture 2 is not the second advent. Second advent: Christ with the saints after tribulation, ushers the Millennium. Range: Revelation 6–19.

Temporary: Matthew 9:25, dies again. Permanent: immortal body, Christ firstfruits of all permanent, 1 Corinthians 15:1-23. Matthew 27:52-53 saints now in heaven with their bodies. No other Foundation School teaching.

Five companies in the first resurrection. 1 Past: Christ and the many saints — 1 Corinthians 15:20, 23; Matthew 27:52-53; Ephesians 4:8-10. Begins. 2 Rapture 2: they that are Christ’s at His coming — 1 Corinthians 15:23, 51-54; John 14:1-3; Luke 21:34-36; 2 Corinthians 5:1-8. Before the seven. Not advent. 3 Hundred forty and four thousand Jews, first half — Revelation 7:1-8 only. 4 Great multitude after rapture 2 — Revelation 6:1–19:21; return with Him, 19:11-21. 5 Two witnesses — Revelation 11:7-12. Ends.

Refuse, in writing, the five flattenings this chapter will not carry: one rapture swallowing 1–5; advent treated as rapture 2; Millennium treated as the last judgment; the wicked raised before the Millennium; new birth offered after death.

Charge 29. Separate spiritual from material in one page a babe can follow.

Charge 30. Why can new birth not be postponed past death? Use Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11 as a unit. Keep 15:19 with bodily hope.

Charge 31. John 5:28-29: who comes forth, to what two resurrections?

Charge 32. A thousand years between the two: place both issues on the chronology.

Charge 33. Rapture 2 is not the second advent: state the difference from the core sentence.

Charge 34. Five raptures in the first resurrection: name who, when, and the texts. Do not merge 2 and the advent.

Charge 35. Temporary versus permanent: why Matthew 9:25 is not 1 Corinthians 15:20-23.

Charge 36. All without Christ raised after the Millennium: who is not in the first resurrection?

This teaching marked further reading: Millennium.

Millennium is a companion volume, not a seventh course, not a seventh principle, not a substitute for Hebrews 6:2. Directed sections when the book is in your hand — the thousand years, the reign, the binding that Course 6 will name as the abyss — not an assignment to finish every page of a library before you may close this chapter. Completing this stone does not require purchasing the whole first wave. Completing this stone does require the core order, the two kinds, the two issues, and the five companies without flattening.

An Intensive student writes longer. A Walk student writes the same doctrine shorter. The chronology does not change with the clock.

The next chapter opens eternal judgment: eternal punishment, the book of life, three deaths, five prisons, none identical with the grave. This chapter will not steal that file.

Write the order. Write the five. Write the two kinds. Then teach a babe without flattening. That is the charge of resurrection of the dead.

chapters.title: Eternal Judgment
chapters.body:
Hebrews 6:2 — “Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.”

This is the last of the six. Course 5 mapped the two bodily issues, the thousand years, and the companies. This chapter sits on that map. You do not reopen the companies. You learn duration, the book, the blotting, the three deaths, and the five prisons. None of those prisons is the grave.

In this present age the righteous who die go to heaven. The wicked go to hell. After the Millennium hell is emptied, the dead stand before the great white throne, and whosoever is not found written in the book of life is cast into the lake of fire. That is the map.

Eternal is duration. Not metaphor. Not annihilation. Soul and spirit are immortal. Resurrection texts in this lesson are bodies from the dust. Three deaths stay three. Five prisons stay five.

I. ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

Matthew 25:46 is translated eternal punishment. The King James reads everlasting punishment and life eternal. Everlasting and eternal are duration. The goats do not go into a figure of loss. They go away into punishment that does not end. The sheep go into life that does not end. One verse, two destinies, same kind of duration.

Matthew 25:31-33 — “When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.”

This is not a parable you may empty into a social mood. The King is judging. Sheep on the right. Goats on the left.

Matthew 25:34 — “Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:”

Matthew 25:41 — “Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:”

The fire was prepared for the devil and his angels. Men who stand with that rebellion enter it. Prepared is not a metaphor for disappointment.

Matthew 25:46 — “And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.”

Punishment. Not a pause. Not a wiping out of the person. translation is eternal punishment. You will not turn aionios into “age-long until they vanish.” You will not turn punishment into “they simply cease.” Cease is not punishment that goes on. Annihilation is not this verse.

Revelation 14:9-11 — “And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.”

Smoke of torment that ascends for ever and ever is not a brief pain and then nothing. No rest day nor night is not sleep, and not a metaphor for regret that later cools. For ever and ever is duration.

Revelation 14:14 is the Son of man on a cloud — harvest. The lake-of-fire passage later sits 14:9-11 with 14:14. Do not flatten the angel’s warning into the harvest so that torment disappears.

Revelation 20:11-15 — “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

Great white throne — after the Millennium on Course 5’s map. Hell delivers up. Hell is not the last room. The lake is. Section XII will keep hell until the Millennium’s end. Section XIV will keep the lake as gehenna. Do not merge them here.

Isaiah 66:22-24 — “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD. And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.”

The worm does not die. The fire is not quenched. That is not a short burning of a corpse that then is gone. A dead worm and a quenched fire would be annihilation’s picture. Mark 9 will say it again under gehenna.

Eternal is duration. Not metaphor. Not annihilation. Everlasting punishment. Smoke for ever and ever. No rest day nor night. Worm does not die. Fire not quenched. Second death in the lake. If you preach a kinder vanishing, you have left Matthew 25:46.

Course 1 already forbade Hell-avoidance as if it were metanoia. Eternal punishment is real. It is not the definition of repentance. You lay both stones.

Charge of this section. Write Matthew 25:46. What is translated eternal punishment? Write Revelation 14:11 and Isaiah 66:24. What do “for ever and ever,” “no rest,” and “worm shall not die” refuse? Name annihilation and name metaphor. Put both down.

II. THE BOOK OF LIFE

Revelation 20:15 — “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

Whosoever. Not a class exempted by rank. Not a nation exempted by history. Not a minister exempted by office. Not a rich man exempted by purple. Not a poor man exempted by sores. Whosoever was not found written.

Acts 10:34-35 — “Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

God is no respecter of persons. Peter says it at a Gentile’s house. The book of life is not a Jewish privilege and a Gentile rumour. It is not a Gentile slogan that empties Israel. In every nation. He that feareth Him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with Him. Status does not write the name. Status does not blot the name. God is no respecter of persons.

Revelation 20:12 already opened the books and another book, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. Then 20:15: if the name is not in the book of life, the lake.

Works are in the books. The name is in the book of life, or it is not. Do not flatten the two into one ledger you can balance by labour. Do not empty either sentence.

Revelation 20:14 — “And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.”

The second death is the lake. Whosoever not found written is cast in. That casting is the second death.

Whom does “whosoever” refuse to exempt? The man who thought his office, his nation, his poverty, or his Course 1 tears were a second book if he never received the Son. God is no respecter of persons.

The book of life is not a contradiction of sonship. It is the throne’s record. Overcome, and He will not blot — section III. Refuse the Son, and you shall not see life — John 3:36.

This scene is after the Millennium. You will not move the great white throne into the present age. You will not postpone the book until a later kindness God did not write.

Charge of this section. Whom does “whosoever” refuse to exempt? Write Revelation 20:15 and Acts 10:34. Write what the books contain and what the book of life decides. Do not invent a respecter of persons God refused.

III. BLOTTING OF NAMES

God blots the names of sinners out of His book. The book of life is not a slogan of unconditional listing. A name can be written. A name can be blotted. The warning is for those who refuse to be born again, and for those who take away from the words of this book.

Exodus 32:31-33 — “And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold. Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin--; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. And the LORD said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.”

Moses offers himself. Blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. The LORD will not take the substitute Moses offers in that sentence. Whosoever hath sinned against Me, him will I blot out of My book. The blot lands on the sinner. Not on the intercessor who has not sinned that sin in Moses’ place.

Whosoever again. God is no respecter of persons in writing or in blotting.

Psalm 69:20-21 — “Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none. They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.”

This blotting was predicted of Judas. Gall and vinegar sit in the psalm. The Gospels will show you the cup.

Psalm 69:22-28 — “Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap. Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake. Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them. Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents. For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded. Add iniquity unto their iniquity: and let them not come into thy righteousness. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.”

Acts 1:20 sets “let their habitation be desolate” on Judas. Predicted of Judas. You will not move this psalm off him. Course 1 already distinguished μεταμέλομαι (metamellomai) from metanoia. Judas regretted condemnation. Do not baptize that remorse into new birth.

John 3:36 — “He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.”

Christ warned of the blot for all who refuse to be born again. Life is in the Son. Wrath abideth — not a passing weather. Refuse the Son, and you shall not see life.

Revelation 3:5 — “He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.”

The promise not to blot is spoken to the overcomer. The verse is not a charm you wear while you refuse the Son.

Revelation 22:18-19 — “For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.”

The verses are Revelation 22:18-19. Teach the two verses. Do not invent a third address. Take away the words, and the part in the book is taken away.

Hold the file as one. Exodus 32:32-33 — God blots the sinner, not Moses in his place. Psalm 69:20-28 — predicted of Judas. John 3:36 — refuse the Son. Revelation 3:5 — the overcomer is not blotted. Revelation 22:18-19 — take away the words, and the part is taken.

The book is not a slogan of unconditional listing. It is not a threat you use to keep babes shivering and never receiving the Son.

Charge of this section. Teach Exodus 32:32-33, Psalm 69:20-28, and Revelation 3:5 as one Scripture set. Who is blotted in Exodus? Of whom was Psalm 69 predicted? What does Revelation 3:5 promise the overcomer? Write John 3:36 and Revelation 22:18-19. Name the print 22:1819 and keep the two verses.

IV. DEATH AS CUTTING OFF FROM GENESIS 1:26-28

Dead in the Bible predominantly, if not definitely, means man’s separation or cutting off from realizing God’s purpose for which he was created. That purpose is Genesis 1:26-28. Teach those verses as written. Do not put a softer sentence in their place.

Genesis 1:26 — “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.”

Course 2 already read ’ĕlōhîm as plural: Trinity. “Let us make” is not a committee of angels inventing a lesser thing. Image. Likeness. Dominion in the same breath.

Genesis 1:27 — “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”

The Living Bible (TLB) gloss, kept as a gloss beside the KJV, not as a rival Bible: “So God made man like his Maker. Like God did God make man; Man and maid did he make them.”

Like his Maker. Mark it TLB. Keep the KJV as the text you teach. God created man in His own image. Male and female created He them.

Genesis 1:28 — “And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.”

Fruitful. Multiply. Replenish. Subdue. Have dominion. Male and female. The making as written. Man is who he is by design and by Who designed him.

Death is cutting off from realizing that purpose. Not a poetry about sleep that never answers Genesis. A man may still walk and already be cut off. A man may already be in the dust and still be a soul. Sections V–VII will keep three deaths. Here you define the word without using only “stopped breathing.”

This chapter keeps a Scripture set with Genesis 1:26-28. You will not detach it. You will not use it to empty the verses.

John 14:12 — “Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.”

1 John 4:17 — “Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.”

Boldness in the day of judgment. This chapter is that day in view. As He is, so are we in this world. The making was not cancelled so that judgment could be preached to a lesser creature. Judgment is preached to the man God made.

Psalm 82:6 — “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

Romans 8:17 — “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

John 17:20-23 — “Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.”

Death cuts a man off from realizing that purpose. Spiritual death is that cut while he still breathes. Physical death is the inner man leaving the outer. The second death is that cut made eternal in the lake.

You will not hedge Genesis 1:26-28 to make death smaller. Restoration in Christ is not a new species God did not make. It is the man brought back on course.

If you define death only as the heart stopping, you will not hear Matthew 8:22. If you define it only as the lake, you will flatten three into one. Define it first as cutting off from Genesis 1:26-28. Then keep the three.

Charge of this section. Define death without using only “stopped breathing.” Write Genesis 1:26-28 as written. Write the TLB as TLB. What purpose is a dead man cut off from? Hold one sentence from John 14:12 or 1 John 4:17 with the making, not against it.

V. PHYSICAL DEATH — INNER FROM OUTER

Physical death is the separation of the inner man from the outer man: soul and spirit from the body. James 2:26 is the verse.

James 2:26 — “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.”

The body without the spirit is dead. Inner from outer. Do not steal the verse from this lesson to preach only ethics.

Genesis 35:18 — “And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Benoni: but his father called him Benjamin.” The soul departs. She dies.

Ecclesiastes 12:7 — “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.” The verse is the split, not a third prison. The body is dust until resurrection. The soul did not become dust.

Luke 8:55 — “And her spirit came again, and she arose straightway: and he commanded to give her meat.” Physical death reversed for a time. Course 5 already distinguished temporary raising from the immortal body. Do not flatten Matthew 9:25 into 1 Corinthians 15.

Physical death is not Tartarus. It is not Paradise. It is not hell. It is not the abyss. It is not the lake. It is the split. The body without the spirit is dead. The grave holds the body. The grave is not one of the five prisons.

A man can be physically alive and spiritually dead. Section VI. A man can be physically dead and not yet in the second death. Section VII. Keep this one as this one.

Charge of this section. Write James 2:26. What separates from what? What does physical death not equal among the five prisons? Why is the grave not this lesson’s prison?

VI. SPIRITUAL DEATH — FROM GOD BECAUSE OF SIN

Spiritual death is the separation of man from God because of sin. The man may walk. He may bury. He may live in pleasure. He is dead.

Matthew 8:21-22 — “And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father. But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.”

Follow Me. Let the dead bury their dead. The buriers are dead while they walk. The buried are dead in the body. The Lord will not let you hear only one death in that sentence. This teaching sets Matthew 8:22 under spiritual death. Men cut off from God because of sin are burying men whose spirit has left the body. Both are dead. Not the same death.

Colossians 2:13-14 — “And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses; Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;”

You, being dead in your sins. That is spiritual death. He quickened. Course 5 already named spiritual resurrection: new birth, in this life only. This teaching lists Colossians 2:14 here.

Hear the two blottings and do not merge them. Exodus 32: God blots the sinner out of His book. Colossians 2: He blots out the handwriting that was against us. One is a name removed. One is a debt removed.

1 Timothy 5:6 — “But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.”

Dead while she liveth. Physical life. Spiritual death. Pleasure did not raise her. Breathing did not raise her. She is cut off from Genesis 1:26-28 while she still spends.

Spiritual death is from God because of sin. It can be reversed in this life by new birth. Hebrews 9:27 and Revelation 22:11 already closed the window after death. You will not offer a second womb in hell.

Spiritual death is not the second death. Do not call every sinner “already in gehenna.” Do not call the lake “only a strong name for the old man.”

Charge of this section. Write Matthew 8:22, Colossians 2:14, and 1 Timothy 5:6. Who is dead while he lives? What blotting in Colossians 2 is not the blotting of Exodus 32? Why can this death be reversed now and not after death?

VII. THE SECOND DEATH — ETERNAL SEPARATION IN THE LAKE

The second death is the second and eternal separation from God in the lake of fire. It is not physical death repeated. It is not spiritual death prolonged as a mood. It is the lake.

Revelation 20:14 — “And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.”

The name is the lake. Hell is cast in. Hell is not the second death.

Revelation 2:11 — “He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.”

Same address-family as Revelation 3:5. Overcome. Not blotted. Not hurt of the second death.

Revelation 20:6 — “Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.”

Course 5’s companies. Second death hath no power. The rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished — Revelation 20:5. Then the throne. Then, if not written, the lake.

Revelation 21:8 — “But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.”

The list is not a metaphor for a bad decade. Three deaths stay three.

1. Physical — inner from outer. James 2:26.
2. Spiritual — from God because of sin. Matthew 8:22; Colossians 2:14; 1 Timothy 5:6.
3. Second — eternal separation in the lake. Revelation 20:14; 2:11; 20:6, 14; 21:8.

Give one text for each. Keep them. If the second death were annihilation, the persons would be gone. Revelation 20:10 keeps them: tormented day and night for ever and ever.

Charge of this section. Give one text for each of the three deaths. Write Revelation 20:14 and 21:8. What hath no power on the first resurrection? What will you not collapse?

VIII. SOUL AND SPIRIT IMMORTAL — BODIES RISE FROM DUST

The soul and spirit of man is immortal. All Scriptures on resurrection of the dead, without exception, refer to bodies which die and will be resurrected from dust again. You will not raise a soul from dust. The soul did not become dust. You will not kill the soul to make death tidier. Matthew 10:28 will forbid you under gehenna.

Daniel 12:2 — “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

The sleepers are bodies in dust. The awaking is bodily. Everlasting contempt is not a moment of shame and then nothing.

John 5:28-29 — “Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.”

All that are in the graves. Hear His voice. Come forth. Graves hold bodies. Two issues: resurrection of life; resurrection of damnation. Course 5 placed a thousand years between them. Revelation 20:4-6 and 20:11-15. You do not reopen chapter 10 of Revelation as that passage. Chapter 10 is the seven thunders and the little book. The two bodily issues are in Revelation chapter 20.

1 Corinthians 15:21-23 — “For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

Course 5 already named that coming as rapture 2, not the second advent. This chapter will not collapse them. Firstfruits of them that slept — slept as bodies.

1 Corinthians 15:44 — “It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.” The spiritual body is still a body. Luke 24:39: a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see Me have.

1 Corinthians 15:52-53 — “In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.”

Mortal is the body that can die. Immortality put on is the body raised. Soul and spirit were already immortal. The verse is not granting the soul a first existence.

1 Corinthians 15:19 stays with bodily hope, as Course 5 locked it. “If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.” If there is no resurrection of the dead, the hope is this-life only, and we are miserable. He is not defining new birth by that verse. He is proving the body.

1 Thessalonians 4:13-17 — “But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.”


This sits in the immortal-body file and also describes Company 2. Asleep is the body. Rise is the body. He brings them with Him, and their bodies rise.

Revelation 20:4-6 — “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.”


They lived — body, because resurrection language is bodily without exception. Lived not again is the second bodily issue after the Millennium.

Matthew 27:52-53 — “And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.”

Bodies of the saints. Course 5: those saints are right now in heaven with their bodies. There is not another Foundation School teaching. Section XI will empty Paradise of the righteous. Do not put these saints back into an underworld waiting-room. They have bodies. They are in heaven.

What then is raised from the dust? The body. What never dies as a person? Soul and spirit. What sleeps in the dust? The body. What comes forth from the graves? All that are in the graves. Two destinies. Life or damnation. Everlasting life or shame and everlasting contempt.

Charge of this section. What is raised from the dust? Write Daniel 12:2 and John 5:28-29. Write 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17. Why will you not treat soul and spirit as mortal? Where are the Matthew 27 saints now, and with what?

IX. FIVE PRISONS — NOT ONE IS THE GRAVE

There are five distinct prisons in the underworld of the departed. Not one is the same as the grave.

The grave holds the body. James 2:26 already split inner from outer. Call the grave any of the five and you have mixed dust with a prison.

The five:

1. Tartarus — fallen angels who sinned before the flood. No humans. No demons.
2. Paradise — once the abode of the righteous at death; now empty of the righteous.
3. Hell / sheol-hades — torment of the wicked until the end of the Millennium.
4. Abyss / Abaddon — demons and some angelic beings; Satan bound a thousand years.
5. Lake of fire = gehenna (G1067) — final, eternal, body and soul, after judgment.

None of these is the grave. You will write that until you cannot merge them.

Course 6 sits on Course 5’s map. Present age: righteous to heaven; wicked to hell. Tartarus already holds those angels. The abyss already holds what it holds; in the Millennium it holds Satan bound. After the Millennium: hell emptied, great white throne, lake. Tartarus, the abyss, and sheol-hades empty into gehenna.

Charge of this section. Name the five. For each, say it is not the grave. What does the grave hold? What do the five hold?

X. TARTARUS

Tartarus is a special prison for fallen angels who sinned before the flood. No human beings. No demons. The Greek of 2 Peter 2:4 is tartarōsas — cast them down to Tartarus. The King James reads hell there. You will keep the name Tartarus so you do not pour these angels into the rich man’s flame or into the lake before their time.

1 Peter 3:18-20 — “For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.”

The prison is tied to that disobedience in Noah’s days. The spirits in prison are not the eight souls in the ark. They are not the human dead of all ages. They are the disobedient of that wait.

2 Peter 2:4-5 — “For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;”

Cast them down to hell — tartarōsas. Chains of darkness. Reserved unto judgment. The next breath is the old world and Noah. They are not yet the lake.

Jude 6-7 — “And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.”

Sodom is the example of eternal fire, not a claim that Sodom’s men are in Tartarus. Tartarus is the chains of those angels until the great day.

No humans. You will not put the rich man here. You will not put Judas here as if Psalm 69 sent him to Tartarus. Judas is a man. Men of the wicked go to hell until the Millennium’s end.

No demons. Demons in this school’s abyss file beg not to go into the deep — Luke 8:31. That is not Tartarus. Do not pour Legion into 2 Peter 2:4 to make one underworld soup.

Who is here? Fallen angels who sinned before the flood. Who is not? Every human. Every demon. The righteous. The wicked dead of this age. Satan in the Millennium — he is in the abyss, not here.

Charge of this section. Write 1 Peter 3:19-20, 2 Peter 2:4, and Jude 6-7. What is tartarōsas? Who is in Tartarus? Who is not? What will you not merge with the rich man’s hell?

XI. PARADISE — NOW EMPTY OF THE RIGHTEOUS

Teach this as this school teaches it. Paradise held the righteous until Christ. It is now empty of the righteous. The righteous go to heaven at death. There is not another Foundation School teaching.

Luke 16:19-22 — “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;”

Luke 16:22 is in Paradise file. That was the righteous abode at physical death. Not the grave. The rich man is buried. Lazarus is carried.

Luke 16:23-26 — “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

Abraham’s bosom — comfort. Hell — torments, flame. A great gulf fixed. Course 1 used this narrative as Hell the consequence, and used Luke 16, not Matthew 16. You will not teach Matthew 16 as this narrative. Luke 16:27-31 remains Abraham’s refusal: Moses and the prophets already enough.

Luke 23:42-43 — “And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.”

To day. With Me. In paradise. You will not move “to day” into a later age. You will not make Paradise the grave. A grave is not “with Me.”

Ephesians 4:8-10 — “Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men. (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth? He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)”

He led captivity captive. He captured the captives. The righteous had been held against their will. He took them to heaven when He ascended. Paradise is now empty of the righteous.

Hebrews 2:14-15 — “Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.”

Held against their will. Delivered. Since that capture, the righteous go to heaven at death. Absent from the body, present with the Lord — 2 Corinthians 5:8. Depart, to be with Christ — Philippians 1:23.

The Matthew 27 saints are in heaven with their bodies. Do not contradict Course 5 to keep Paradise occupied. They are not in Abraham’s bosom under the earth.

Who was there? The righteous at death, until Christ. Who is there now among the righteous? None. Where do they go now? Heaven. Why? He captured the captives. The rich man was never there. He lift up his eyes in hell.

Charge of this section. Where do the righteous go at death now, and why? Write Luke 16:22, Luke 23:43, Ephesians 4:8, and Hebrews 2:15. Why is Paradise not the grave? Where are the Matthew 27 saints, and with what? What print error will you not repeat — Matthew 16 for this narrative?

XII. HELL / SHEOL-HADES

Hell is the torment compartment of sheol-hades. The wicked go there. They have always gone there, and they will always go there until the end of the Millennium. Then they are brought out, reunited with resurrected immortal bodies, and cast into the lake of fire for eternity. Revelation 20:11-15.

Hell as consequence was already Luke 16, not Matthew 16. Flame. Tongue. Gulf. Not Tartarus, not the abyss, not the lake yet, not Paradise, not the grave — he was buried, and he lift up his eyes.

You will not empty hell in this age because Christ led captivity captive. He led the righteous. He did not empty the flame.

Revelation 20:13-14 — “And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.”

Hell delivered up the dead which were in it. Then hell itself is cast into the lake. That is after the thousand years. Course 5: the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. Then bodies. Then the throne. Then the lake.

Until that hour the wicked dead are in hell without those bodies. Inner man in torment. Body in dust. Reunion with immortal bodies is not a kindness that undoes torment. It is the body joining the person for the last prison.

Do not flatten sheol-hades into unconsciousness. Luke 16 will not let you. Do not put first-resurrection companies here, nor the present righteous, nor Tartarus’s angels, nor Legion.

Who is here? Wicked souls, until the Millennium’s end. Who is not? The righteous now. The Matthew 27 saints. The companies that reign. Fallen angels of 2 Peter 2:4. Demons of Luke 8:31.

Charge of this section. Until when do the wicked go to hell? What happens to hell after the Millennium? Write Revelation 20:13-15. Write Luke 16:23-24 as this prison, not as Matthew 16, not as the lake. What does hell deliver up?

XIII. THE ABYSS / ABADDON

The abyss is the bottomless pit. Abaddon. Destruction. Abode of demons and some angelic beings. Not the grave. Not Tartarus. Not men’s hell. Not the lake yet.

Owner texts: Luke 8:31; Revelation 9; Revelation 20:3. Also Romans 10:7; Revelation 17:8; 20:1-10; Psalm 88:11, destruction.

The assigned reference listed 11:17 in the abyss list. You will not reopen 11:7 versus 11:17 as a question. Teach both addresses as the course already assigned them. The beast from the pit is Revelation 11:7 — Course 5, the two witnesses. Revelation 11:17 is the elders’ thanksgiving. Both stand. Neither is a riddle for this school to reopen.

Luke 8:30-31 — “And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him. And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.”

The deep is abyssos. The man had abode in the tombs — Luke 8:27. The tombs are not the deep. The grave is not this prison. Demons know the abyss as a place they fear to be sent.

Romans 10:6-7 — “But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)”

This teaching keeps Romans 10:7 in this lesson. You will not turn it into a claim that Christ is still in the pit. He is raised. You do not descend to fetch Him.

Revelation 9:1-2 — “And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit. And he opened the bottomless pit; and there arose a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit.”

Revelation 9 gives the assigned terms: key, pit, smoke, and locusts in 9:3.

Revelation 9:11 — “And they had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name Apollyon.”

Abaddon. Apollyon. The angel of the bottomless pit. The name sits on this prison.

Psalm 88:11 — “Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? or thy faithfulness in destruction?”

Destruction here is abaddon. Two words in one verse: grave, and destruction. Do not merge them.

Revelation 11:7 — “And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.”

Course 5: the beast from the pit kills the two witnesses. That is 11:7. Teach it there.

Revelation 11:16-17 — “And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.”

That is 11:17: elders’ thanksgiving. The print put 11:17 in the abyss list. Teach 11:7 as the beast from the pit — Course 5, two witnesses. Teach 11:17 as thanks. Do not ask which verse “really” belongs.

Revelation 17:8 — “The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition: and they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.”

The pit and the book sit in one verse. Perdition is the end, not the pit as last room.

Revelation 20:1-3 — “And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.”

Satan bound a thousand years in the pit. You will not bind him in Tartarus, in men’s hell, or in the grave.

Revelation 20:7 — “And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison,”

Revelation 20:10 — “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.”

The prison was the pit. Then the lake, where the beast and the false prophet already are — cast alive at the advent, Revelation 19:20. The abyss is not the last room. Gehenna is. range is 20:1-10. Teach the loosing and the lake. Do not invent a sixth prison for Gog and Magog.

Who is here? Demons. Some angelic beings. Satan for the thousand years. The beast in the sense of ascending from the pit. Who is not? The righteous. The wicked dead of sheol-hades as their ordinary abode. The pre-flood angels of Tartarus. Bodies in graves.

Charge of this section. Write Luke 8:31, Revelation 9:11, and Revelation 20:3. What is Abaddon in Psalm 88:11? Teach Revelation 11:7 and Revelation 11:17 as already assigned — beast from the pit; elders’ thanks. Do not reopen which number is “the” abyss verse. Where is Satan for a thousand years?

XIV. THE LAKE OF FIRE = GEHENNA (G1067)

The lake of fire is gehenna. Greek gehenna, G1067. Place of future and eternal torment. Found twelve times, always rendered hell. The same as the lake of fire, named five times: Revelation 19:20; 20:10-15; 21:8.

Not the grave. Body and soul. After judgment. Tartarus, the abyss, and sheol-hades empty into it. Eternal torment. People put in alive. Degrees. The worm does not die.

Luke 12:4-5 — “And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

Hell here is gehenna. After He hath killed. Power to cast into gehenna. Men can kill the body. They cannot finish the person. God only has power to put into gehenna. Matthew 10:28 says it with both parts: “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” Soul and body. Gehenna. Not the grave — the grave already has the body without needing God’s last cast.

Matthew 25:41 — “Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:”

Matthew 25:46 you already wrote: everlasting punishment. Life eternal. The fire prepared for the devil and his angels is this last prison. Men enter it. It was not prepared as a metaphor for earthly misery.

Revelation 14:9-11 you already wrote: fire and brimstone; smoke of torment for ever and ever; no rest day nor night. The lake-of-fire passage also sits 14:9-14. Verse 14 is the harvest. Keep torment. Do not let the cloud erase the smoke.

Revelation 19:20 — “And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.”

Cast alive. People put in alive. The beast and the false prophet do not wait for the great white throne to enter the lake. They go in at the advent. Revelation 20:10 finds them already there when the devil is cast in. After the Millennium the rest follow from the throne.

Revelation 20:10-15 you have in pieces. Devil cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are. Tormented day and night for ever and ever. Then the throne. Then the book. Then death and hell into the lake. Whosoever not written, into the lake. Bodies are not put there until the judgment — Revelation 20:11-15 — except those already cast alive, 19:20. Teach both. Do not use 19:20 to deny the throne. Do not use the throne to deny 19:20.

Revelation 21:8 you wrote: the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.

Revelation 22:15 — “For without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.”

Without. The last prison leaves a without. This is not the grave’s quiet.

Isaiah 66:22-24 again: worm shall not die; fire not quenched. Mark 9:43-44 — “And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” Mark 9:47-48 repeats the same fire and the same worm of the eye. The refrain is the doctrine.

Gehenna. Fire never quenched. Worm dieth not. Victory over sin is the escape — Matthew 5:29-30; 18:9; Revelation 21:8. People can repent and escape — Matthew 3:2-8; 23:33. That escape is in this life. Course 1. Not a second repentance after the throne.

Only certain people are in danger of it — Matthew 5:22; 23:15, 33. Only the wicked — Revelation 20:11-15; 21:8; Psalm 9:17. God only puts in. James 3:6: the tongue is set on fire of hell — gehenna can set on fire the course of nature.

Degrees of punishment: Revelation 20:13; Matthew 23:14-15, greater damnation. Degrees are not a ladder out, and not annihilation for the lighter. Eternal fire, damnation, punishment, judgment, contempt — Matthew 25:41, 46; Mark 3:29; 9:43-48; Hebrews 6:2; Jude 7; Revelation 14:9-11; Daniel 12:2. Weeping, wailing, gnashing of teeth — Matthew 8:12; 13:42, 50; 24:51.
