Matthew 8:12 — “But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” Matthew 13:42: furnace of fire; wailing and gnashing of teeth.

All the wicked in Tartarus (2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6-7), the abyss (Luke 8:31; Revelation 9; 20:3), and sheol-hades will be put into gehenna (Revelation 20:10-15). The five do not remain five forever as occupied rooms. Four empty into the last. Paradise already emptied of the righteous toward heaven. The last is eternal.

Who is here? Fallen angels, demons, and wicked men — the eternal hell and perdition of all of them. Beast and false prophet already. Devil after the last rebellion. Then the dead not found in the book of life. Who is not? The overcomer. Those who have part in the first resurrection. Anyone whose name is found written.

Charge of this section. What is G1067? Why is gehenna not the grave? Write Luke 12:5, Matthew 25:41 and 25:46, Revelation 19:20, and Revelation 20:10. Who is put in alive? What empties into it? What does the worm that does not die refuse?

XV. WHO IS WHERE

Write the map as a table in your mind until you can teach it without mixing rooms.

Present age, after the ascension.

The righteous who die — heaven. Paradise is empty of them. Absent from the body, present with the Lord. The Matthew 27 saints — heaven, and they have their bodies. Company 1 already.

The wicked who die — hell / sheol-hades. Torment. Until the end of the Millennium. Bodies still in dust.

Tartarus — fallen angels who sinned before the flood. Still reserved unto judgment. No humans. No demons.

The abyss — demons and some angels. Legion feared it. Abaddon. In the Millennium, Satan bound there a thousand years. The beast ascends from it — Revelation 11:7; 17:8.

The lake — not yet the ordinary abode of the wicked dead of this age. Exception already named: beast and false prophet cast alive at the second advent. The lake waits as the last room.

During the Millennium: first-resurrection companies reign; Satan in the pit; the wicked dead still in hell. After the Millennium: Satan loosed, then the lake, where the beast and the false prophet already are. Hell delivers up. Bodies raised. Great white throne. Book of life. Tartarus, the abyss, and sheol-hades empty into gehenna.

Righteous now: heaven. Wicked now: hell. Pre-flood angels: Tartarus. Demons and some angels: abyss; Satan there in the thousand years. Final: lake of fire, gehenna, second death. Grave: bodies, not a prison of this five. All without Christ are raised after the Millennium.

Charge of this section. For each of the five: who is there, who is not, what Scripture, what relation to the Millennium and the lake? Where do the righteous go at death now? Who is already in the lake before the great white throne?

XVI. THE CHARGE OF THE YEAR — BACK-LIST IS NOT A COURSE

This principle closes the foundation. It is not laid to produce fear as a product. It is laid so that a people will not treat judgment as a rumour.

No required companion is named for this course. Completing this chapter does not wait on a volume this school does not name at the point of teaching. Course 4 was the same: a further-reading mark with no title. Course 5 named Millennium. Course 6 names none. This school will not invent a book to fill a silence.

The old reference list named other titles. Faith Toward God and Resurrection of the Dead are not Year-1 courses by those book abbreviations. Those titles are not Year-1 courses. You will not promote a back-list title into a seventh principle. You will not make the year a shop of volumes. Directed reading later, if a volume is in your hand and a section is assigned. The $400 school does not grant those books as if they were Hebrews 6:1-2.

Fearfully Made is its own book. It is not Why We’re Beyond. Why We’re Beyond was named at baptisms / sonship. Fearfully Made sits on the back-list. Proximity on a page is bibliographic, not a merger.

Presence of Sons 1–4 is its own series. It is not Spirit Witness. Spirit Witness was named at baptisms. If a catalogue once set the titles near each other, that proximity is not a series assignment. You will not call Volume 5 of Presence of Sons a witness this teaching gave another title.

The old reference list includes other titles: Knowing (1 and 2), Makers, Thinking Eternity, He Hath Abounded Toward Us, Fearfully Made, Presence of Sons 1-4, Mind of Christ 1-3, Your Fellowship Your Meditation, The Christ, It Is Finished, The Noetic Church, Doctrine of Faith (Compendium), Doctrine of Man, and All Things Are Become New. Those titles may serve later directed reading, but historic contact lines on a source page are not Shop SKUs.

Doctrine of Man on page 5 does not make it Course 6. Thinking Eternity is not this chapter. Knowing is not a seventh stone. Week 52 is the final integration, not a seventh doctrine. The six remain the six. You leave them when they are laid, if God permit. You do not leave them by renaming a back-list.

Charge 37. Whom does “whosoever” refuse to exempt? Revelation 20:15. Acts 10:34. God is no respecter of persons.

Charge 38. God blots names of sinners. Teach Exodus 32:32-33, Psalm 69:20-28 predicted of Judas, and Revelation 3:5 as one Scripture set. Add John 3:36 and Revelation 22:18-19.

Charge 39. Dead means cut off from realizing Genesis 1:26-28. Define death without using only “stopped breathing.” Teach Genesis as written. Image. Likeness. Dominion. Keep the translation note where it belongs, but teach the doctrine from Scripture.

Charge 40. Three kinds of death. One text each. Physical: James 2:26. Spiritual: Matthew 8:22; Colossians 2:14; 1 Timothy 5:6. Second: Revelation 20:14; 2:11; 20:6, 14; 21:8. Do not collapse them.

Charge 41. Soul and spirit immortal. Resurrection is of bodies from dust. Daniel 12:2; John 5:28-29; 1 Corinthians 15; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-17; Revelation 20:4-6, 11-15. What is raised from the dust? The body.

Charge 42. Five prisons. Not one is the grave. For each: who is there, who is not, what Scripture, what relation to the Millennium and the lake.

Charge 43. Paradise now empty. The righteous go to heaven at death now, because Christ captured the captives. Luke 16:22; Luke 23:43; Ephesians 4:8; Hebrews 2:15. Matthew 27 saints in heaven with their bodies. Do not contradict Course 5.

Write also what this chapter locked at the first stone of duration. Matthew 25:46 — eternal punishment. Revelation 14:9-11. Revelation 20:11-15. Isaiah 66:22-24. Eternal is duration. Not metaphor. Not annihilation.

Write the map Course 5 already gave you, and do not redraw it. Present age: righteous to heaven; wicked to hell. After the Millennium: hell emptied; great white throne; lake. Rapture 2 is not the second advent. The two bodily issues are a thousand years apart in Revelation chapter 20, not in chapter 10.

Do not treat judgment as spectacle or as denial. Do not treat Hell-avoidance as Course 1’s repentance. Do not treat the lake as a metaphor, the soul as mortal, or the grave as one of the five. Do not put humans or demons in Tartarus. Do not keep the righteous in Paradise. Do not empty hell before the Millennium’s end. Do not reopen 11:7 and 11:17 as a dispute. Do not make the back-list into Year-1 courses. Do not merge Fearfully Made with Why We’re Beyond, or Presence of Sons 1–4 with Spirit Witness.

The principle closes the six. It is not a product of fear. Lay it where Hebrews laid it. Then go on. If God permit.

lessons.title: Truth before conclusion
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The investigation begins with truth itself before it asks the reader to accept a theological conclusion.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 1–3.

Word drill
1. Distinguish truth, belief, assertion, opinion, convention, and error.
2. State the difference between what is actually the case and a person's acceptance of a proposition.
3. Explain why sincerity and repetition do not create truth.
4. Write the governing movement: Truth → Reality → Knowledge → Evidence → Warrant.

Assessment
Give a one-page account of a claim, its supporting evidence, and the distinction between believing it and establishing it.

lessons.title: Knowledge, evidence, and rational warrant
lessons.body:
Central proposition
A warranted conclusion requires more than assertion. Knowledge, evidence, testimony, inference, and rational warrant must be distinguished.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 4–6.

Word drill
1. Define evidence and testimony in the terms of the investigation.
2. Distinguish evidence from the authority of the conclusion it supports.
3. Trace evidence → analysis → inference → conclusion.
4. Identify one conclusion that would be stronger than its evidence permits.

Assessment
Build one Claim → Definition → Evidence → Analysis → Inference → Conclusion chain without importing an unsupported premise.

lessons.title: Reasonability and ultimate authority
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Reason and sound judgment are required for examining claims, but reason itself cannot simply be assumed to be the final authority when competing claims exist.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 7–8. Isaiah 1:18.

Word drill
1. Explain what Isaiah 1:18 contributes to the investigation.
2. Distinguish reason as an instrument of judgment from an asserted ultimate court.
3. State the problem of ultimate authority in one paragraph.
4. Name the question that must be answered before later claims about Scripture can function as conclusions.

Assessment
Defend why the course begins by establishing the question of authority rather than merely declaring the answer.

lessons.title: God, truth, and revelation
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The investigation moves from truth to its ultimate ground, then asks how God is known without replacing revelation with speculation.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 9–14.

Word drill
1. Distinguish the ontological, epistemological, evidential, and hermeneutical questions.
2. State what the manuscript establishes about God as truthful, faithful, immutable, and incapable of lying.
3. Distinguish revelation from human commentary about revelation.
4. Explain why human accounts about God must themselves be tested.

Assessment
Produce a structured summary that separates what is established by the biblical record from what a commentator merely says about it.

lessons.title: What kind of record is the Bible?
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Before calling the Bible an authoritative revelation, the investigation establishes what kind of written record it is and what kinds of testimony it contains.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 15–19.

Word drill
1. Describe the Bible as a body of writings and historical testimony.
2. Distinguish direct eyewitness testimony from received or investigated testimony.
3. Identify the kinds of claims the biblical record makes about its own origin.
4. Explain why historical claims must be treated as claims capable of evidential examination.

Assessment
Write a two-page evidence map: record → source of testimony → claim → possible examination.

lessons.title: Graphē, Holy Writ, and Scripture
lessons.body:
Central proposition
γραφή (graphē, G1124) names writing and, in biblical usage, Scripture/Holy Writ. The course must distinguish the written authority from books written about it.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 20–22. John 10:35.

Word drill
1. Define γραφή (graphē) from the manuscript's lexical and biblical treatment.
2. Keep these designations related without flattening them: graphē · Holy Writ · Scripture · Bible · written Word.
3. Explain why this course is not Holy Writ.
4. State what is meant by written authority.

Assessment
Defend the distinction: the Graphē is the authoritative written record; the Aletheia book and course are subordinate works that study it.

lessons.title: How revelation reaches written testimony
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The manuscript traces divine communication through speech, angels, prophets, Christ, apostles, visions, dreams, revelation, inspiration, and written testimony.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 23–32.

Word drill
1. Name the major modes of divine communication examined in the movement.
2. Distinguish revelation, reception, witness, recording, and transmission.
3. Explain the significance of 2 Timothy 3:15–17 and the phrase “all Scripture.”
4. State why the written record cannot be treated as a loose collection of human impressions.

Assessment
Draw the chain from divine communication to written testimony and explain every transition without collapsing distinct categories.

lessons.title: Authentication: evidence to warrant
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The claim that the biblical record is authentic must be reasoned through cumulative evidence rather than asserted because the record says so.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 33–42.

Word drill
1. Define authentication.
2. Distinguish eyewitness evidence, miracles, prophecy, unity, external corroboration, transmission, and cumulative convergence.
3. Explain why one isolated argument is not the whole case.
4. Trace evidence → rational warrant without circularly assuming the conclusion.

Assessment
Build a cumulative evidential outline and mark every place where an inference is stronger than the evidence.

lessons.title: Christ as historical and apostolic witness
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Jesus Christ is examined first as a historical figure and central witness before the argument moves to His theological significance and treatment of Scripture.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 43–47.

Word drill
1. Separate historical claims about Christ from later conclusions about Christ.
2. Identify the role of apostolic testimony.
3. Explain why eyewitness testimony matters to the evidential case.
4. State what must be established before Christ can function as the decisive witness in the argument.

Assessment
Write a concise historical-evidential brief on Christ using only claims established by the assigned chapters.

lessons.title: Christ, Scripture, and apostolic authority
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Christ's relationship to Scripture and the apostles is central to the authority argument, but the course must not confuse apostolic testimony with every later interpretation of it.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 48–50.

Word drill
1. Identify ways Christ received, quoted, interpreted, and appealed to Scripture.
2. Distinguish Christ's confirmation of Scripture from later doctrinal systems.
3. Explain the evidential role of apostolic testimony concerning Christ.
4. State why apostolic authority matters to the New Testament witness.

Assessment
Defend the distinction between Christ's treatment of the written record and an interpreter's claim about Christ's treatment of it.

lessons.title: Canon, inspiration, and infallibility
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Canon, prophetic and apostolic authority, revelation, inspiration, and infallibility are related but distinct questions.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 51–58.

Word drill
1. Distinguish the scriptural corpus from the process of canon recognition.
2. Distinguish revelation, inspiration, and canon.
3. Explain what the manuscript argues inspiration guarantees.
4. Trace the premises leading toward the infallibility of the written record.

Assessment
Create a four-column distinction table: Revelation | Inspiration | Canon | Infallibility.

lessons.title: The scripture cannot be broken
lessons.body:
Central proposition
John 10:34–36 must be read as an argument. Christ's appeal to what is written culminates in the statement that the scripture cannot be broken.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 59–65. John 10:34–36; Psalm 82:6; John 17:17.

Word drill
1. Read John 10:34–36 as a complete argumentative unit.
2. Examine Christ's citation of Psalm 82:6 in context.
3. Explain what “the scripture cannot be broken” contributes to the argument.
4. Connect John 17:17 — “thy word is truth” — to the established authority argument.

Assessment
Write the reasoning chain that earns the conclusion that the Graphē is the primary written authority. Do not state the conclusion as a premise.

lessons.title: Text, interpretation, and secondary authorities
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Scriptural authority does not make every human interpretation of Scripture authoritative. The text and the interpreter must remain distinct.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 66–70.

Word drill
1. Distinguish the authority of the text from the fallibility of the interpreter.
2. Identify how perception, context, inference, tradition, philosophy, institution, and experience can distort handling.
3. Explain when a secondary source becomes a primary authority.
4. State why a course, teacher, commentary, or tradition must remain under the Graphē.

Assessment
Take one interpretation and separate: biblical text | inference | synthesis | pedagogical method | institutional claim.

lessons.title: Turning aside, accepted heresies, and unskillfulness
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The manuscript diagnoses doctrinal turning aside, accepted heresies, aridity, and unskillfulness as failures that can occur among people who possess Scripture.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 71–73. Hebrews 5:11–14.

Word drill
1. Explain how erroneous teaching can become normalized without becoming true.
2. Define aridity as the manuscript uses the term; do not turn it into a generic emotional “dry season.”
3. Define ἄπειρος (apeiros) as unskillfulness/inexperience in the word of righteousness.
4. Connect unskillfulness to the Hebrews diagnosis without inventing extra marks.

Assessment
Defend the distinction between possessing Scripture, quoting Scripture, understanding Scripture, and being skilled in the word of righteousness.

lessons.title: Scholarly labour: from perception to rightly dividing
lessons.body:
Central proposition
The final movement turns authority into disciplined labour: perception, learning, understanding, reasoning, quotation, knowledge, diligence, exercise, maturity, skill, and rightly dividing.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapters 74–84. 2 Timothy 2:15.

Word drill
1. Trace perception → learning → understanding → reasoning → knowledge.
2. Explain why quotation is not ignorance and why quotation alone is not complete understanding.
3. Define σπουδάζω (spoudazō, G4704) in its range of diligence, endeavour, labour, and study.
4. Explain the approved workman and rightly dividing the word of truth.
5. Identify the disciplines required for responsible biblical interpretation.

Assessment
Produce a written study showing the full labour chain on one biblical passage, clearly separating text, observation, inference, and conclusion.

lessons.title: Capstone — Graphē as Gate, not seventh principle
lessons.body:
Central proposition
Chapter 85 closes the canonical Work by showing why the Doctrine of the Graphē prepares the learner for the Six First Principles without becoming a seventh principle.

Reference
One Source of Truth, Chapter 85, with review of Chapters 65, 66, 73, and 82–84.

Word drill
1. State the conclusion that the Graphē is the primary written authority without making this book or course Holy Writ.
2. Explain the difference between a canonical Work, a course, a handbook, and a first principle.
3. Name the six first principles in Hebrews 6:1–2.
4. Explain the sequence: Graphē → Doctrine of the Graphē → Preparation → Readiness → Six First Principles.
5. Defend why the Graphē Gate is not a seventh first principle.

Assessment
Final written defense required: establish the authority argument, preserve the Book/Course distinction, and explain why the learner is now ready to enter the Six First Principles.

lessons.title: The graphē: primary authority for hearing and growth
lessons.body:
Central principle
Holy Writ — the graphē — is the primary authority for hearing from God and for spiritual growth. Foundation School rests on the writing, not on religious imitation.

Key Scripture
John 10:35 — the scripture cannot be broken.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, sections I–II.

Teaching
Holy Writ is writings or sayings of unchallenged, unquestionable authority. The Lord Jesus answered a charge of blasphemy by appeal to that which was written. He would not let men set His person against the Scripture.

John 10:34-36 — “Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?”

The writing He cites is Psalm 82:6 — “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Course 2 will open that psalm with verse 7 and with this same appeal. Here the point is narrower and it will stay narrower: the Lord rests His answer on the graphē. The school rests where He rested. You do not get private authority because you are sincere. You do not get a safer Bible because an organization is old.

Holy Writ is unchallenged authority, whether for persons, organizations, governments, or nations. Graphē is not a mood that accompanies a meeting. It is the writing. If you will hear from God in this year, you will hear Him where He has spoken.

A Christian life shaped by Scripture follows the teachings of Jesus Christ and bears His qualities and spirit. It conforms to the sincerity and truth the graphē commands. The opposite is a religious substitute that imitates the vocabulary of faith while refusing to sit under the text. That substitute can use the vocabulary. It can fill a room. But it will not be judged by the writing. Foundation School will not trade the graphē for that substitute.

The graphē is the primary authority for hearing from God and for growth. The leaflet, textbook, and course serve the Scripture; they do not replace it. Over the ages the design of God for Christian life has rested in conformity with that writing. This book and this course give focused teaching on the essential cornerstone of Christianity: the first principles of the oracles of God (Hebrews 5:12). They open the foundation; they do not replace the writing.

Growth under that convention is two movements, not one slogan: first principles, then maturity — perfection. You do not skip the foundation to appear mature. You do not lay the foundation again every year as a lifestyle and call that growth. Hebrews 6:1 says we do not lay again the foundation once it is laid. We go on.

The cover of the textbook may say Truth · Knowledge · Maturity. That line belongs to the book. The house that holds the book is Aletheia: Truth · Identity · Dominion. Do not confuse the two. This course is the first stone of the first movement. You will not be asked to invent a more convenient Bible.

Sit the charge. John 10:31-33 — “Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him. Jesus answered them, Many good works have I shewed you from my Father; for which of those works do ye stone me? The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.” He does not answer with a substitute. He answers with “Is it not written.” Graphē is the court He will stand in.

The graphē carries the unchallenged authority. Persons are under it. Organizations are under it. Governments and nations are under it. You do not outrank the writing by office. You do not outrank it by sincerity. You do not outrank it by a year of enrolment. If a teaching will not sit down under John 10:35, it is religious imitation, however Christian the vocabulary.

Under the graphē, growth is first principles, then maturity. Hebrews 5:12 already waits in the next lesson: the first principles of the oracles of God. This book is not a second Bible. It opens what is already written. If you treat the textbook as the primary authority, you have already left the writing. If you treat the graphē as a collection of slogans, you have already taken up the substitute.

Write this week as a student under the writing. Name the religious substitute you have treated as if it were Scripture. Name the verse you will continue in. Do not name a verse you will not open.

Labour
This is the page-work. The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same. The hours differ. The oracles do not.

The Walk — one page. Quote John 10:34-36 in full. Name what charge the Lord was answering. Name what writing He appealed to (Psalm 82:6). Then write, in your own hand, that the graphē — not a leaflet, guide, or course — is the primary authority for hearing from God and for growth, and what “the scripture cannot be broken” forbids you to do with a religious substitute for faith.

Intensive — three pages on that same Scripture set. Page 1 is The Walk page. Page 2: sit John 10:34-36 in its chapter — the Jews take up stones; they say He, being a man, maketh Himself God; He answers from the writing. Do not import Course 2’s later use of Psalm 82:7 here. Page 3: teach as if you had to teach it clearly to another student: the graphē is the primary authority; first principles, then maturity; this book opens the cornerstone, it is not a second Bible.

Write in your own hand. Quote the governing verses in full. Name graphē: Holy Writ, the Bible, Scripture. Draw the distinction: writing versus religious imitation. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Scripture is not religious imitation. The school does not invent a more convenient Bible. The textbook is not the primary authority; the graphē is.

Charge
Write what you will teach: Holy Writ carries unchallenged authority and is the primary authority for hearing and growth; the Lord answered blasphemy by the writing; a religious substitute will not sit down under the text; growth is first principles, then maturity. Then complete the practice assignment. Name one place you have treated a substitute as if it were the graphē, and the verse you will continue in this week.

lessons.title: Hebrews 5:11–12 — you ought to be teachers
lessons.body:
Central principle
There is a time when you ought to be teachers. Milk after that time is a recession, not a kindness.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 5:11-12.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, sections III and X.

Teaching
The writer had hard things to utter concerning the Son. He could not, because they were dull of hearing. The fault was not in the doctrine. The fault was in the ear.

Hebrews 5:11-14 — “Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing. For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat. For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.”

Mark the time. They had been under the word long enough that they ought to be teachers. They had become such as need milk. Become is a direction. A people can recede. Milk is not an insult to a newborn. Milk is an indictment to a man who has had years to grow. Strong meat is for those of full age. The first principles are not a lesser gospel. They are the foundation that makes meat possible.

Hebrews 6:1-2 names the six: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.” Leaving them does not mean forgetting them. It means they are laid, and you go on to perfection. A man who has never laid them is not “leaving” them. He is skipping them.

Hebrews 6:3 — “And this will we do, if God permit.” After the six are named, we go on to perfection if God permit. That is a short hinge, not a seventh course. The writer does not treat maturity as a human schedule you can force. He treats it as a work we intend, under permission. You may enrol in fifty-two weeks. You cannot enrol God. Walk the year as labour. Ask for permission to go on. Do not call unfinished foundations “perfection.”

Foundation School exists because the oracles have a beginning that must be known, distinguished, reasoned, and taught. If you cannot teach repentance from dead works from the Scriptures, you are not ready to speak as if you were past it.

Hear the “of whom.” Hebrews 5:10 has just named Melchisedec. The hard things concern the Son after that order. The writer is not withholding milk because he is unkind. He is unable to utter meat because the ear is dull. Dullness is not a quiet temperament. It is an ear that has had time and has receded.

“Teach you again” is the indictment. The oracles were already given. They need to be taught again because they were not laid. Milk after years is not patience. It is “become.” A people can move backward while they keep the meetings.

Hebrews 6:1-2 will not let you merge the six. Repentance from dead works is not faith toward God. Baptisms are not hands. Resurrection is not eternal judgment. You do not skip the first stone because you have heard the sixth named. You do not call unfinished foundations “perfection” because you have enrolled for fifty-two weeks.

Hebrews 6:3 remains the hinge: “And this will we do, if God permit.” Permission is not fatalism. It is dependence. You labour. You ask. You do not enrol God. If you cannot yet teach this first principle from the Scriptures, you are still in 5:12 — needing to be taught again — and you will not pretend you have left the principles.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Hebrews 5:12 in your own hand. Reason “ought to be teachers,” “teach you again,” “become,” and “milk” in that one verse. Name the time you have already had under the word. Do not write a general confession.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Hebrews 5:11-14 in full, then Hebrews 6:1-3 in full. Show how “leaving” in 6:1 is not forgetting, and how 6:3 is dependence, not a seventh principle. Page 3: teach these passages as if you had to teach it clearly to another student — dull hearing, recession, the six named, if God permit.

Write in your own hand. Quote Hebrews 5:11-14 and 6:1-3 listed in the practice assignment. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Leaving the first principles (Hebrews 6:1) is not forgetting them. It is not laying them again once they are laid. A man who never laid them is not leaving them. He is skipping them.

Charge
Write what you will teach: there is a time when a hearer ought to be a teacher; milk after that time is a recession; the six are named; we go on if God permit. Then complete the practice assignment. Where are you still a hearer who must be taught the oracles again?

lessons.title: Apeiros — unskilled in the word of righteousness
lessons.body:
Central principle
Unskill here is inexperience in the word of righteousness, not lack of church activity.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 5:13 — every one that useth milk is unskilful (apeiros) in the word of righteousness.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, section IV.

Teaching
Hebrews 5:13 — “For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.”

Unskilful is Greek apeiros: inexperienced, that is, ignorant — unskilful. The inexperience is not in crowding a meeting. It is in the word of righteousness. The verse will not let you hide unskill behind a calendar of services. A man may be present every week and still be apeiros. An organization may be age-old and still be apeiros.

Hear the severity: when sound judgment is absent and unskill remains, dryness and doctrinal shifting appear among persons and even among age-old organizations that appear Christianized. What follows can be damnable heresies accepted as doctrines. That sentence is not an insult to make the lesson longer. It is a diagnosis of what unskill breeds. Dryness appears where the word should have been. Doctrinal shifting appears when a people will not sit down under the text and therefore cannot stay with a doctrine.

That lack of skill is blamed on failure to take Scripture seriously enough to know it and align with it. A digital Bible or a printed Bible does not help if there is no labour. The cure is not a louder room. The cure is labour in the word.

Hebrews 5:14 remains in these passages: “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” Full age is not years since enrolment. It is senses exercised by use. Use is labour. You will not become skilful by collecting headings. You become skilful by holding the word of righteousness until you can discern.

The Word is the basis for salvation. If you are unskilled there, you are unskilled at the root. This lesson aims at productive, godly living shaped by skill in the word of righteousness, not by slogans.

Hebrews 5:12 has already said they have need that one teach them again which be the first principles of the oracles of God. 5:13 names what that need is: unskilful in the word of righteousness. Apeiros is not “new to the building.” It is inexperience in that word. The word of righteousness is not a topic among topics. It is the word by which a man is aligned, or by which he is left arid.

The chain is severe and it is exact. Absence of sound judgment plus presence of unskilfulness produces dryness and doctrinal shifting. Dryness is a people empty of the oracles while they still speak Christian language. Doctrinal shifting is a people who will not stay with a doctrine because they never knew the Scriptures that would have held them. Damnable accepted heresies called doctrines follow that unskill. An age-old organization can wear the name and still be that chain.

Format is not the issue. A man with a phone full of Bibles can be ἄπειρος (apeiros), unskilled. A man with a worn printed Bible and no labour can be ἄπειρος (apeiros), unskilled. The serious study Scripture requires is not the same as a degree. It is knowing what is written and aligning with it. The cure is labour in the word. The next lessons will name that labour spoudazō and word drill. This lesson will not let you substitute a crowded room for that labour.

Name the hour. Name the text. If you cannot, you are not yet a workman, however present you have been.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Hebrews 5:13. Define apeiros: inexperienced, ignorant, unskilful — in the word of righteousness. Then name your actual study labour this week: the hour and the text. If you cannot name it, you are not yet a workman. Do not name a meeting in the place of labour.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Hebrews 5:12-14 in full. Show how “milk,” “unskilful,” “babe,” and “senses exercised” sit in one stretch. Reason why a crowded room can still be apeiros. Page 3: teach what Foundation School blames — failure to know the Scriptures and to align — and what it will not accept as a cure. Write the teaching as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote Hebrews 5:13. Define apeiros. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Skill is not performance. A crowded room can still be apeiros.

Charge
Write what you will teach: apeiros is unskill in the word of righteousness; the blame is failure to know the Scriptures and to align; the cure is labour, not a louder room. Then complete the practice assignment. Name the hour and the text.

lessons.title: Nēpios — two marks of babes
lessons.body:
Central principle
A babe is dull of hearing and unskilled in the Word, which is the basis for salvation.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 5:11 and 5:13.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, section V.

Teaching
Hebrews 5:11 — “Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.” Hebrews 5:13 — “For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.”

The same verse that names the milk-user unskilful also names him a babe: Greek nēpios — implying negation; figuratively a simple-minded person, an immature Christian: babe, child. Do not take “babe” as a term of endearment in this chapter. It is a diagnosis. A babe may be sincere and still be apeiros. An organization may be old and still be nēpios. Sincerity does not cancel the two marks. Age of an assembly does not cancel the two marks.

Two characteristics of babes:

1. Dull of hearing (Hebrews 5:11).
2. Unskilled in the Word, which is the basis for salvation.

Hold the two marks as two. Dullness of hearing is the ear that will not take in what is hard to be uttered. Unskill is inexperience in the word of righteousness. A man may hear often and still be dull. A man may quote often and still be unskilled. The writer could not utter the hard things concerning the Son because of the ear, not because the meat was lacking.

Hebrews 5:14 sets the other man: “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” Babe versus teacher is not a personality contrast. It is milk versus meat, dullness versus an exercised sense, unskill versus discernment. The Word is the basis for salvation. Unskill there is unskill at the root.

This lesson aims at productive, godly living shaped by skill in the word of righteousness, not by slogans. You will not become a teacher by remaining a babe who enjoys being called a babe.

Hold Hebrews 5:11 and 5:13 as the two marks, not as two nicknames. Dull of hearing is the ear that cannot take what is hard to be uttered concerning the Son. Unskilled in the Word is apeiros in the word of righteousness. The Word is the basis for salvation. Unskill there is unskill at the root. You may be sincere in both marks. Sincerity does not cancel them.

Nēpios implies negation: a simple-minded person, an immature Christian — babe, child. In other rooms “babe” is affection. In this chapter it is a diagnosis. An organization may be old and still be nēpios. A man may be earnest and still be nēpios. Do not take the word as endearment and then refuse the two marks.

Hebrews 5:14 is the other man in the same stretch: strong meat belongs to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. Full age is not the date of your first meeting. It is use. Senses exercised. Discernment. Babe versus that man is milk versus meat. You will not become the second by remaining pleased to be called the first.

Name your dullness. Name the place of your unskill. Write the place, not a general confession. The diagnosis is useless if you will not locate it.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write the two marks, each with its verse. Name your dullness of hearing. Name where you are apeiros in the word of righteousness. Do not write a general confession. Write the place.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Hebrews 5:11-14 in full. Define nēpios. Show why “babe” is a diagnosis and not an endearment. Page 3: teach babe versus the man of full age whose senses are exercised. Write the teaching as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote the two marks with their verses. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Babe vs teacher whose senses are exercised to discern both good and evil (Hebrews 5:14).

Charge
Write what you will teach: nēpios is a diagnosis; the two marks are dull of hearing and unskilled in the Word; the Word is the basis for salvation. Then complete the practice assignment. Name the place of your dullness and the place of your unskill.

lessons.title: Spoudazō and 2 Timothy 2:15
lessons.body:
Central principle
Study is labour. Approval here is the approval of a workman who rightly divides the word of truth.

Key Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, section VI.

Teaching
2 Timothy 2:15 — “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.”

The Greek behind that study is spoudazō: to use speed, to make effort, be prompt or earnest; do diligence, be diligent, endeavour, labour, study — intellectually. Speed here is not haste that skips context. It is earnestness that will not postpone the labour. You do not “study” by collecting quotations you cannot reason. You study by sitting under the word of truth until you can divide it rightly.

Read the verse in its stretch. 2 Timothy 2:3-4 — “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” 2 Timothy 2:8-9 — “Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.” 2 Timothy 2:13 — “If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.” 2 Timothy 2:14 — “Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.”

Then 2:15. Approval before God in this verse is the approval of a workman. The work is the word of truth, rightly divided. Shame here is the shame of a workman who cannot divide the word. 2 Timothy 2:16 follows: “But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” Right division is not a hobby of phrases. It is the labour that refuses babbling.

If you will walk this year at three hours a week or at eight, the difference is not a second doctrine. The difference is how much labour you put on the same oracles. The Walk and The Intensive are the same teaching. The hours differ. The oracles do not.

2 Timothy 2:15 does not sit in a vacuum of study tips. The man addressed is to endure hardness as a good soldier. He is not to entangle himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier. He is to remember Jesus Christ of the seed of David, raised from the dead. The word of God is not bound though the apostle is in bonds. He is to charge them that they strive not about words to no profit, to the subverting of the hearers. Then: study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

Spoudazō is speed, effort, promptness, earnestness; diligence, endeavour, labour, study — intellectually. Speed is earnestness that will not postpone. It is not haste that skips context and calls the skip “faith.” Approval is a workman’s approval. Shame is a workman’s shame — the man who cannot divide the word. Rightly dividing is the work. Profane and vain babblings increase unto more ungodliness (2 Timothy 2:16). Collecting quotations you cannot reason is nearer babbling than labour.

The Walk is about three hours a week. Intensive is about eight. Same oracles. The doctrine is the same. Same 2 Timothy 2:15. The difference is hours on the same work. You will not invent a second teaching for the longer week. You will put more labour on this verse until “approved,” “workman,” and “rightly dividing” can be reasoned without a slogan.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page — a word drill. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Do a word drill on 2 Timothy 2:15 until you can reason “study,” “approved,” “workman,” “ashamed,” and “rightly dividing” without a slogan. Write the verse. Then write six sentences, one for each of those five words and one for the soldier-context that sits before the verse.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that word-drill page. Page 2: write 2 Timothy 2:3-15 as a stretch. Show how the soldier, the bonds, the charge not to strive about words to no profit, and the workman sit together. Page 3: teach spoudazō — speed, effort, promptness, earnestness, diligence, labour, study, intellectually — and teach what speed is not. Write the teaching as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote 2 Timothy 2:15. Reason the five words. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Study as labour vs study as collecting quotations.

Charge
Write what you will teach: spoudazō is labour; approval is a workman’s approval; right division is the work; The Walk and The Intensive share one doctrine. Then complete the practice assignment. Do not submit a list of books you have not opened.

lessons.title: Knowledge: perception, learning, reasoning
lessons.body:
Central principle
Knowledge is a mental result of perception and learning and reasoning. The practice is word exercise, word drill.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 5:14 — senses exercised to discern.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, section VII.

Teaching
Knowledge is a mental result of perception, learning, and reasoning. The practice is named: word exercise, word drill. That is not a seminary extra. It is how Foundation School will ask you to know.

Perception: you see what the text says, not what you wish it said. Learning: you take it in, and you keep it. Reasoning: you can hold a set of Scriptures together and draw the distinction the text itself makes.

A man may quote a verse and still be a babe. Quotation without reasoning is not skill. Hebrews 5:13-14 — “For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” The man of full age has senses exercised by use. Use is the drill. Discernment is the fruit. You do not skip perception and call your opinion reasoning. You do not skip learning and call a memory of a heading knowledge.

2 Timothy 2:15 remains in these passages: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Right division is reasoning under the text. The questions Foundation School asks are charges, not decorations. Foundation School asks questions. You will answer them from these passages, not from a remembered heading.

Take Hebrews 5:12 as the drill this lesson will not let you postpone: “For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.” Perceive it — what it says. Learn it — write it. Reason it — why “ought to be teachers” and “become” belong in one verse. If you can only recite the verse, you have not yet done the drill.

This lesson will not let knowledge be a pile of headings. Perception sees what the text says. If you see what you wish it said, you have not perceived. Learning takes it in and keeps it. If you heard it and cannot write it, you have not learned it. Reasoning holds a set of Scriptures and draws the distinction the text itself makes. If you can only recite one verse and cannot hold it with its neighbours, you have not reasoned.

Hebrews 5:12 is the drill because it contains the indictment and the direction in one sentence. “For the time” names what you have already had. “Ought to be teachers” names what that time required. “Teach you again” names recession. “First principles of the oracles of God” names what must be known. “Become such as have need of milk” names the direction backward. Perceive that order. Learn it by writing it. Reason why “ought” and “become” belong together: a people can have time enough to teach and still become babes.

2 Timothy 2:15 remains: a workman, rightly dividing. Right division is this reasoning under the text. The questions Foundation School asks are charges. You will not decorate a page with them and then refuse to answer. Word exercise, word drill — that is the practice. A man may quote and still be a babe. Do the drill until you can reason Hebrews 5:12, not only recite it.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page — the word drill on Hebrews 5:12. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Hebrews 5:12. Then three short movements on that one verse: perceive (what it says, in order); learn (write it again without looking, then check); reason (why “ought,” “again,” and “become” sit together). Do not add a second verse until that page is done.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that drill on Hebrews 5:12. Page 2: write Hebrews 5:13-14 and 2 Timothy 2:15. Show how perception, learning, and reasoning are that mental result, and how “senses exercised” and “rightly dividing” are the same labour under two addresses. Page 3: teach knowledge versus information collected. Write the teaching as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Perceive, learn, reason — on the page. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Knowledge vs information collected.

Charge
Write what you will teach: knowledge is perception, learning, and reasoning; the practice is word drill; quotation without reasoning is not skill. Then complete the practice assignment. Do the drill on Hebrews 5:12 until you can reason it, not only recite it.

lessons.title: John 8:32 — truth makes free
lessons.body:
Central principle
Truth makes free where you continue in His word. This is not a motto for the cover.

Key Scripture
John 8:31-36.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 1, section VIII.

Teaching
John 8:31-36 — “Then said Jesus to those Jews which believed on him, If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free? Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever. If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.”

Read the verse in its place. Freedom here is not a political cry and not a mood. It is the freedom of those who continue in His word and know the truth. The Lord sets that freedom over against being the servant of sin. They claimed Abraham and denied bondage. He named sin as the master. The Son makes free. Continuance in His word is the path He named to knowing the truth.

The opening of this book is therefore not a motto. Truth makes free where the word is continued in. Dull hearing will not get you that freedom. Unskill in the word of righteousness will not get you that freedom. Hebrews 5:11-14 remains in these passages: they were dull of hearing; they had become such as have need of milk; every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness; strong meat belongs to those who by reason of use have their senses exercised. A man who will not continue in the word will not know the truth that makes free. A man who continues only as a babe — quoting, not reasoning — has not yet used the word unto discernment.

You will not treat John 8:32 as a cover line and then refuse John 8:31 and 8:34-36. Disciples indeed are those who continue. Servants of sin are those who commit sin. Free indeed is the Son’s doing. The graphē you opened in lesson 1 is the word you continue in here.

They answered from Abraham and from a claimed freedom: “We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man.” The Lord did not accept the claim. Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. The servant abideth not in the house for ever. The Son abideth ever. If the Son shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed. In these passages, freedom is the Son’s work against the servitude of sin. It is not a cry against Rome. It is not a mood after a song.

“If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” Continuance is the condition He named. Knowledge of the truth is not a motto on the cover. It is the fruit of remaining in His word. Dull hearing (Hebrews 5:11) will not continue. Unskill in the word of righteousness (Hebrews 5:13) will not know. Milk after the time you ought to have been a teacher will not make you free indeed.

The graphē of lesson 1 is the word you continue in here. You do not continue in a substitute. You do not continue in a heading. Name one word of His you will continue in this week, and continue in it. Free from what, in John 8? From being the servant of sin — if the Son make you free, and if you continue in His word. Write that from these passages, not from a political or emotional cry.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write John 8:31-36 in full. Answer from these passages: free from what, if you continue in His word? Then name one word of His you will continue in this week. Do not answer with a political or emotional cry.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: hold John 8:31-36 with Hebrews 5:11-14. Show why dull hearing and unskill cannot produce the freedom the Lord named. Page 3: teach these passages as if you had to teach it clearly to another student — continue, know, free; servant of sin; the Son abides; free indeed.

Write in your own hand. Quote John 8:31-36 in full. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Freedom from remaining in His word vs a political or emotional cry.

Charge
Write what you will teach: truth makes free where you continue in His word; freedom here is over against the servant of sin; the Son makes free indeed. Then complete the practice assignment. Free from what, in John 8, if you continue in His word?

lessons.title: Seven words for repent — metanoia vs metamellomai
lessons.body:
Central principle
Metanoia is a real change of mind toward sin and its cause. Metamellomai regrets consequences, not the cause.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:1; Matthew 27:3; Luke 13:3; Matthew 3:8.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, sections I–II.

Teaching
Hebrews 6:1 — “not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works…” This is the first stone. If this stone is a slogan, the year is a slogan. This principle is headed: Greek metanoia from nekros ergon.

The authorized list for Foundation School is seven. There is no eighth. You were not given an eighth. Do not invent one.

1. Hebrew nacham (H5162) — to sigh, breathe strongly, to be sorry (Genesis 6:6; Exodus 13:17; Job 42:6; Jonah 3:10).
2. Hebrew shuwb (H7725) — to turn back (1 Kings 8:47; Ezekiel 14:6).
3. Hebrew nocham (H5164) — regret (Hosea 13:14).
4. Hebrew nichuwm (H5150) — compassion (Hosea 11:8).
5. Greek metanoeō (G3340) — to change the mind for the better morally; to change the attitude toward sin (Luke 13:3).
6. Greek metamellomai (G3338) — to regret consequences of sin, not the cause (Matthew 27:3; 2 Corinthians 7:8).
7. Greek metanoia (G3341) — a real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, not merely the consequences (Matthew 3:8, 11; 9:13; Luke 24:47).

Hold 6 and 7 together until you can teach the difference in your sleep.

Matthew 27:3-5 — “Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.” He “repented himself” (metamellomai) when he saw the condemnation. He regretted the consequence. He did not come to a new mind over sin and its cause.

Luke 13:3 — “I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent (metanoeō), ye shall all likewise perish.” That is a change of mind toward sin, not a regret that the tower fell on someone else. Matthew 3:8 — “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance (metanoia).” Metanoia includes reformation: new creature, all things new (2 Corinthians 5:17). It is not a tear without a turn. It specifies compunction for guilt including reformation: regeneration, quickening, recreation. A real change of mind and attitude over sin and the cause.

If you treat Judas’s remorse as if it were metanoia, you have not laid this foundation. You have laid a feeling.

Walk the seven as they are taught, not as a seminary extra list.

Nacham (H5162): Genesis 6:6 — “And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.” Also Exodus 13:17; Job 42:6; Jonah 3:10. To sigh, breathe strongly, to be sorry. Shuwb (H7725): 1 Kings 8:47; Ezekiel 14:6 — to turn back. Nocham (H5164): Hosea 13:14 — regret. Nichuwm (H5150): Hosea 11:8 — compassion. Metanoeō (G3340): Luke 13:3 — change the mind for the better morally; change the attitude toward sin. Metamellomai (G3338): Matthew 27:3; 2 Corinthians 7:8 — regret consequences, not the cause. Metanoia (G3341): Matthew 3:8, 11; 9:13; Luke 24:47 — a real change of mind and attitude toward sin and its cause, not merely the consequences.

Matthew 3:8 — “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.” Matthew 9:13 — “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” Luke 24:47 — “And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.” Metanoia includes reformation because the man in Christ is a new creature: 2 Corinthians 5:17 — old things passed away; all things new. It is not a tear without a turn.

Hold 6 and 7 until you can teach them in your sleep. Judas saw the condemnation and “repented himself.” He brought the silver. He said he had sinned. He hanged himself. That is metamellomai. Luke 13:3 will not let you treat another man’s ruin as your change of mind. Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. If you treat Judas’s remorse as the foundation, you have laid a feeling.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write the seven words with one verse each, as the school lists them. Then write ten lines: where have you treated regret as if it were metanoia? Hold metamellomai and metanoia until the difference can be taught without a slogan.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Matthew 27:3-5 and Luke 13:3 and Matthew 3:8 in full. Reason Judas’s metamellomai against metanoeō and metanoia. Do not add an eighth word. Page 3: teach the seven as if you had to teach them clearly to another student — each word, then the distinction between 6 and 7.

Write in your own hand. The seven words with verses. Then Judas against Luke 13:3. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Metanoia vs metamellomai. Cause vs consequence. Reformation vs remorse only.

Charge
Write what you will teach: the seven words only; metanoia is a change of mind toward sin and its cause; metamellomai regrets consequences, not the cause; Judas is not the foundation. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Cause, not consequence — Luke 16:19-31
lessons.body:
Central principle
Hell is a consequence. It is not the definition of repentance.

Key Scripture
Luke 16:19-31; Revelation 20:10-15.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section III.

Teaching
The correct passage for this narrative is Luke 16:19-31, not Matthew 16.

Luke 16:19-31 — “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried; And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence. Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

That narrative is the consequence. The rich man in torment lift up his eyes. A great gulf is fixed. He asks for water. He asks that Lazarus be sent to his five brethren. Abraham refuses: they have Moses and the prophets. If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rose from the dead. Fear of that place is not yet a change of mind over sin and its cause. A man may fear that fire and still love the cause of his death.

Revelation 20:10-15 — “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever. And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

That is the end of the consequence. Chapter 7 will open eternal judgment at length. Do not turn this lesson into that chapter. Here the point is narrower: if your “repentance” is only the wish not to go there, you have not yet changed your mind over sin and its cause.

Abraham’s refusal is the point this lesson will not let you skip. The rich man wants a messenger from the dead. Abraham will not send one. They have Moses and the prophets. If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rose from the dead. The living were already under the writing. A sign from torment will not do what the graphē was given to do. Fear of that flame, in the mouth of a man who still wants water and still wants a warning for his brothers, is not yet a change of mind over sin and its cause.

You may fear Hell and love the cause of your death. That fear can fill a testimony and leave the old man unnamed. That fear can fill a prayer and leave outward sin unlisted. Course 6 will open the lake, the book of life, and the prisons. Here you will not turn Luke 16 into that chapter. Here you will say: Hell is a consequence. Metanoia is toward sin and its cause. The narrative is Luke 16:19-31, not Matthew 16.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Luke 16:27-31 in your own words after you have written the stretch. What did Abraham refuse? Then answer: where have you treated Hell-avoidance as if it were metanoia?

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Luke 16:19-31 in full. Keep the correction clear: Luke 16, not Matthew 16. Sit the rich man, the gulf, Moses and the prophets, and the refusal. Page 3: write Revelation 20:10-15 in full. Teach consequence versus cause. Do not open Chapter 7’s prisons here. Write the teaching as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote Luke 16 as named. Abraham’s refusal must be on the page. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Repentance over sin and its cause vs Hell-avoidance.

Charge
Write what you will teach: Hell is a consequence; the narrative is Luke 16:19-31, not Matthew 16; Moses and the prophets were already enough for the living; fear of the lake is not yet metanoia. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Nekros ergon — dead works
lessons.body:
Central principle
Dead works are the works of the old man and the old nature. The conscience is later purged from them by blood (Hebrews 9:14).

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:1; Ephesians 2:1; Ephesians 4:22; Romans 6:23.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section I and the opening of IV.

Teaching
Hebrews 6:1 names the first stone: repentance from dead works. The phrase is Hebrews’ own phrase. You will hear it again in Hebrews 9:14, when the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God. Do not empty “dead works” into “things I did that felt empty.” This lesson will not let you.

Nekros ergon — dead works — are the works of the old man: the spirit and nature of the devil (Ephesians 4:22); old things (2 Corinthians 5:17); the old nature (Ephesians 2:1). Ephesians 2:1-2 — “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience.” Trespasses, in Ephesians 2:1, are deviation from moral equity, and sins. The wages thereof is death (Romans 6:23).

Ephesians 4:22 — “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts.” 2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.” Dead works are the works of that old nature — the spirit and nature of the devil, and the sins that issue. They are not a boredom you renamed. A work can be crowded, admired, and still be dead if it is of the old man.

Metanoia also carries the force of reversal. Do not flatten that into a technique. Keep this: repentance is not less than a change of mind. The change is toward sin and its cause. The works that belong to the old man are the works you repent from. The next two lessons will split the two old things. This lesson will not let you call a dull religious habit “dead” while you keep the old nature unnamed.

Hebrews 9:14 will later say: “How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” Keep that verse as the destination of this phrase. Do not empty dead works now so that blood later has nothing to purge. Dead works are the works of the old man and the old nature. They issue in death (Romans 6:23). They are the conversation you put off (Ephesians 4:22). They are the walk according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air (Ephesians 2:2).

A work that bored you is not therefore a dead work. A work that filled a room is not therefore a living work. The test is the man — old or new — and the nature that produced it. If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away. The two old things will be split in the next lessons. This lesson names the pile they belong to: nekros ergon, the works you repent from. Do not call a dull habit “dead” while the old nature goes unnamed. Do not call the old nature a theory while the works go unrepented.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Hebrews 6:1, Ephesians 2:1-2, and 2 Corinthians 5:17. Define dead works: the works of the old man, not a task that bored you. Then name one work you have called “dead” because it bored you, and one the Scripture would call a dead work because it is of the old man. Do not confuse them.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Ephesians 4:22 and Romans 6:23 with the verses already on page 1. Show the line from old man to dead works to wages. Page 3: teach nekros ergon as if you had to teach it clearly to another student, and show why Hebrews 9:14 will later name blood as the purge — without turning this lesson into the blood lesson.

Write in your own hand. Quote Hebrews 6:1 and Ephesians 2:1-2. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Dead works vs the service of the living God after the conscience is purged (Hebrews 9:14).

Charge
Write what you will teach: dead works are the works of the old man and the old nature; they are not a boredom you renamed; the conscience is purged from them by blood. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Old thing 1 — the old man
lessons.body:
Central principle
The old man is nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience.

Key Scripture
Ephesians 4:22; John 8:44; Ephesians 2:2; 1 John 3:8-9; 5:18; 2 Corinthians 4:4.

Read
That section, old thing 1 only.

Teaching
2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.” Repentance from dead works separates two kinds of “old things” that have passed away in Christ. This lesson is old thing 1 only. Do not merge it with the list of acts.

Old thing 1. The spirit, nature, and power of sin — the old man: nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience.

Ephesians 4:22 — “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts.”

John 8:44 — “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

Ephesians 2:2 — “Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience.”

2 Corinthians 4:4 — “In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.”

1 John 3:8-9 — “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil. Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.”

1 John 5:18 — “We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.”

Do not soften these passages. Do not turn it into a personality type. Do not reduce the old man to a bad habit. This lesson will not let you. The old man is the spirit and nature of the devil in the disobedient. Put off the old man. Ye are of your father the devil. The spirit now worketh in the children of disobedience. The god of this world hath blinded minds. He that committeth sin is of the devil. Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; the wicked one toucheth him not.

You cannot hide the old man behind a list of acts. The next lesson will open the acts. Both must pass. They are not one undistinguished category.

Put these passages in order and keep it severe. Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth. The spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience is the prince of the power of the air. The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil. Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; his seed remaineth in him. He that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.

The old man is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts. Put him off. He is nothing more nor less than the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience. A bad habit can be broken and the old man remain. A personality can be managed and the old man remain. Foundation School will not let you teach John 8:44, Ephesians 2:2, and 1 John 3:8-9 as a temperament category. In Christ this old thing is passed away. Outward sin is the other old thing. Both must pass. They are not one undistinguished category.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Teach John 8:44, Ephesians 2:2, and 1 John 3:8-9 as one Scripture set without calling the old man “a bad habit.” Write the three verses. Write the teaching.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: add Ephesians 4:22, 2 Corinthians 4:4, and 1 John 5:18 in full. Keep old thing 1 as old thing 1. Do not walk Galatians 5 here. Page 3: teach the old man as if you had to teach it clearly to another student — spirit and nature of the devil in the disobedient; put off; born of God; the wicked one toucheth him not.

Write in your own hand. Quote the three verses of the tight Scripture set in full. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Old man vs outward sin. Both must pass. They are not one undistinguished category.

Charge
Write what you will teach: the old man is the spirit and nature of the devil working in men of disobedience; the governing passages are John 8:44, Ephesians 2:2, 1 John 3:8-9, and the rest of this lesson; the old man is not a habit. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Old thing 2 — outward sin
lessons.body:
Central principle
Outward sin is the second old thing. It has its own Scripture teaching. It is not another name for the old man.

Key Scripture
Galatians 5:19-21; 1 John 3:4; James 1:13-15; Mark 7:20-23; Romans 1:18-32; Romans 4:15.

Read
That section only. Do not skip the lists.

Teaching
Old thing 2 is outward sin. You cannot hide the acts behind a theory of nature. You cannot hide the old man behind a list of acts. Both must pass. In Christ they are passed away.

Galatians 5:19-21 — “Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.”

1 John 3:4 — “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” Romans 4:15 — “Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.”

James 1:13-15 — “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.”

Mark 7:20-23 — “And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Romans 1:18 — “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness.” The catalogue that follows through Romans 1:32 is not a curiosity. It is outward sin named. Walk it in the Labour. Do not skip the lists because they are long.

Sin is the transgression of the law. Lust conceives, brings forth sin, sin finished brings death. What proceeds from the heart defiles the man. The works of the flesh are manifest. The wrath of God is revealed against ungodliness. These two old things are not one undistinguished category labelled “sin” so that you can hide the old man behind a list of acts, or hide the acts behind a theory of nature.

Walk Romans 1:18-32. Do not skip it because it is long. “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness.” They knew God and glorified him not as God. Their foolish heart was darkened. God gave them up. The catalogue names uncleanness, vile affections, a reprobate mind, unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness, envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity, whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful. Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.

That is outward sin named. Galatians 5:19-21 is outward sin named. Mark 7:20-23 is what proceeds from the heart and defiles. 1 John 3:4 is the definition: sin is the transgression of the law. James 1:13-15 is the conception: lust, sin, death. You cannot hide these acts behind a theory of the old man. You cannot hide the old man behind these acts. Write the lists without calling them “the old man.” Then state what must pass besides the list.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Walk Galatians 5:19-21 and Mark 7:20-23 without calling them “the old man.” Write both lists. Then state what must pass besides the list — old thing 1, already taught.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write 1 John 3:4, Romans 4:15, and James 1:13-15 in full. Show transgression, lust conceiving, sin finished, death. Page 3: write Romans 1:18-32 in full. Teach outward sin as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Keep the two old things as two.

Write in your own hand. The lists must be on the page. The page is not a journal of feelings.
