Distinction
Two old things, not one confession.

Charge
Write what you will teach: outward sin is the second old thing; it has its own teaching; the lists must be walked; both old things must pass. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Romans 6:23 — the wages
lessons.body:
Central principle
The wages of sin is death. Sin is the cause of all death and depravity. Salvation from sin is the salvation you need.

Key Scripture
Romans 6:23 in Romans 6:16-23.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section V.

Teaching
Romans 6:16-23 — “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness? But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you. Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness. I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness. For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness. What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death. But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life. For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Read the verse in Romans 6. You were the servants of sin. You are to be the servants of righteousness. Death is the wage of the old things. Eternal life is the gift of God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Wage versus gift. Cause versus consequence. Do not build a repentance that wants to keep the cause and escape the wage.

Hold the line: salvation from sin is the salvation you need, because sin is the cause of all death and depravity. Death in this book is not only the stopping of breath. Chapter 7 will open three kinds of death. Here it is enough to refuse a shallow “death,” and to refuse a repentance that wants the gift while it keeps the service of sin.

2 Corinthians 5:17 remains in these passages: if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away; all things are become new. The wage belongs to the old things. The gift belongs to the man in Christ. You do not collect the gift as a wage you earned. You do not treat the wage as a mood you can talk down.

Yield is the verb Romans 6 will not let you skip. To whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Sin unto death. Obedience unto righteousness. Ye were the servants of sin. Ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you. Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness. When ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness. The end of those things is death. Now, made free from sin and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

Wage versus gift is not a slogan for a card. The wage is earned by the service of sin. The gift is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. You do not earn the gift. You do not talk the wage down into a metaphor so shallow that Course 6 will have nothing to open. Three kinds of death wait for that course. Here you refuse a repentance that wants to keep the cause — sin, the old things — and escape the wage. Salvation from sin is the salvation you need, because sin is the cause of all death and depravity. What other “salvation” have you put in that place? Name it and put it down.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Romans 6:23, then write the verse that names the gift. Then answer: what other “salvation” have you put in the place of salvation from sin?

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Romans 6:16-23 in full. Show servants of sin, servants of righteousness, fruit unto death, fruit unto holiness, wage, gift. Page 3: teach wage versus gift and cause versus consequence as if you had to teach them clearly to another student. Name that three kinds of death wait for Course 6. Do not open that course here.

Write in your own hand. Quote Romans 6:23 and the gift clause. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Wage vs gift. Cause vs consequence.

Charge
Write what you will teach: the wages of sin is death; eternal life is the gift through Jesus Christ our Lord; salvation from sin is the salvation you need; do not keep the cause and hunt the gift. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Christ the only way — Hebrews 9:14
lessons.body:
Central principle
The only way out of sin unto true repentance is Christ Jesus. His blood purges the conscience from dead works.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 9:14; Ephesians 2:1-5; 2 Corinthians 5:17.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section VI, through 2 Corinthians 5:17.

Teaching
Hebrews 9:11-14 — “But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?”

The phrase “dead works” is Hebrews’ own phrase. The conscience is purged from them by the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without spot to God, to serve the living God. Self-reformation without that blood is still a dead work. You do not purge your own conscience by a new schedule. The high priest entered by His own blood, once, having obtained eternal redemption.

Ephesians 2:1-5 — “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience: Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others. But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)”

You were dead in trespasses and sins. God quickened you together with Christ. 2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.” The new creature is in Christ. The two old things pass in Him. The conscience is purged by blood, not by a substitute of reformation that never came to the altar.

The comparison in Hebrews 9 is blood for blood. The blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer, sanctified to the purifying of the flesh. How much more the blood of Christ. He offered Himself without spot to God through the eternal Spirit. He entered in once into the holy place by His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption. The conscience is purged from dead works — Hebrews’ own phrase — to serve the living God. Self-reformation that never comes to that blood is still a dead work. A new schedule that never comes to that blood is still a dead work.

Ephesians 2 will not let you start as a man who was only tired. You were dead in trespasses and sins. You walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air. You were by nature the children of wrath. But God, who is rich in mercy, for His great love wherewith He loved us, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ — by grace ye are saved. The only way out of sin unto true repentance is Christ Jesus. The new creature is in Him. Answer from Hebrews 9:14 in a paragraph a babe could follow: how does blood purge the conscience from dead works? Do not answer with a rite. Do not answer with a course.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Answer from Hebrews 9:14 in a paragraph a babe could follow: how does blood purge the conscience from dead works? Write the verse. Write the paragraph.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Hebrews 9:11-14 in full. Sit “his own blood,” “once,” “eternal redemption,” and “dead works” in one stretch. Page 3: write Ephesians 2:1-5 and 2 Corinthians 5:17. Teach Christ the way versus self-reformation as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote Hebrews 9:14. The paragraph a babe could follow must be on the page.

Distinction
Christ the way vs self-reformation as the way.

Charge
Write what you will teach: the only way out of sin unto true repentance is Christ Jesus; His blood purges the conscience from dead works; self-reformation without that blood is still a dead work. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: No other name — Acts 4:12
lessons.body:
Central principle
There is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved.

Key Scripture
Acts 4:10-12.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section VI, Acts 4:12.

Teaching
Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, answers rulers about a man made whole.

Acts 4:8-12 — “Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him doth this man stand here before you whole. This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.”

The stone rejected, Jesus Christ of Nazareth, crucified, whom God raised. Neither is there salvation in any other. No second saviour. No rite in the place of His name. Water is a sign after one is saved. It is not this stone. Course 3 will open water as figure. You will not put the font in Acts 4:12.

2 Corinthians 5:17 remains in these passages: if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature. The name that saves is the name you receive. The new creature is in Him, not in a second name, not in a sign that follows, not in an enrolment. There is none other name under heaven given among men. “Given among men” will not let you keep a private saviour for a private people. “Must be saved” will not let you treat the name as one option among rites.

Acts 4:7 is the examination: “By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?” Peter does not offer a second name. Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead — by Him this man stands whole. This is the stone set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. Psalm 118:22 sits under that sentence. The rejected stone is not a rite. It is this Jesus.

“Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.” Under heaven. Given among men. Must be saved. No private saviour for a private people. No second saviour beside the stone. Water will be taught in Course 3 as a sign after one is saved. It is not this stone. A confession that puts another name — a church, a tank, a man, a method — in the place of this name is a sentence you will not say again. Write Acts 4:12. Write the sentence you will not say. The new creature is in Christ, not in the sign that follows.

Peter is standing before rulers and elders. The man made whole is standing there. The name that made him whole is the name whereby we must be saved. You will not divide those two uses of the name — one for a body, one for the soul — as if Acts 4:12 were a smaller word than Acts 4:10. The stone set at nought is become the head of the corner. There is none other. Course 3 will open water as figure after one is saved. This stone is not the font. This stone is Jesus Christ of Nazareth, crucified, whom God raised.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Acts 4:12. Then write one sentence you will not say again if it puts another name in that place. Name the stone. Name what the font is not.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Acts 4:8-12 in full. Sit the examination, the name, the crucifixion, the resurrection, the stone, and “none other.” Page 3: teach the name that saves versus signs that follow, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Keep water for Course 3. Do not open that course here.

Write in your own hand. Quote Acts 4:12. The sentence you will not say must be on the page.

Distinction
The name that saves vs signs that follow.

Charge
Write what you will teach: none other name under heaven; Jesus Christ of Nazareth, crucified, whom God raised; water is a sign after one is saved, not this stone. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Receive Him — John 1:12; Romans 10:8-9
lessons.body:
Central principle
As many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God. Confess the Lord Jesus; believe God raised Him; thou shalt be saved.

Key Scripture
John 1:12-13; Romans 10:8-10.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 2, section VII.

Teaching
John 1:11-13 — “He came unto his own, and his own received him not. But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.”

Romans 10:6-10 — “But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.”

Born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. The word is nigh thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart — the word of faith. With the heart man believeth unto righteousness; with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Sonship language begins here. Course 2 will open the heir. Course 3 will open the Spirit’s witness. You do not wait for those courses to receive Him.

The charge stands: Receive Him today. Receiving Him is not enrolling in a course. A course can sit around an unreceived Christ and call the sitting growth. John 1:11 will not let you hide in a people who did not receive Him. John 1:12 will not let you postpone the receiving. Romans 10:9 will not let you invent a confession the text does not ask. Confess the Lord Jesus. Believe in thine heart that God hath raised Him from the dead. Thou shalt be saved.

John 1:1-4 has already named the Word: in the beginning, with God, was God; all things were made by Him; in Him was life, and the life was the light of men. He came unto His own. His own received Him not. Reception is not a mood about a course. It is receiving Him. To them that received Him He gave power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on His name. Born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. Lineage will not do it. Appetite will not do it. Another man’s will will not do it.

Romans 10:6-7 forbids a hunt that would bring Christ down or bring Him up from the dead, as if the word were far. The word is nigh thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart — the word of faith. Confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus. Believe in thine heart that God hath raised Him from the dead. Thou shalt be saved. With the heart man believeth unto righteousness; with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. That is the confession the text asks. Sonship language begins here. Course 2 will open the heir. Course 3 will open the Spirit’s witness. You do not wait. Have you received Him? Write the confession. If you have, write John 1:12-13 without a slogan. The charge stands: Receive Him today.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Have you received Him? Write the confession Romans 10:9 actually asks. If you have, write what “power to become the sons of God” means from John 1:12-13, not from a slogan. If you have not, write the confession and do not hide in the course.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write John 1:11-13 in full. Reason “received him not,” “received him,” “power to become,” “believe on his name,” and “born… of God.” Page 3: write Romans 10:6-10 in full. Teach receiving Him versus enrolling in a course, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote John 1:12-13 and Romans 10:9. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Receiving Him vs enrolling in a course.

Charge
Write what you will teach: as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God; born of God, not of blood or will; confess the Lord Jesus; believe God raised Him. Then complete the practice assignment. The charge stands: Receive Him today.

lessons.title: Charge and examination of the principle
lessons.body:
Central principle
The first stone is laid when a man has changed his mind over sin and its cause, and has received the One whose blood purges the conscience from dead works.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:1; 2 Corinthians 5:17; Hebrews 9:14; Acts 4:12; John 1:12; Romans 10:9.

Read
Chapter 2, sections VIII–IX. Directed reading: The Power of Salvation, when that volume is in your hand — assigned sections only, not a second course.

Teaching
This lesson is the examination of the principle, not a new doctrine.

Hebrews 6:1 — “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works…” 2 Corinthians 5:17 — “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.” Hebrews 9:14 — the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God. Acts 4:12 — none other name under heaven. John 1:12 — as many as received Him. Romans 10:9 — confess the Lord Jesus; believe God raised Him; thou shalt be saved.

You should now be able to teach, from Scripture:

1. Graphē over religious imitation. John 10:34-36; the scripture cannot be broken.
2. Babe vs teacher; apeiros; nēpios; two marks — dull of hearing; unskilled in the Word.
3. Spoudazō as labour. 2 Timothy 2:15. Knowledge as perception, learning, reasoning.
4. The seven words; metanoia vs metamellomai. Judas regretted the consequence. Metanoia is a change of mind toward sin and its cause.
5. Cause vs consequence. Luke 16:19-31, not Matthew 16. Revelation 20:10-15 as the end of the consequence.
6. Two old things: the old man (spirit and nature of the devil in the disobedient); outward sin (its own lists). Both must pass.
7. Wages and the only salvation you need. Romans 6:23. Salvation from sin.
8. Christ the only way; no other name; receive Him.

This chapter will not treat Hell-avoidance as metanoia. It will not treat Judas’s regret as the foundation. It will not merge the old man and outward sin into one vague confession. It will not offer another name. It will not tell you that a course enrolment is the new creature.

The new creature is in Christ. The foundation is laid when a man has changed his mind over sin and its cause, and has received the One whose blood purges the conscience from dead works. Directed reading: The Power of Salvation, when that volume is in your hand — assigned sections only. It is a companion, not a seventh course, and not a substitute for this chapter.

Then you are ready to be taught faith toward God — not as a feeling, but as the state of sons.

Chapter 2, sections VIII–IX, will not do five things, and this examination will not do them either. It will not treat Hell-avoidance as metanoia. It will not treat Judas’s regret as the foundation. It will not merge the old man and outward sin into one vague confession. It will not offer another name. It will not tell you that a course enrolment is the new creature.

Write the eight as teaching, not as headings you remember. Graphē: John 10:34-36. Babe and teacher: Hebrews 5:11-14; apeiros; nēpios; two marks. Spoudazō: 2 Timothy 2:15; knowledge as perception, learning, reasoning. Seven words; metanoia versus metamellomai; Matthew 27:3 against Luke 13:3 and Matthew 3:8. Cause versus consequence: Luke 16:19-31, not Matthew 16; Revelation 20:10-15 limited. Two old things, each with its teaching. Romans 6:16-23: wage and gift; salvation from sin. Christ the only way: Hebrews 9:14; Acts 4:12; John 1:12; Romans 10:9.

The Power of Salvation, when that volume is in your hand, is directed reading — assigned sections only. It is a companion, not a seventh course, and not a substitute for this chapter. Completion of activities is not mastery. Write the principle as you would teach it to a babe, then as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. The first stone is laid when a man has changed his mind over sin and its cause, and has received the One whose blood purges the conscience from dead works.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page on each of the eight — eight tight paragraphs if you must keep it to one sitting, but the eight must be written. Intensive: write the full page on each of the eight. The doctrine is the same. The hours differ. The eight do not.

The Walk — eight tight paragraphs, one for each head above, each paragraph quoting the governing verse and stating the distinction. Then one further paragraph: the principle as you would teach it to a babe.

Intensive — eight full pages, one for each head, then a ninth page: the principle as you would teach it to a babe, and as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Do not submit a feeling in the place of these passages. Do not treat The Power of Salvation as this course.

Write in your own hand. The eight must be teaching, not headings. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Completion of activities vs mastery. A certificate later will ask more than a click.

Charge
Write the principle as you would teach it to a babe, then as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Name the two old things. Name the difference between metanoia and metamellomai. Name Luke 16:19-31 as the Hell narrative. Name the confession Romans 10:9 actually asks. Do not submit a feeling in the place of these passages. The practice assignment lists the eight you must write. Write them.

lessons.title: Pistis — credence that defines sons
lessons.body:
Central principle
Faith defines our state as children of God. Greek pistis means credence. It is not a feeling you work up.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:1 — and of faith toward God.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section I.

Teaching
This is Course 2 of Foundation School. One curriculum. The second of the six principles.

Hebrews 6:1 — “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God.” Toward God. The object is a Person. Not a system, not a method, not a school, not a mood you have learned to call faith.

Faith defines our state as children of God. Greek pistis means credence: it credits what God says about our true nature and adoption as sons. Pistis is not a feeling you work up. It is credence that agrees with what God has done and who you are by that doing. Servant is not the name. Son is the name. Heir follows son.

Galatians 4:5-7 — “To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.”

Romans 8:15 — “For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.”

Ephesians 1:5 — “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.”

Course 1 turned you from dead works. You do not turn into a vacuum. You turn toward God. That is why the two principles stand in the same verse. A definition of faith that has no object can be worked up in a room. Pistis credits a Person and a state: son, not servant; adoption, not a nickname you earn. You will write “heir” as its own lesson. Hold the order here: toward God, credence, son.

Do not preach Hebrews 11 as a pep talk in the place of this verse. This course will not walk the whole of that chapter. The principle is faith toward God as Hebrews 6:1 names it, opened by the adoption Scripture set with pistis.

Toward God is the phrase that will not let faith be a method. A man can work up a feeling and call it faith while the object is a system, a school, a technique, or a room. Pistis is credence. Credence has an object. The object here is God. Course 1 turned you from dead works. You do not turn into a vacuum. You turn toward God. That is why repentance from dead works and faith toward God stand in one verse.

With pistis, acceptance means true nature, and espousal means adoption as sons of God. Galatians 4:6 — because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Romans 8:15 — not the spirit of bondage again to fear, but the Spirit of adoption. Ephesians 1:5 — predestinated unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will. Servant is not the name. Son is the name. Heir follows son, and you will write heir later. Hold the order: credence, toward God, son.

This course will not walk Hebrews 11 as a pep talk. The principle is not “heroes of faith” as a mood. The principle is faith toward God as Hebrews 6:1 names it, opened by this adoption Scripture set. Write what “toward God” does that a definition without an object cannot do. Write what pistis credits that a mood cannot credit.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same. The hours differ. The oracles do not.

The Walk — one page. Write, in your own words, what “toward God” does to the word faith that a definition without an object cannot do. Then write what pistis credits that a mood cannot credit. Quote Hebrews 6:1 and Galatians 4:7.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Galatians 4:5-7, Romans 8:15, and Ephesians 1:5 in full. Sit adoption, Abba, no more a servant, son, heir in one stretch. Do not open the heir lesson’s full charge here. Page 3: teach pistis as credence that defines sons, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Refuse faith as a feeling you manufacture.

Write in your own hand. Quote Hebrews 6:1 and Galatians 4:7. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Faith as state and sonship vs faith as a feeling you manufacture.

Charge
Write what you will teach: pistis is credence; it defines our state as children of God; the object is God; servant is not the name. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Acceptance, espousal, adoption
lessons.body:
Central principle
Because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. No more a servant, but a son; if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

Key Scripture
Galatians 4:5-7; Romans 8:15; Ephesians 1:5.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section I, the adoption sentences.

Teaching
Galatians 4:4-7 — “But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.”

God sent forth His Son to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. Because ye are sons — not because ye climbed — the Spirit of His Son is sent into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son. The “wherefore” is not a suggestion. Servant is refused as the name. Son is the name. If a son, then an heir of God through Christ. You will write “heir” as its own lesson. Hold the order here: son, then heir.

Romans 8:15-17 — “For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

Ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear, but the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit in this passage is already the cry of sonship. Course 3 will open the witness and the enduement. Do not wait for that course to refuse the name servant.

Ephesians 1:5 — “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” Predestinated unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will. Adoption is the Father’s doing. It is not a religious nickname you earn.

Fulness of the time. God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. The sending is the Father’s. The redeeming is the Son’s. The receiving is adoption. Because ye are sons — already sons — the Spirit of His Son is sent into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. The cry is not a technique you learn in order to become a son. The cry is because ye are sons.

“Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son.” Wherefore. The name servant is refused. If you keep calling yourself a servant as your standing, you are arguing with Galatians 4:7. If a son, then an heir of God through Christ. The “then” is sonship, not a wage. Romans 8:16-17 will add: the Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God; if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ. Course 3 will open that witness as its own principle. Do not wait for Course 3 to refuse bondage again to fear.

Ephesians 1:5 is the Father’s will, not your climb: predestinated unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will. Adoption is not a religious nickname you earn. Write Galatians 4:7. Write what you must stop calling yourself if son is the name.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Galatians 4:7. Then write what you must stop calling yourself if son is the name and servant is not.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Galatians 4:4-7 and Romans 8:15-17 in full. Sit fulness of time, sent forth, redeem, adoption, Abba, no more a servant, children, heirs, joint-heirs. Keep “heir” named but not exhausted. Page 3: write Ephesians 1:5. Teach adoption as the Father’s doing, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote Galatians 4:7. The name you must stop using must be on the page.

Distinction
Adoption as the Father’s doing vs a religious nickname you earn.

Charge
Write what you will teach: because ye are sons, Abba; no more a servant, but a son; if a son, then an heir; adoption is by Jesus Christ according to His will. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: ’Ĕlōhîm — Let us make man
lessons.body:
Central principle
This acceptance is on the basis of our true nature from creation with respect to God. ’Ĕlōhîm said, Let us make man.

Key Scripture
Genesis 1:26.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section II, the ’ĕlōhîm sentences.

Teaching
This acceptance is grounded in the true nature God gave man at creation.

Genesis 1:26 — “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.”

Hebrew ’ĕlōhîm. This lesson reads it as plural: Trinity. “Let us make” is not a committee of angels inventing a lesser thing. God speaks as God, and man is made in that image, after that likeness. Foundation School will not put a softer sentence in the place of Genesis 1:26.

Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. Dominion is in the making-verse, not in a later slogan. Man is who he is by how he was designed and by Who designed him. That is the text.

Genesis 1:27-28 remain in these passages and will be opened as image and likeness in the next lesson. Do not skip 1:26 to make the making safe. Do not hedge “image” until it means only that man can worship from a distance. Who speaks? God — ’ĕlōhîm. What is made? Man. In whose image? Ours — the image of the Speaker. After whose likeness? Ours. What is given in the same breath? Dominion.

You will not write a safer verse in the place of this one. You will not treat “Let us make” as a figure you are free to empty. This lesson reads ’ĕlōhîm as God speaking as God. Foundation School teaches that reading. A lesser maker of a lesser creature is not this verse.

Genesis 1:26 as written will not bear a hedge. And God said. Let us make man. In our image. After our likeness. And let them have dominion — fish, fowl, cattle, all the earth, every creeping thing. Who speaks? ’Ĕlōhîm. This lesson reads the plural as Trinity. “Let us make” is God speaking as God. It is not a committee of angels inventing a lesser thing. What is made? Man. In whose image? Ours. After whose likeness? Ours. What is given in the same breath? Dominion.

Man is who he is by how he was designed and by Who designed him. This acceptance — the acceptance pistis credits — is grounded in that true nature from creation. You will not write a safer verse in the place of this one. You will not empty “image” until it means only that man may worship from far. You will not empty “likeness” until it means only a moral hint. You will not move dominion to a later slogan as if 1:26 had not already said “let them have dominion.”

Genesis 1:27-28 remain and will be opened next. Do not skip 1:26 to make the making safe. Write the verse. Name Who speaks, what is made, and in whose image. Foundation School will not put a softer sentence in the place of Genesis 1:26.

Acceptance, as Chapter 3 opens it, is grounded in this true nature from creation. Pistis credits what ’ĕlōhîm said, not what a safer teaching would rather He had said. If you flatten “Let us make” into a figure, you have already begun to flatten image, likeness, and dominion. The next lesson will keep 1:26-28 as written and mark the TLB as a gloss. This lesson holds the text steady: Who speaks, what is made, in whose image, and dominion in the same breath.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Genesis 1:26. Name Who speaks, what is made, and in whose image. Do not write a safer verse in its place.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Genesis 1:26-28 in full. Keep the making as written. Do not hedge image, likeness, or dominion. Page 3: teach ’ĕlōhîm — plural, Trinity, God speaking as God — as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Refuse a committee of angels.

Write in your own hand. Quote Genesis 1:26 as written. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
’Ĕlōhîm as God speaking as God vs a lesser maker of a lesser creature.

Charge
Write what you will teach: ’ĕlōhîm said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; dominion is in the same verse; man is who he is by how he was designed and by Who designed him. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Image and likeness — like his Maker
lessons.body:
Central principle
God created man in His own image. Male and female created He them. Image. Likeness. Dominion.

Key Scripture
Genesis 1:26-28.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section II.

Teaching
Genesis 1:26-28 — “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.”

Genesis 1:27 as written: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. The Living Bible (TLB) gloss, kept as a gloss beside the KJV: “So God made man like his Maker. Like God did God make man; Man and maid did he make them.” Mark it TLB. Do not preach the gloss as if it were the King James. Do not hide the King James behind the gloss.

Genesis 1:28 — Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion. Image. Likeness. Dominion. That is the text. Foundation School will not put a softer sentence in the place of Genesis 1:26-28.

John 14:12 — “Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.”

1 John 4:17 — “Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.”

Romans 8:17 — “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

Teach these passages as written. Do not empty Genesis to make it safe. Do not detach the later verses from the making. John 14:12 and 1 John 4:17 are held with the making, not against it. Psalm 82:6 and John 17:20-23 sit in these passages and will be opened in their own lessons. Do not exhaust them here. Do not skip them as if they were not already named.

Genesis 1:27 twice says image: in his own image; in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. The TLB gloss — marked TLB, not preached as KJV — says: “So God made man like his Maker. Like God did God make man; Man and maid did he make them.” Keep the gloss as a gloss. Do not hide the King James behind it. Do not preach the gloss as if it were the text you must answer from.

Genesis 1:28 is blessing and charge in one breath: be fruitful, multiply, replenish, subdue, have dominion. Image. Likeness. Dominion. Male and female. That is the making as written. What does Genesis 1:26 actually say, and what does it not say? It says Let us make man in our image, after our likeness, and let them have dominion. It does not say a reduced man who is only a worshipper of a distant God. It does not say a later hedge you invented to make the verse safe.

John 14:12 — he that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also, and greater works, because I go unto my Father. 1 John 4:17 — as he is, so are we in this world. Hold those with the making, not against it. Romans 8:17 — heirs of God, joint-heirs with Christ — will be opened as heir. Psalm 82:6 and John 17 will have their lessons. Do not detach them. Do not exhaust them here. Teach these passages as written.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. What does Genesis 1:26 actually say, and what does it not say? Write the verse. Write the TLB as a gloss, marked TLB. Then write one sentence from John 14:12 or 1 John 4:17 that you will hold with the making, not against it.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Genesis 1:26-28 in full. Sit image, likeness, male and female, fruitful, multiply, replenish, subdue, dominion. Page 3: write John 14:12, 1 John 4:17, and Romans 8:17. Teach these passages as written, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Do not empty Genesis. Do not detach the later verses.

Write in your own hand. Quote Genesis 1:26-28. Mark the TLB as TLB. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Image and likeness as the text states them vs a reduced man who is only a worshipper of a distant God.

Charge
Write what you will teach: God created man in His own image; male and female; image, likeness, dominion; TLB is a marked gloss, not the KJV; John 14:12 and 1 John 4:17 are held with the making. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: True nature — partakers
lessons.body:
Central principle
You are not being invited to invent another nature. You are being returned to the one Genesis named, in Christ.

Key Scripture
2 Peter 1:4.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section III.

Teaching
2 Peter 1:3-7 — “According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

2 Peter 1:4: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

This lesson places this with man’s true nature and with the glory he came short of through sin. Dikaiosynē, later in this course, is equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God — original: back on course. Partaker is not a tourist of divinity. It is the man restored to the nature Genesis named, having escaped the corruption.

You are not being invited to invent another nature. You are being returned to the one Genesis named, in Christ. “Back on course” forces you to stop calling the new creature a new invention God did not make. The making was Genesis 1:26-28. The shortcoming will be Romans 3:23. The partaking is here. The promises are the means the verse names. Escape from the corruption that is in the world through lust is already in the verse. Do not preach partaking as a climb that never escaped.

His divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue. Given. Not earned as a wage. The adding in 1:5-7 is diligence beside what was given, not a second nature you construct. Faith is already in that list as the thing you add to — pistis already credited. Do not turn the list into a ladder that replaces credence.

2 Peter 1:3 is already gift: his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue. Given. Then the promises: exceeding great and precious, that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. Partaker is by the promises. Escape is already in the verse. You are not being invited to invent another nature. You are being returned to the one Genesis named, in Christ.

Dikaiosynē will later be equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God — original: back on course. “Back on course” forces you to stop calling the new creature a new invention God did not make. The making was Genesis 1:26-28. The shortcoming will be Romans 3:23. The partaking is here. The adding in 1:5-7 begins with faith — pistis already credited — and adds virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity. That adding is diligence beside what was given. It is not a second nature you construct, and it is not a ladder that replaces credence.

Write 2 Peter 1:4. Write what “back on course” forbids you to call a new invention. Partaker is not a tourist of divinity.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write 2 Peter 1:4. Then write what “back on course” forces you to stop calling a new invention.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write 2 Peter 1:3-7 in full. Sit given, promises, partakers, escaped, and the adding that begins with faith. Page 3: teach partaker of the divine nature versus inventing another nature God did not make, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Hold Genesis as the nature named.

Write in your own hand. Quote 2 Peter 1:4. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
Partaker of the divine nature vs inventing another nature God did not make.

Charge
Write what you will teach: partakers of the divine nature by the promises; escaped the corruption; returned to the nature Genesis named, in Christ; not a new invention. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Psalm 82:6 with John 10:34-35
lessons.body:
Central principle
I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. The Scripture cannot be broken.

Key Scripture
Psalm 82:6; John 10:34-35.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section II, the psalm and the Lord’s appeal.

Teaching
Jesus answered a charge of blasphemy by the writing.

John 10:34-36 — “Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?”

Psalm 82:6-7 — “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.”

Psalm 82:7 remains in the psalm. Teach 82:6 with 82:7 and with John 10. Do not detach the verse from the writing. Do not empty the verse to make it safe. The Lord would not let men set His person against the Scripture. Neither will Foundation School.

Course 1 already used John 10:35 as the graphē lesson: the scripture cannot be broken. This lesson will not repeat that lesson as if Psalm 82 had not been cited. The Lord appeals to the writing: I said, Ye are gods. If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken. The psalm also says they shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes. Both verses stay. A slogan that keeps 82:6 and drops 82:7 has not kept these passages. A verse so emptied that the Lord could not have appealed to it has not been taught as Scripture.

The psalm addresses those unto whom the word of God came. The Lord uses that writing against the charge that He blasphemed by saying, I am the Son of God. You will write what these passages force. You will not write a detached boast. You will not write a safer psalm.

Psalm 82 is a psalm of judgment among the mighty. Verse 6 is not a detached boast. “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Verse 7 remains: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” The Lord takes up verse 6 in John 10 against a charge of blasphemy. They said He, being a man, made Himself God. He said: Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken — say ye of Him whom the Father sanctified and sent, Thou blasphemest, because I said, I am the Son of God?

Course 1 already taught John 10:35 as graphē: the scripture cannot be broken. This lesson will not drop 82:7 to keep 82:6 as a slogan. This lesson will not empty 82:6 until the Lord could not have appealed to it. Both verses stay. The Lord’s use stays. Write Psalm 82:6-7 and John 10:34-35 as one Scripture set. Then write what you must not say if you keep both verses and the Lord’s use of them. Do not write a detached boast. Do not write a safer psalm.

The Lord rests His answer on the writing. Course 1 taught that as graphē. Here the writing He will not let them break is this psalm, including the verse that says they shall die like men. A school that empties 82:6 to make it safe has already decided the Lord should not have appealed to it. A school that detaches 82:6 from 82:7 has already made a slogan. Keep both. Keep His use. Write what you must not say.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write Psalm 82:6-7 and John 10:34-35 as one Scripture set. Then write what you must not say if you keep both verses and the Lord’s use of them.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Psalm 82:6-7 and John 10:34-36 in full. Sit the charge of blasphemy, the appeal, “unto whom the word of God came,” and “die like men.” Page 3: teach the verse as the Lord used it, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Refuse a slogan detached from the Word. Refuse a verse so emptied that the Lord could not have appealed to it.

Write in your own hand. Quote Psalm 82:6-7 and John 10:34-35. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
The verse as the Lord used it vs a slogan detached from the Word, or a verse so emptied that the Lord could not have appealed to it.

Charge
Write what you will teach: Psalm 82:6 with 82:7 and John 10; ye are gods, children of the most High; ye shall die like men; the scripture cannot be broken. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Why did Jesus come?
lessons.body:
Central principle
Jesus came because the glory was come short. He did not come to invent a different creature. He came that the man made in the image might be justified freely and set back on course.

Key Scripture
Romans 3:23-24.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section IV.

Teaching
Romans 3:23-26 — “For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”

The glory come short is deviation from true nature. This lesson will not let you answer “Why did Jesus come?” with a slogan that never names that glory. He came because all have sinned. He came because the image-bearer came short. Justification is already in the same breath: freely, by grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

He did not come to invent a different creature. He came that the man made in the image might be justified freely and set back on course. Genesis named the nature. 2 Peter 1:4 named the partaking. Romans 3:23 names the shortcoming. You will open 1 Corinthians 11:7 in the next lesson as the glory named here. Hold the question until you can answer it from these passages. Do not answer with a religious atmosphere you have learned to call glory.

God hath set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness; that He might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. The coming is not a mood. It is blood, propitiation, righteousness declared, the Just justifying the one who believes in Jesus. Why did Jesus come? Because the glory was come short. That is the answer. Write it from the verse.

Romans 3:21-22 has already set the righteousness of God without the law, witnessed by the law and the prophets; the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe; for there is no difference. Then: all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God. The glory come short is deviation from true nature — the nature Genesis named, the nature 2 Peter 1:4 makes you a partaker of. 1 Corinthians 11:7 will name that glory in the next lesson: man is the image and glory of God. Hold the question until you can put “glory” back on the verse.

Why did Jesus come? Because that glory was come short. He did not come to invent a different creature. He came that the image-bearer might be justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. God set Him forth a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness, that He might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Answer in terms of glory and true nature, not a slogan, not a religious atmosphere you have learned to call glory. Write Romans 3:23-24 and reason it.

All have sinned. There is no difference. The image-bearer came short. Justification is already in the same sentence as the shortcoming: freely, by grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Do not answer “Why did Jesus come?” with a sentence that never names that glory and never names that free justification. He came because the glory was come short. He came that the man made in the image might be set back on course. The next lesson will put 1 Corinthians 11:7 on that glory. Hold the question until the clause can sit with Romans 3:23.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Why did Jesus come? Answer in terms of glory and true nature, not a slogan. Write Romans 3:23-24 and reason it.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Romans 3:23-26 in full. Sit all have sinned, come short, justified freely, grace, redemption, propitiation, faith in His blood, just and justifier. Page 3: teach why He came, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Glory as true nature, not as a religious atmosphere. Hold 1 Corinthians 11:7 for the next lesson; name that it is coming.

Write in your own hand. Quote Romans 3:23-24. Answer why He came from these passages.

Distinction
Glory as true nature vs glory as a religious atmosphere.

Charge
Write what you will teach: Jesus came because the glory was come short; He did not come to invent a different creature; justified freely by grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Man the image and glory of God
lessons.body:
Central principle
Man is the image and glory of God. That is the glory Romans 3:23 says was come short.

Key Scripture
1 Corinthians 11:7.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section IV, the glory clause.

Teaching
1 Corinthians 11:7 — “For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.”

This lesson sets that clause as the glory named in Romans 3:23 — “For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.” Man “is the image and glory of God.” The glory come short is not a lost mood. It is deviation from the image and glory the text names.

The immediate context of the chapter is headship and covering in the assembly. Do not skip the verse because its chapter is contested. Foundation School teaches the clause. You are not being asked to reopen every dispute in 1 Corinthians 11. You are being asked to hear the identity clause: he is the image and glory of God.

Romans 3:23-24 remains in these passages: all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. The glory named in 3:23 is the glory 11:7 names. Jesus came because that glory was come short. He came that the man made in the image might be justified freely and set back on course.

Do not answer “what glory was come short?” with a word you cannot put back on the verse. If you cannot put “glory” back on 1 Corinthians 11:7 and Romans 3:23 together, you have not yet answered. Image and glory. Come short. Justified freely. That is the stretch.

1 Corinthians 11:3-7 is headship in the assembly: the head of every man is Christ; the head of the woman is the man; the head of Christ is God. A man praying or prophesying with his head covered dishonoureth his head. A man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God. Foundation School teaches that clause as the glory Romans 3:23 says was come short. You are not assigned every dispute in the chapter. You are assigned the identity: he is the image and glory of God.

What glory was come short? The image and glory of God that man is. Not a lost mood. Not a religious atmosphere. Deviation from that identity. Romans 3:24 is already in the same breath: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Jesus came because that glory was come short, that the man made in the image might be justified freely and set back on course. Write 1 Corinthians 11:7 with Romans 3:23 as one paragraph. If you cannot put “glory” back on both verses, you have not answered.

The chapter is contested in many rooms. Foundation School will not skip the clause because of that. Man is the image and glory of God. That is the glory come short. That is why Jesus came — not to invent a different creature, but that this man might be justified freely and set back on course. Do not answer with a word you cannot put back on 11:7 and 3:23 together. Image and glory. Come short. Justified freely. Write the paragraph.

Avoiding the verse because the chapter is argued is not Foundation School. Teaching the identity clause is. Man is the image and glory of God. That glory was come short. Jesus came because of that shortcoming. Hold the clause with Romans 3:23-24 until you can teach both as one stretch.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write 1 Corinthians 11:7 with Romans 3:23 as one paragraph. What glory was come short? Do not answer with a word you cannot put back on the verse.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write 1 Corinthians 11:7 and Romans 3:23-24 in full. Sit the clause in its chapter without skipping it, and sit the clause as the glory Romans names. Page 3: teach the identity clause, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Refuse avoiding the verse because the chapter is argued.

Write in your own hand. Quote 1 Corinthians 11:7 with Romans 3:23. The page is not a journal of feelings.

Distinction
The identity clause vs avoiding the verse because the chapter is argued.

Charge
Write what you will teach: man is the image and glory of God; that is the glory Romans 3:23 says was come short; the clause is taught, not skipped. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Dikaioō — justified freely
lessons.body:
Central principle
Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. Dikaioō: render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt.

Key Scripture
Romans 3:24-26.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section V.

Teaching
Has man been justified? Yes. And freely.

Romans 3:23-26 — “For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”

Justified: Greek dikaioō — render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt. A derivative of dikaiosynē: righteousness, justification. Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. God hath set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness; that He might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

Freely. By grace. Through redemption. Do not preach a justification you must finish by labour. Labour belongs to study (Chapter 1). Innocence before God is free in Christ. You will open apolutrōsis as ransom in full in its own lesson. Hold “through the redemption” here as the means already in the verse. You will open dikaiosynē as equity in its own lesson. Hold “righteousness” here as what God declares, as the Just who justifies.

Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. That answer will not let you add a remainder you must complete. That answer will not let you treat “freely” as a slogan and then charge a price. The justifier is just. He does not declare righteous by a fiction that has no Christ under it. He justifies the one who believes in Jesus.

Dikaioō: render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt. It is a derivative of dikaiosynē — righteousness, justification — which the next lesson will open as equity. Here the question is clear: Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Freely is not a slogan you chant while you add a remainder. Freely is the manner of the rendering.

God hath set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; to declare at this time His righteousness: that He might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. The justifier is just. He does not declare righteous by a fiction that has no Christ under it. He justifies the one who believes in Jesus. Labour belongs to study (Chapter 1). Innocence before God is free in Christ. Apolutrōsis will be named ransom in full in its own lesson. Hold “through the redemption” here. Write the answer: yes, and freely. Write what you must stop adding to “freely.”

Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. That is the answer, not a mood you work up. Dikaioō is render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt. You do not complete that rendering by religious work. You study as labour. You do not pay the rest of a price Christ finished. The justifier is just, and He is the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Stop adding to “freely.”

Write Romans 3:24-26. Name dikaioō as render just or innocent. Name freely, grace, redemption, propitiation, blood, just and justifier. If you add a remainder, you have not heard the answer.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Has man been justified? Write the answer: yes, and freely. Then write what you must stop adding to “freely.”

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Romans 3:23-26 in full. Define dikaioō: render just or innocent, free from evil or guilt. Page 3: teach freely, by grace, through redemption, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Labour belongs to study. Innocence before God is free in Christ.

Write in your own hand. Quote Romans 3:24-26. Scripture’s answer must be on the page.

Distinction
Justification as God’s free rendering vs a righteousness you complete by religious work.

Charge
Write what you will teach: has man been justified? Yes, and freely; dikaioō is render just or innocent; freely, by grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Dikaiosynē — equity; back on course
lessons.body:
Central principle
Dikaiosynē is equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God. Original: back on course.

Key Scripture
Romans 3:21-26 with 2 Peter 1:4.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, sections III and V, the equity sentences.

Teaching
Romans 3:21-26 — “But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”

Dikaiosynē is equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God. Original: back on course. Righteousness here is not a costume. It is conformity with the nature of God — the nature 2 Peter 1:4 named, the nature Genesis named.

2 Peter 1:4 — “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.”

Back on course. That is original. You are not being offered a new species. You are being set on the line from which sin turned you. The justifier is just. He does not declare righteous by a fiction that has no nature under it. He justifies the one who believes in Jesus, and the righteousness is conformity with His nature.

What course? The course Genesis named: image, likeness, dominion — true nature with respect to God. Whose nature? The nature of God, of which 2 Peter 1:4 makes you a partaker by the promises, having escaped the corruption. Equity is impartiality to that nature and conformity with it. A score you display is not this word. A costume you wear on a good day is not this word.

Romans 3:21-22 names the righteousness of God without the law, witnessed by the law and the prophets; by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe; no difference. That righteousness is dikaiosynē. The original sense is equity: impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God. Original: back on course. Not a costume. Not a score you display. Conformity with the nature 2 Peter 1:4 named — partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust — the nature Genesis named.

You are not being offered a new species. You are being set on the line from which sin turned you. The course is image, likeness, dominion — true nature with respect to God. The nature is God’s. The justifier is just: He does not declare righteous by a fiction that has no nature under it. He justifies the one who believes in Jesus, and the righteousness is conformity with His nature. Write what “back on course” means from dikaiosynē and 2 Peter 1:4 together. What course? Whose nature? Do not answer with a display.

Equity is impartiality to the nature of God and conformity with it. A costume is not impartiality. A score is not conformity. The righteousness of God is manifested without the law, witnessed by the law and the prophets, by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe. Back on course is original for that conformity: returned to the line Genesis named, in Christ, having escaped the corruption. Write the two questions from the verses.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write what “back on course” means from dikaiosynē and 2 Peter 1:4 together. What course? Whose nature?

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Romans 3:21-26 in full. Sit righteousness of God without the law, by faith of Jesus Christ, unto all and upon all that believe, declared, just and justifier. Page 3: write 2 Peter 1:4 again with the equity sentences. Teach dikaiosynē as conformity with God’s nature, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. What course, whose nature — on the page, from the verses.

Distinction
Equity as conformity with God’s nature vs righteousness as a score you display.

Charge
Write what you will teach: dikaiosynē is equity — impartiality to and conformity with the nature of God; original: back on course; not a costume; not a new species. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Apolutrōsis — ransom in full
lessons.body:
Central principle
There is no unpaid remainder on that ransom. Apolutrōsis: redemption; ransom in full.

Key Scripture
Romans 3:24.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section V, the ransom sentences.

Teaching
Romans 3:24-26 — “Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”

Justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Greek apolutrōsis — ransom in full. Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. Through a ransom that is not partial.

You cannot add a second payment and still call it this redemption. You cannot treat the blood as a deposit you must finish. Course 1 already laid Hebrews 9:14: the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without spot to God, purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God. This lesson names the ransom as full. Hold both.

There is no unpaid remainder on that ransom. Do not preach a justification you must finish by labour. Labour belongs to study (Chapter 1). Innocence before God is free in Christ. The propitiation is through faith in His blood. The righteousness declared is His. The justifier is just. A remainder you invent is not humility. It is a second price.

Shew apolutrōsis in Romans 3:24. The word is in the verse as redemption. The gloss is ransom in full. Write the verse. Write the gloss . Then stop adding.

Apolutrōsis in Romans 3:24 is the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. The gloss is ransom in full. Full will not bear a second payment. Full will not bear treating the blood as a deposit you must finish. Justified freely by His grace through that redemption. God set forth Christ a propitiation through faith in His blood. The righteousness declared is His. The justifier is just.

Hebrews 9:12-14 already sits from Course 1: by His own blood He entered in once, having obtained eternal redemption; the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God. Once. Eternal redemption. Ransom in full. There is no unpaid remainder. Do not preach a justification you must finish by labour. Labour belongs to study. Innocence before God is free in Christ. A remainder you invent is not humility. It is a second price. Show apolutrōsis in Romans 3:24. Write the verse. Write one sentence you will not say again if the ransom is in full.

Ransom in full means there is no unpaid remainder. You cannot add a second payment and still call it this redemption. You cannot treat the blood as a deposit. Course 1 laid Hebrews 9:14: the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works. This lesson names that ransom as full. Hold both. Labour belongs to study, not to finishing the price. Innocence before God is free in Christ. Write the sentence you will not say again.

Through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus — that is where apolutrōsis sits. Ransom in full. Propitiation through faith in His blood. No unpaid remainder. A second price, however religious, is not this verse. Hold Hebrews 9:14 with Romans 3:24: the blood purges; the ransom is full. Do not preach a justification you must finish. Has man been justified? Yes. And freely. Through a ransom that is not partial.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Show apolutrōsis in Romans 3:24. Write the verse. Then write one sentence you will not say again if the ransom is in full.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write Romans 3:24-26 in full. Sit freely, grace, redemption, propitiation, blood, just and justifier. Page 3: hold Hebrews 9:14 with this ransom. Teach ransom in full versus a redemption that still leaves you to complete the price, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student.

Write in your own hand. Quote Romans 3:24. The sentence you will not say must be on the page.

Distinction
Ransom in full vs a redemption that still leaves you to complete the price.

Charge
Write what you will teach: apolutrōsis is redemption, ransom in full; justified freely through that redemption; no unpaid remainder; labour belongs to study, not to finishing the price. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: You are the dikaiosynē of God now
lessons.body:
Central principle
So right now, you are the dikaiosynē of God in Christ. Present tense. Not an aspiration you visit on a good day.

Key Scripture
2 Corinthians 5:21.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section VI.

Teaching
2 Corinthians 5:21 — “For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.”

The present tense stands: right now, you are the dikaiosynē of God in Christ. This is not an aspiration you visit on a good day. It is the state pistis credits. Course 1 laid the new creature — 2 Corinthians 5:17: if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. This lesson names the righteousness of that creature.

He hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin. The One who knew no sin was made sin for us. The purpose clause is not a wish: that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. In Him. Not beside Him on a good day. Not after you have finished a remainder. Romans 3:24 remains in these passages: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Freely. Now. In Christ.

Pistis credits this state. It does not wait for a mood to confirm it. The next lesson will ask, according to Hebrews 1:8, what that makes you. Do not invent the answer here. Hold the verse until you can reason from these passages. “Right now” forbids you to say about yourself, if you are in Him, that you are still only hoping to become what 5:21 says you were made.

2 Corinthians 5:17-21 is one movement. If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away; all things are become new. All things are of God, who hath reconciled us to Himself by Jesus Christ. He hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. The new creature and the righteousness of God in Him are not two gospels. Course 1 laid the creature. This lesson names the righteousness of that creature.

The present tense stands: right now, you are the dikaiosynē of God in Christ. Not an aspiration you visit on a good day. Not a costume you wear when the mood confirms it. Pistis credits this state. Romans 3:24 remains: justified freely through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. “Right now” forbids you to say, if you are in Him, that you are still only hoping to become what 5:21 says you were made. The next lesson will ask, according to Hebrews 1:8, what that makes you. Do not invent the answer here. Write 5:21. Write what “right now” forbids.

He knew no sin. He was made sin for us. That we might be made the righteousness of God in Him. In Him — not beside Him on a good day, not after a remainder, not when a mood confirms it. The present tense will not let you visit this as an aspiration. Pistis credits it now. The next lesson will ask what Hebrews 1:8 makes of that. Hold 5:21 until you can reason. Do not invent a title here.

The present tense stands: right now, you are the dikaiosynē of God in Christ. A future costume is not this verse. A good-day visit is not this verse. The new creature Course 1 laid is the man of whom 5:21 speaks. Write what “right now” forbids you to say if you are in Him.

Labour
The Walk: write one tight page. Intensive: write three pages on the same Scripture set. The doctrine is the same.

The Walk — one page. Write 2 Corinthians 5:21. Then write what “right now” forbids you to say about yourself if you are in Him.

Intensive — three pages. Page 1 is that tight page. Page 2: write 2 Corinthians 5:17 and 5:21 together. Sit new creature and righteousness of God in Him. Add Romans 3:24. Page 3: teach present righteousness in Christ versus righteousness as a future costume, as if you had to teach it clearly to another student. Do not invent the Hebrews 1:8 title here. Name that the next lesson will ask the question.

Write in your own hand. Quote 2 Corinthians 5:21. What “right now” forbids must be on the page.

Distinction
Present righteousness in Christ vs righteousness as a future costume.

Charge
Write what you will teach: he was made sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him; right now, you are the dikaiosynē of God in Christ. Then complete the practice assignment.

lessons.title: Hebrews 1:8 — what does that make you?
lessons.body:
Central principle
After 2 Corinthians 5:21, the question is: according to Hebrews 1:8, what does that make you? The lesson does not print the answer. Reason from these passages. Do not invent a title.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 1:8; Hebrews 1:3.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 3, section VII.

Teaching
Hebrews 1:1-8 — “God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high; Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
