What you are still coming unto: the unity of the faith, the knowledge of the Son of God, a perfect man, the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. Hold both. Do not chase a fullness as if He were empty. Do not pretend Ephesians 4:13 has already been finished because Colossians 2:10 is true.

The savour of Christ — to one death, to one life. Triumph in Christ. Manifest the savour of His knowledge. This is not a meeting-cry. It is the son in the world held under fullness. Crucified with Christ is baptism 1 still speaking. Complete in Him is not a second saviour. It is the same Christ.

Without measure and fullness sit together. Lesson 3-12 forbade stingy measure-talk. This lesson forbids emptiness-talk. You are complete in Him. You are still coming unto the measure of the stature of His fullness. A babe can hold both if you will not flatten one to save a slogan.

It pleased the Father. All fullness dwells in Him. Godhead bodily. Head of all principality and power. Ye are complete in Him — not complete in a meeting, not complete in a second slogan. Members in particular. I live; yet not I; Christ liveth in me; the life I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God. Always causeth us to triumph in Christ. Savour of His knowledge in every place. To the one, death; to the other, life. Who is sufficient for these things?

Till we all come — unity of the faith, knowledge of the Son of God, a perfect man. That “till” does not undo “ye are complete in Him.” It names what the body is still coming unto. Fullness is the son, whelmed, witnessing, complete. Not a slogan for a meeting.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Colossians 2:9-10 and Ephesians 4:13. What is already true in Him, and what are you still coming unto? Hold both. Word drill: fullness / complete / stature / body / Christ liveth in me.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write the full fullness-in-Christ Scripture set in KJV quoted above. Page 2: already true in Him — complete, body, crucified, savour, power and wisdom. Page 3: still coming unto — unity, knowledge, perfect man, measure of the stature; write the chase you will stop if He is not empty. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Complete in Him vs a fullness you chase as if He were empty.

Charge
Write Colossians 2:9-10 and Ephesians 4:13. What is already true in Him, and what are you still coming unto? Hold both.

lessons.title: Not slaves — you are the fear and dread
lessons.body:
Central principle
Not slaves. Not timidity. God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. It is not possible for you to fear. You are the fear and dread.

Key Scripture
Galatians 4:6-7; 2 Timothy 1:7; Genesis 9:2; Deuteronomy 11:25.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 4, section XIV.

Teaching
Because ye are sons… no more a servant, but a son; if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. You rather are the fear and dread of the world: thieves and all wickedness alike, demons and Satan inclusive.

Galatians 4:6-7. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

2 Timothy 1:7. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

Genesis 9:2. And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.

Deuteronomy 11:25. There shall no man be able to stand before you: for the LORD your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.

Romans 8:17. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

Genesis 1:26-28. And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

Psalm 139:14. I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

Heir. Image. Fearfully and wonderfully made. Foundation School will not soften that charge for babes. We do not teach James 2:9 as these passages. James 2:9 is not the governing text here. Fear and dread are Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. Further reading when the volume is in your hand: Why We’re Beyond — its own book, not Fearfully Made.

Do not turn the charge into a boastful claim without these passages. Power, and love, and a sound mind stand in the same breath. A man who boasts without Abba, without heir, without image, without 2 Timothy 1:7, has not heard the charge. A man who softens the charge into timidity God did not give has not heard it either. It is not possible for you to fear — as Foundation School teaches it. You are the fear and dread.

The LORD your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you. Into your hand are they delivered. Dominion was spoken in Genesis 1:26-28. Course 2 already forbade a safer verse in the place of that making. This lesson will not put a safer verse in the place of Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Teach 2 Timothy 1:7 with Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. Write the three texts. Do not submit a boastful claim, and do not submit a softer sentence the Aletheia teaching forbids. Word drill: not slaves / not the spirit of fear / you are the fear and dread.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write the full Scripture set in KJV quoted above. Page 2: heir, image, fearfully made — with Galatians 4:6-7 and Romans 8:17; Why We’re Beyond is its own book, not Fearfully Made; James 2:9 is not the governing text here. Page 3: power, love, and a sound mind in the same breath as the fear and dread — write the boastful error you will refuse and the softening you will refuse. The doctrine is the same. Do not soften the doctrine. Do not boast without these passages.

Distinction
Son (Abba, heir, informant Spirit) vs slave (timidity). You are the fear and dread vs a spirit of fear God did not give.

Charge
Teach 2 Timothy 1:7 with Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. Write the three texts. Do not submit a boastful claim, and do not submit a softer sentence the Aletheia teaching forbids.

lessons.title: Anangellō — He shall shew you Mine
lessons.body:
Central principle
The Spirit of truth guides into all truth. He shall receive of Mine and shew it unto you. Mine is the express image — Genesis 1:26-28.

Key Scripture
John 16:13-15; Genesis 1:26-28.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 4, section XV.

Teaching
When He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will guide you into all truth: for He shall not speak of Himself. He shall glorify Me: for He shall receive of Mine, and shall shew it unto you. All things that the Father hath are Mine.

John 16:13-15. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you. All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall shew it unto you.

Genesis 1:26-28. And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

Anangellō: to announce in detail — declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell. Mine: the express image of God, announced unto you — express image and likeness of Me (Genesis 1:26-28). The Spirit does not invent another image. He shews what Course 2 already named. He glorifies the Son. He does not speak of Himself.

A private revelation that never returns to Genesis 1:26-28 is not this shewing. The Spirit of truth guides into all truth. Whatsoever He shall hear, that shall He speak. He will shew you things to come. He shall glorify Me. He shall receive of Mine. All things the Father hath are Mine; therefore He takes of Mine and shews it. This lesson ties Mine to the express image and likeness. Write the likeness from the words. Do not invent a title these passages do not grant.

Further reading when the volume is in your hand: Spirit Witness — its own book, not a volume of Presence of Sons 1–4. If a catalogue once set the titles near each other, that proximity is bibliographic, not a series assignment. Completing this course does not require finishing every page of the library. Directed sections when the volumes are in your hand.

Course 2 taught image and likeness as written. This lesson will not hedge that making. The Spirit announces it in detail. He rehearses it. He reports it. He shews it. Man made in the image, after the likeness, given dominion — that is Mine as Foundation School ties John 16 to Genesis 1. The Spirit glorifies the Son who is the image; He shews you that you were made after that likeness. He does not speak of Himself as a rival image.

Whatsoever He shall hear, that shall He speak. Things to come. All things the Father hath are Mine; therefore He takes of Mine and shews it. anangellō is not a private language. Declare. Rehearse. Report. Show. Speak. Tell. In detail. If what you call “the Spirit shewed me” never returns to image, likeness, and dominion, it is not this Mine. Let us make man. So God created. Male and female. Blessed them. Be fruitful. Multiply. Replenish. Subdue. Have dominion. Write the likeness from those words. Do not invent a safer verse.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. What is “Mine” in John 16:14-15 as Foundation School ties it to Genesis 1:26-28? Write both. Write the likeness from the words. Word drill: anangellō — announce in detail; declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write John 16:13-15 and Genesis 1:26-28 in full; mark guide, not of Himself, glorify, Mine, shew, image, likeness, dominion. Page 2: anangellō: announce in detail, declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell. Mine as express image — not a private revelation that never returns to Genesis 1:26-28. Page 3: Spirit Witness is its own book, not Presence of Sons; write what you will not let a catalogue proximity become. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Mine as the image announced vs a private revelation that never returns to Genesis 1:26-28.

Charge
What is “Mine” in John 16:14-15 as Foundation School ties it to Genesis 1:26-28? Write both. Write the likeness from the words.

lessons.title: Charge and examination of the principle
lessons.body:
Central principle
The third stone is laid when a man can name the three essential baptisms, keep “one baptism” as the only one that saves the soul, keep water as the figure after salvation, and keep the Spirit as witness of the son — without measure, not a slave.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:2; Ephesians 4:5; 1 Peter 3:21; Galatians 3:26-27; Galatians 4:6-7; John 16:13-14.

Read
Chapter 4, section XVI. Directed reading when the volumes are in your hand — assigned sections only, not a second course: Spirit Witness; Why We’re Beyond.

Teaching
This lesson is the examination of the principle, not a new doctrine. These passages of the year on this stone is the texts already opened. Write them again.

Hebrews 6:2. Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Ephesians 4:5. One Lord, one faith, one baptism.

1 Peter 3:21. The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

Galatians 3:26-27. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

Galatians 4:6-7. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

John 16:13-14. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.

You should now be able to teach, from Scripture:

1. Baptismos as washing; Hebrews 6:2 as baptisms — the plural. The Word as agency of new birth (Ephesians 5:26; 1 Peter 1:23; John 3:5).
2. Seven in Scripture; three for believers, in order: into Christ, water after, Spirit. Three agents. Baptizō from baptō, regardless of the element.
3. Into Christ — one baptism; the only one that saves the soul. Whelmed; put on Christ; Romans 6; Colossians 2; 1 Corinthians 12:13. The Spirit the agent of this one.
4. Water after one is saved — sign, not object. 1 Peter 3:21 — is it the water, or what it figures? The cross, not water, is power (1 Corinthians 1:17-24). Galatians 3:26 with 3:27 in one paragraph.
5. Spirit as witness of sonship; prerequisite new birth; enduement with the witness, not instead of it. Before water or after it. Christ the agent.
6. Without measure; unto Him in the sentence; unto you in the application given here. Fullness; complete in Him; still coming unto the stature.
7. Not slaves; power, love, sound mind; you are the fear and dread (Genesis 9:2; Deuteronomy 11:25). Not James 2:9. Anangellō; Mine; Genesis 1:26-28.

Companions are not a seventh course. Spirit Witness is not a volume of Presence of Sons. Why We’re Beyond is not Fearfully Made. The next principle is laying on of hands. It is resultant. It is not a substitute for these three stones. It does not cancel Christ as Spirit-baptizer.

Charges 20–25 are the examination summary. Name the three essential; do not invent the four; why “one baptism” does not cancel water and Spirit. Is it the water that saves, or what it figures — 1 Peter 3:21 with 1 Corinthians 1:17-18. Hold Galatians 3:26 with 3:27. Who is the Spirit sent into (Galatians 4:6)? Teach 2 Timothy 1:7 with Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25 — not James 2:9, not a boastful claim without these passages, not a softer sentence. What is Mine — John 16:14-15 with Genesis 1:26-28. Do not submit a feeling in the place of these passages.

Baptizō from baptō remains: dip; overwhelm with suffering; bury into — regardless of the element. Three agents remain: Spirit into Christ; Christ in the Spirit; minister in water. Unto Him in John 3:34’s sentence; the Spirit not by measure unto you in the application given here. Directed sections of the companions when the volumes are in your hand. Completing this course does not require finishing every page of the library.

Labour
The Walk — thirteen tight paragraphs: one on each of the thirteen heads named in the thin charge of this course, using the verses above. The doctrine is the same. Not thirteen new teachings. Then answer Charge 20–Charge 25 from these passages, not from a heading.

Intensive — a full page on each of the thirteen heads. Use the same passages. The doctrine is the same. Do not invent a fourteenth baptism to fill the hours. Then write the examination answers from the Charge without a feeling in the place of these passages. Page the three agents and the seven; page the 1 Peter 3:21 question; page Genesis 9:2 with Deuteronomy 11:25. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Completion of activities vs mastery. Directed companion sections vs treating those books as this course.

Charge
Name the three essential. Why does “one baptism” not cancel water and Spirit? Is it the water that saves, or what it figures? Hold Galatians 3:26 with 3:27. Who is the Spirit sent into? Teach 2 Timothy 1:7 with Genesis 9:2 and Deuteronomy 11:25. What is Mine? Do not submit a feeling in the place of these passages.

lessons.title: Resultant, not the foundation
lessons.body:
Central principle
Laying on of hands is among the first principles. It is rightly practiced only after the earlier foundations are laid. It follows those foundations; it does not establish the believer.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:2 — and of laying on of hands.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section I.

Teaching
This is Course 4 of Foundation School. One curriculum. The fourth of the six principles. When? Nine occasions. This lesson is not yet the nine. This lesson is why “when?” comes after Courses 1–3.

Hebrews 6:1-2. Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Hands do not invent the son. Hands do not replace metanoia. Hands do not replace pistis. Hands do not replace baptism into Christ, water as figure, or the Spirit as witness. A man who has not laid those stones and then treats hands as if they were the house has not heard “when?”

The principle is among the first principles. Hebrews 6:2 names it in the same breath as baptisms, resurrection, and eternal judgment. The same verse is cited again under imparting gifts. The principle is real. The role is not the house. Do not skip the nine because they are resultant. Do not make the nine a substitute for the three stones already laid.

Course 3 named three essential baptisms. Into Christ saves the soul. Water is the figure after one is saved. The Spirit is witness of sonship and enduement; Christ is the baptizer in the Spirit. This course will show hands in certain accounts of Spirit baptism. Those accounts do not cancel Christ as Spirit-baptizer. They do not make hands the foundation. They are the ninth occasion, after “when?” has been heard.

Foundation School names no required companion here. Directed reading later, if a volume is assigned. Completing this chapter does not wait on a book Foundation School does not name. Companions are not a seventh course. Course 4 has no required companion.

Laying on of hands is rightly practiced only after the earlier foundations are laid: repentance from dead works, faith toward God, and the doctrine of baptisms. It follows those foundations; it does not establish the believer. A practice you have been using to replace those stones is not this principle. Name it in the charge and put it down. The nine will still be nine. They will not become the house.

Leaving the first principles is not forgetting them. It is not laying them again once they are laid. A man who never laid repentance, faith, and baptisms is not leaving them when he runs to hands. He is skipping them. Hebrews 6:1-2 will not let you treat the fourth name as the first house.

The six are named in order. Repentance from dead works. Faith toward God. The doctrine of baptisms. Then laying on of hands. Then resurrection. Then eternal judgment. “When?” is answered after the first three foundations are laid. The principle is real. The role follows; it does not establish the believer. Do not skip the nine because they are resultant. Do not make the nine the house.

The question is, When? The answer is nine occasions, each with its own text, practiced only after the earlier foundations are laid. This lesson will not preview Genesis 48 as if blessing men were the definition of the principle. It will not preview Acts 8 as if Spirit baptism by hands were the definition. It will hold “when?” until the three stones are named as already necessary. Course 4 has no required companion. Do not invent a required companion to make the course feel like Courses 1–3.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? Name the three that stand before this one. Write what you have been using hands to replace. Word drill: resultant / not the foundation / when?

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Hebrews 6:1-2 in full; reason the order — repentance, faith, baptisms, then hands. Page 2: what hands do not replace — metanoia, pistis, into Christ, water as figure, Spirit as witness; Christ remains Spirit-baptizer. Page 3: no required companion; write the practice you will not treat as the house. The doctrine is the same. Do not invent a tenth occasion to make the lesson longer.

Distinction
Resultant practice vs foundation. The principle is real. The role is not the house.

Charge
Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? Name the three that stand before this one. Write what you have been using hands to replace.

lessons.title: Blessing men — Genesis 48:14
lessons.body:
Central principle
Israel laid his hands on Ephraim and Manasseh and blessed Joseph’s sons. The first occasion is blessing men.

Key Scripture
Genesis 48:14.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section II.

Teaching
Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn. The blessing is spoken. The hands are laid. Joseph objects. Israel will not uncross them.

Genesis 48:8-20. And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who are these? And Joseph said unto his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them. Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them. And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed. And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth. And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near unto him. And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn. And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head unto Manasseh’s head. And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head. And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.

Who lays hands? Israel. On whom? Ephraim and Manasseh — Joseph’s sons. What is spoken? The blessing of the God of Abraham and Isaac; the Angel which redeemed him; name and multitude. The hands are guided wittingly. The younger receives the right hand. Joseph would uncross them. Israel will not.

This is blessing men — not a technique you copy without the God who spoke to the patriarch. Do not turn the crossed hands into a tenth system. The occasion is the first in the teaching because Foundation School names it first. It is not ordaining. It is not healing. It is not imparting Spirit baptism. Blessing men remains blessing men.

Eyes dim for age. He kissed them and embraced them. He blessed Joseph and the lads. I know it, my son, I know it. The account will not be reduced to a manual of gestures. The God who fed him all his life long is in the mouth of the blessing. If you submit a method in the place of the account, you have left this lesson's Scripture.

Who are these? My sons, whom God hath given me in this place. Bring them, and I will bless them. God hath shewed me also thy seed. Joseph bows. Joseph arranges Ephraim toward Israel’s left and Manasseh toward his right. Israel crosses them wittingly. The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads. Let my name be named on them. Grow into a multitude. Joseph displeased; he would remove the right hand. Not so, my father. Israel refused. The younger shall be greater. He set Ephraim before Manasseh. That is the teaching for this lesson. Not a tenth system. Not Course 1. Blessing men.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Genesis 48:14. Who lays hands? On whom? What is spoken? Do not submit a method in the place of the account. Word drill: blessing men / guided wittingly / the younger and the right hand.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Genesis 48:8-20 in full; mark who, whom, the blessing spoken, the objection, the refusal. Page 2: blessing men as the account stands — not ordaining, not healing, not a tenth system from the crossed hands. Page 3: write the method you will not submit in the place of this account. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Blessing men as the account stands vs a ritual you invent from the gesture.

Charge
Write Genesis 48:14. Who lays hands? On whom? What is spoken? Do not submit a method in the place of the account.

lessons.title: Offerings — Numbers 8:10
lessons.body:
Central principle
The children of Israel put their hands upon the Levites. The Levites are offered before the Lord. This is making offerings.

Key Scripture
Numbers 8:10.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section III.

Teaching
Thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites. The hands serve the offering God commanded. Identification and presentation. They do not invent a priesthood, and they do not replace the grounding principles with a ceremony.

Numbers 8:5-15. And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them. And thus shalt thou do unto them, to cleanse them: Sprinkle water of purifying upon them, and let them shave all their flesh, and let them wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean. Then let them take a young bullock with his meat offering, even fine flour mingled with oil, and another young bullock shalt thou take for a sin offering. And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt gather the whole assembly of the children of Israel together: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites: And Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD for an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD. And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the heads of the bullocks: and thou shalt offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, unto the LORD, to make an atonement for the Levites. And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them for an offering unto the LORD. Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine. And after that shall the Levites go in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt cleanse them, and offer them for an offering.

What is being offered? The Levites. Before whom? The LORD. Who put their hands upon them? The children of Israel — the whole assembly gathered. Aaron offers the Levites for an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD. The Levites then lay their hands upon the bullocks. Separation: the Levites shall be mine.

This is making offerings — identification and presentation — not a private ritual invented in a meeting. The hands here serve the offering God commanded. They do not invent a priesthood. Moses is told; the LORD speaks; the assembly is gathered; the tabernacle is the place. A meeting that invents hands-as-offering without this command has left this lesson's Scripture.

Do not flatten this occasion into blessing men. Genesis 48 was patriarch and lads and a spoken blessing. Numbers 8 is congregation, Levites, offering, service. Each occasion stays distinct. Do not make this a substitute for baptism into Christ. The Levites are offered after they are cleansed as the LORD said. The grounding stones are not this ceremony.

The LORD spake unto Moses. Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them. Water of purifying, shave, wash, bullock, meat offering, sin offering. Whole assembly gathered before the tabernacle. Hands of the children of Israel upon the Levites. Aaron offers them that they may execute the service of the LORD. Levites’ hands on the bullocks. Separate them; they shall be mine. After that they go in to do the service. That is making offerings. A private ritual in a meeting that never heard this command is not this lesson. Hands here identify and present what God named. They do not invent a priesthood the LORD did not speak.

What is being offered? The Levites. Before whom? The LORD. The children of Israel put their hands upon them. That is the teaching for this lesson. Not blessing men. Not ordaining Joshua. Not a ceremony that replaces baptism into Christ. Each occasion stays distinct.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Numbers 8:10. What is being offered, and before whom? What must you not let this occasion become? Word drill: offerings / identification / presentation / before the LORD.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Numbers 8:5-15 in full; mark cleanse, assembly, hands on the Levites, Aaron’s offering, bullocks, mine. Page 2: making offerings as commanded — not a private ritual; not a priesthood invented by hands. Page 3: write what you will not let this occasion become in a meeting. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Hands on the offered vs a private ritual invented in a meeting.

Charge
Write Numbers 8:10. What is being offered, and before whom? What must you not let this occasion become?

lessons.title: Ordaining — Numbers 27:18, 23
lessons.body:
Central principle
Joshua is already a man in whom is the spirit. Moses lays his hand and gives him a charge. Ordaining does not create the Spirit in the man.

Key Scripture
Numbers 27:18, 23.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section IV.

Teaching
The LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. He laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses. The Spirit is already named in the man before the hand. The charge is given as the LORD commanded. Before the priest. Before all the congregation.

Numbers 27:15-23. And Moses spake unto the LORD, saying, Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the LORD be not as sheep which have no shepherd. And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him; And set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight. And thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient. And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation. And Moses did as the LORD commanded him: and he took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation: And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.

What is already true of Joshua before the hand? He is a man in whom is the spirit. What does the hand do? It is laid; a charge is given in their sight; some of Moses’ honour is put upon him; the congregation may be obedient. Moses did as the LORD commanded. The text will not let you make ordination a substitute for the Spirit already in the man.

Do not flatten this into Deuteronomy 34:9. That verse is the next occasion: imparting Spirit — Joshua full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Hold both. Do not invent a tenth occasion to sit between them. In this lesson: ordaining. A man in whom is the spirit. Charge. Before Eleazar. Before all the congregation. Sheep who have a shepherd.

The LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, sets the man. Moses asks. The LORD names Joshua. The hand follows the naming. If you treat hands as the creator of what God has not put in, you have left Numbers 27:18. Course 3 already taught that the Spirit is not sent into a man who has not been made a son. This occasion will not become a back door around that prerequisite.

That the congregation be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Go out, go in, lead out, bring in. Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; give him a charge in their sight. Put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation may be obedient. Urim before the LORD. At his word shall they go out and come in. Moses did as the LORD commanded. He took Joshua. He laid his hands. He gave him a charge. Ordaining here is charge, not creation of the Spirit. Deuteronomy 34:9 will say what it will say. Do not steal that verse into this lesson to flatten the teaching.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Numbers 27:18 and 27:23. What is already true of Joshua before the hand? What does the hand do? Word drill: a man in whom is the spirit / charge / as the LORD commanded.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Numbers 27:15-23 in full; mark the request, the naming, the spirit already in the man, Eleazar, congregation, honour, charge. Page 2: ordaining does not create the Spirit — write the substitute you will refuse. Page 3: hold Numbers 27 beside Deuteronomy 34 without flattening; do not invent a tenth to explain them. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Charge laid on a man in whom is the spirit vs hands creating what God has not put in.

Charge
Write Numbers 27:18 and 27:23. What is already true of Joshua before the hand? What does the hand do?

lessons.title: Imparting the Spirit — Deuteronomy 34:9
lessons.body:
Central principle
Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. The occasion is imparting Spirit.

Key Scripture
Deuteronomy 34:9.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section V.

Teaching
Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

Deuteronomy 34:9. And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

Numbers 27:18. And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.

Numbers 27:23. And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.

Hold this next to Numbers 27. Joshua was a man in whom is the spirit before the charge; he is full of the spirit of wisdom after the hands. Do not flatten the two texts into one slogan. Do not invent a tenth occasion to explain them. Numbers 27 remains ordaining. Deuteronomy 34 remains imparting Spirit. The same Joshua. Two verses. Two things said.

What does Deuteronomy 34:9 force you to say that Numbers 27:18 does not say? He was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Israel hearkened. They did as the LORD commanded Moses. What does Numbers 27:18 force you to say that Deuteronomy 34:9 does not say? He was already a man in whom is the spirit before the hand. The charge is given in their sight. Some of Moses’ honour is put upon him.

The fruit of the occasion is not a feeling in Moses. It is a people who hear the man charged. Hearkened. Did as the LORD commanded Moses. If you measure this occasion by a sensation in the one who laid hands, you have left the verse.

This is not Christian baptism in the Spirit as Course 3 named it — Christ the baptizer; witness of sonship; prerequisite new birth. This is the fourth occasion in the hands teaching: imparting Spirit, as Deuteronomy 34:9 states it. Course 3 is not cancelled. A tenth “bridge” occasion is not required to keep both courses. Teach the verse. Teach it beside Numbers 27. Do not add another occasion.

Full of the spirit of wisdom — for Moses had laid his hands upon him. The “for” is in the verse. Foundation School will not delete it to protect these passages, and will not delete these passages to protect the “for.” Already a man in whom is the spirit. Then full of the spirit of wisdom, for the hands. Two sentences. One Joshua. Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses. The fruit is a hearing people, not a sensation in the one who laid hands.

Do not invent a tenth occasion named “the gap between spirit and wisdom.” Do not collapse both verses into “ordination equals Spirit.” Course 3’s agent remains Christ for baptism in the Holy Spirit. This occasion remains Deuteronomy 34:9. When? After the grounding things. Hands do not become the house because this verse used “for.”

Write Deuteronomy 34:9 beside Numbers 27:18. What does each force you to say that the other does not say? Already a man in whom is the spirit. Then full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands. Israel hearkened. The fruit is not a feeling in Moses. Two texts. No tenth between them. No flatten.

Numbers 27 remains ordaining: charge, Eleazar, congregation, honour, as the LORD commanded. Deuteronomy 34 remains imparting Spirit: full of the spirit of wisdom, for the hands. Same Joshua. Do not steal either verse into the other lesson. Course 3 is not cancelled. Christ remains the baptizer in the Holy Spirit. This is the fourth occasion in the hands teaching, as the verse states it.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Deuteronomy 34:9 beside Numbers 27:18. What does each verse force you to say that the other does not say? Word drill: full of the spirit of wisdom / for Moses had laid his hands / hearkened.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Deuteronomy 34:9 and Numbers 27:18, 23 in full; two columns — already true / after the hands. Page 2: do not flatten; do not invent a tenth; Israel hearkened is the fruit, not a feeling in Moses. Page 3: this occasion does not cancel Course 3 — Christ remains Spirit-baptizer. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Imparting Spirit as the verse states it vs collapsing Deuteronomy 34 into Numbers 27, or inventing a tenth to sit between them.

Charge
Write Deuteronomy 34:9 beside Numbers 27:18. What does each verse force you to say that the other does not say?

lessons.title: Blessing children — Matthew 19:13-15
lessons.body:
Central principle
He laid His hands on the children. The disciples rebuked the bringing. The Lord would not.

Key Scripture
Matthew 19:13-15.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section VI.

Teaching
Then were there brought unto Him little children, that He should put His hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto Me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And He laid His hands on them, and departed thence.

Matthew 19:13-15. Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.

Matthew 19:15 names the laying on of hands, and the full account is 13-15. He laid His hands on them. The disciples rebuked the bringing. The Lord would not. This is blessing children — not a dedication invented to replace new birth, and not a small thing you skip because the children are small.

What did the disciples do? They rebuked them that brought the children. What did the Lord do? He said suffer and forbid them not; of such is the kingdom of heaven; He laid His hands on them; He departed. What must you not let this occasion replace? Course 1. Receive Him. New birth. A rite that pretends to be repentance and faith for a child is not this lesson. Blessing children is blessing children.

He should put His hands on them, and pray. The bringing had a request: hands and prayer. The rebuke met that request. The Lord met the children. Of such is the kingdom of heaven is His sentence, not a slogan you paste on a ceremony He did not invent. He laid His hands on them. Then He departed thence. The account is short. Do not lengthen it with a system.

Do not flatten this into healing. Mark 6 and Mark 16 and Acts 5 are another occasion. Do not flatten this into blessing men. Genesis 48 is patriarch and Joseph’s sons. Little children brought to Jesus is these passages. Each occasion stays distinct. Nine. No tenth.

Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto Me. The disciples’ rebuke is in the text so that you will not repeat it and call it order. Of such is the kingdom of heaven. He laid His hands on them. He departed thence. Teach the full account in Matthew 19:13-15. Hands and prayer were the bringing’s request. The Lord met it without inventing a dedication that replaces new birth.

Course 1 remains receive Him. A child is not saved by this occasion as if it were baptism into Christ. A child is not too small for the Lord to lay hands on. Skip this because they are small and you have taken the disciples’ part. Invent a rite that pretends to be repentance and faith and you have left this lesson's Scripture for a tenth. Blessing children as the Lord did. That is the occasion.

The disciples rebuked the bringing. The Lord said suffer, forbid them not, of such is the kingdom of heaven. He laid His hands on them. He departed. Matthew 19:13-15 is these passages, not 19:15 alone. Not healing. Not blessing men. Not Course 1. This occasion remains blessing children.

He should put His hands on them, and pray. That was the bringing. The rebuke met the bringing. The Lord met the children. Of such is the kingdom of heaven is His sentence, not a slogan pasted on a dedication He did not invent. Do not skip this because the children are small. Do not replace new birth with this occasion. Blessing children as the Lord did. Nine. No tenth.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Matthew 19:13-15. What did the disciples do? What did the Lord do? What must you not let this occasion replace? Word drill: suffer / forbid them not / laid His hands / of such is the kingdom.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Matthew 19:13-15 in full; mark brought, hands, pray, rebuked, suffer, forbid not, kingdom, laid, departed. Page 2: blessing children — not Course 1 for a child; not a small thing skipped because they are small. Page 3: not healing, not blessing men — write the flattening error you will refuse. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Blessing children as the Lord did vs a rite that pretends to be Course 1 for a child.

Charge
Write Matthew 19:13-15. What did the disciples do? What did the Lord do? What must you not let this occasion replace?

lessons.title: Healing — Mark 6:2, 5; 16:18; Acts 5:12
lessons.body:
Central principle
Mighty works by His hands. He laid His hands on a few sick and healed them. They shall lay hands on the sick. By the hands of the apostles many signs.

Key Scripture
Mark 6:2, 5; Mark 16:18; Acts 5:12.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section VII.

Teaching
Nazareth: many were astonished that such mighty works were wrought by His hands. He could there do no mighty work, save that He laid His hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. The risen Lord’s word: they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover. Acts 5:12 — by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people.

Mark 6:2. And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?

Mark 6:5. And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.

Mark 16:18. They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

Acts 5:12. And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people; (and they were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch.

Four texts. One occasion. Healing the sick. What unbelief did in Nazareth: He could there do no mighty work — save that He laid His hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. The hands still did that. Astonishment at wisdom and mighty works by His hands sits in the same town that would not receive a mighty work beyond those few. Teach both sentences. Do not preach only the limit. Do not preach only the few as if Mark 6:2 had not named mighty works by His hands.

The risen Lord includes laying hands on the sick among the signs that follow them that believe. They shall recover. The apostles’ hands wrought many signs and wonders among the people. Solomon’s porch. One accord. This is not a substitute for repentance, faith, or baptism into Christ. It is an occasion in the teaching. Teach the texts. Do not invent a tenth healing system beside them.

A healing brand that no longer needs the verses has left this lesson's Scripture. Four references. One sentence each in The Walk charge. The occasion is healing — not miracles as Acts 19:11 will name them, not blessing children, not imparting gifts. Mark 16:18 has more in the verse than hands on the sick. This text belongs to healing in this lesson. Keep that distinction. Do not build a tenth category from the rest of the verse.

He began to teach in the synagogue. Many hearing Him were astonished. From whence hath this man these things? What wisdom is this which is given unto Him, that even such mighty works are wrought by His hands? Then the limit: He could there do no mighty work, save the few sick healed by His hands. Unbelief in Nazareth did not erase the hands; it limited what it would receive. The risen word still says they shall recover. The apostles still wrought signs and wonders by their hands among the people.

This is not a substitute for repentance, faith, or baptism into Christ. A man healed who has not been baptized into Christ has not laid the third stone. Resultant. Teach the four texts. No tenth healing system. No brand that no longer needs Mark 6:2, 6:5, 16:18, and Acts 5:12.

Write the four references with one sentence each. What unbelief did in Nazareth: no mighty work, save a few sick healed by His hands. What the hands still did: those few were healed. Mighty works by His hands were still the astonishment of Mark 6:2. They shall recover. Signs and wonders by the apostles’ hands. One occasion. Not Acts 19:11.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write the four references with one sentence each. Then write what unbelief did in Nazareth, and what the hands still did. Word drill: mighty works by His hands / a few sick / they shall recover / signs and wonders.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Mark 6:2, Mark 6:5, Mark 16:18, and Acts 5:12 in full. Page 2: Nazareth — astonishment, no mighty work, save the few healed; the risen word; the apostles’ hands. Page 3: not a substitute for Courses 1–3; no tenth healing system; not Acts 19:11. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
The four texts as one occasion vs a healing brand that no longer needs the verses.

Charge
Write the four references with one sentence each. Then write what unbelief did in Nazareth, and what the hands still did.

lessons.title: Miracles — Acts 19:11
lessons.body:
Central principle
God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul. God wrought. By the hands.

Key Scripture
Acts 19:11.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section VIII.

Teaching
God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul. The next verse tells of cloths from his body. The occasion Foundation School names is performing miracles — Acts 19:11. Do not make Paul the source. Do not make the cloth a tenth occasion.

Acts 19:11-12. And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.

Who wrought? God. By whose hands? Paul’s. What tenth will you refuse to add from verse 12? A cloth-system. Handkerchiefs or aprons from his body; diseases departed; evil spirits went out. Verse 12 is in these passages so you will read what followed. The teaching says miracles, Acts 19:11. God wrought. By the hands. The cloth is not a tenth occasion. The man is not the source.

Special miracles. The text uses the word. Foundation School will not invent a tenth category to explain “special.” It will also not pretend verse 11 can be taught if God is removed from the subject. God wrought. Paul is the hands. The sick and the possessed meet what God wrought. If you preach Paul as the fountain, you have inverted the verse. If you preach a cloth-ministry as a tenth category, you have left this lesson’s nine.

This is not the healing lesson. Healing the sick has its four texts. This is performing miracles, Acts 19:11. The sick appear in verse 12; the occasion remains the one Foundation School names. Do not flatten healing and miracles to make the teaching neater. Do not skip verse 12 to protect verse 11. Read both. Recognize one occasion.

Course 1–3 remain the house. Miracles do not invent the son. They do not replace metanoia. They do not replace baptism into Christ. Resultant. When? After the earlier foundations are laid. A miracle-practice treated as the foundation is not this principle.

From his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons. Diseases departed. Evil spirits went out. Verse 12 is read. Verse 12 is not treated as a tenth occasion. This lesson named performing miracles — Acts 19:11. God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul. Subject: God. Instrument: the hands of Paul. Occasion: miracles. Not a cloth-religion. Not Paul as fountain.

The healing lesson already took healing’s four texts. This lesson takes Acts 19:11. The sick in verse 12 do not merge the two occasions. Do not skip verse 12 to make verse 11 tidier. Do not preach verse 12 as if the teaching had ten names. God wrought. By the hands. That is the sentence you can teach without a tenth and without making the man the source.

Who wrought? God. By whose hands? Paul’s. What tenth will you refuse from verse 12? A cloth-system. Handkerchiefs or aprons, diseases departed, evil spirits went out — read it; do not treat it as occasion ten. Special miracles: the text’s word, not a tenth category. Paul is not the fountain. Course 1–3 remain the house. Miracles do not invent the son. They do not replace metanoia. They do not replace baptism into Christ. When? After the grounding things. A miracle-practice treated as the foundation is not this principle. The teaching says miracles, Acts 19:11. Keep the sentence. Refuse the tenth.

Open Acts 19:11-12 so verse 12 is included. The occasion Foundation School names is performing miracles — by the hands. God wrought remains the subject if you teach both verses. A cloth-ministry treated as a tenth has left this lesson's Scripture. A Paul-as-source sermon has inverted the verse. Write Acts 19:11. Who wrought? By whose hands? What tenth will you refuse?

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Acts 19:11. Who wrought? By whose hands? What tenth will you refuse to add from verse 12? Word drill: God wrought / by the hands of Paul / special miracles.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Acts 19:11-12 in full; mark God, wrought, special miracles, hands, Paul, cloths, diseases, spirits. Page 2: Paul is not the source; the cloth is not a tenth. Page 3: healing is not this lesson; write the flattening error you will refuse and the foundation you will not make of miracles. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
God wrought by the hands vs the man as the source, or a cloth-system beside the teaching.

Charge
Write Acts 19:11. Who wrought? By whose hands? What tenth will you refuse to add from verse 12?

lessons.title: Imparting gifts — 1 Timothy 4:14; 2 Timothy 1:6; Hebrews 6:2
lessons.body:
Central principle
The gift given by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. Stir up the gift by the putting on of Paul’s hands. Hebrews 6:2 names the principle and is cited again here.

Key Scripture
1 Timothy 4:14; 2 Timothy 1:6; Hebrews 6:2.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section IX.

Teaching
Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. Stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. Hebrews 6:2 names laying on of hands among the first principles. This lesson cites that same verse again under this occasion. The principle and the gift-occasion are not two religions. One teaching.

1 Timothy 4:14. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

2 Timothy 1:6. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.

Hebrews 6:2. Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

The gift is not to be neglected. It is to be stirred. Hands of the presbytery. Hands of Paul. Prophecy with the laying on. What is not to be neglected? The gift that is in thee. What is to be stirred? The gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. Why is Hebrews 6:2 in these passages twice? Because Foundation School names the principle among the six and cites the same verse again under imparting gifts. The principle is real. This occasion is one of the nine. Not two religions.

Do not treat a gift as if it were the foundation. Do not treat the foundation as if it forbade gifts. A man who has made a gift the house has not heard Course 4’s “when?” A man who has used Hebrews 6:1-2 to forbid the gift the verses name has not heard these passages. Neglect not. Stir up. The gift is in thee. Given by prophecy with the presbytery’s hands. In thee by Paul’s hands.

Timothy is not a tenth system. Two letters. Two sentences. One occasion: imparting gifts. The presbytery in one verse; Paul in the other. Prophecy with the laying on. Remembrance to stir up. Foundation School will not invent a third gift-text to make a nicer triangle. It will not drop Hebrews 6:2 from these passages because it already appeared in the intro.

The gift that is in thee. Given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. The gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up. Neglect not. Two warnings, one occasion. Hebrews 6:2 names laying on of hands among the first principles and is cited again here so that the gift-occasion is not a second religion beside the principle.

Do not treat a gift as the foundation. Do not treat the foundation as if it forbade gifts. When? After Courses 1–3. A neglected gift is still not the house. A stirred gift is still not baptism into Christ. Resultant practice. One teaching.

What is not to be neglected? The gift that is in thee. What is to be stirred? The gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. Why is Hebrews 6:2 here twice? The principle is among the six, and the same verse is cited again under this occasion. Presbytery. Paul. Prophecy with the laying on. Remembrance. Not two religions. Not a tenth gift-text. Not a new foundation.

1 Timothy 4:14 and 2 Timothy 1:6 are two sentences of one occasion: imparting gifts. The gift is in thee. Given by prophecy with the presbytery’s hands. In thee by Paul’s hands. Stir up. Neglect not. Hebrews 6:2 is not a second religion beside the earlier foundation stones. When? After the grounding things. A gift treated as the house has not heard “when?” A foundation that forbids this gift has not heard these passages.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write 1 Timothy 4:14 and 2 Timothy 1:6. What is not to be neglected? What is to be stirred? Why is Hebrews 6:2 in these passages twice? Word drill: neglect not / stir up / presbytery / putting on of my hands.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write 1 Timothy 4:14, 2 Timothy 1:6, and Hebrews 6:2 in full. Page 2: gift with hands — prophecy, presbytery, Paul’s hands; not two religions. Page 3: not a new foundation; not a foundation that forbids the gift — write both refusals. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Gift with hands vs gift as a new foundation, or a foundation that has no room for the gift the verses name.

Charge
Write 1 Timothy 4:14 and 2 Timothy 1:6. What is not to be neglected? What is to be stirred? Why is Hebrews 6:2 in these passages twice?

lessons.title: Imparting Spirit baptism — Acts 8:17-24; 9:17; 19:6
lessons.body:
Central principle
They laid hands; they received the Holy Ghost. Ananias on Saul. Paul at Ephesus. Simon’s money is in the account so you will not make this a market.

Key Scripture
Acts 8:17-24; Acts 9:17; Acts 19:6.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section X.

Teaching
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost. Simon offered money. Peter said the gift of God cannot be purchased. Teach the hands. Do not skip the rebuke.

Acts 8:17-24. Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost. And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity. Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.

Acts 9:17. And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

Acts 19:6. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

Course 3 already taught that Christ baptizes in the Spirit, and that the Spirit may be given before water or after it. This occasion is imparting Spirit baptism by hands in these accounts. It does not cancel the agent Course 3 named. It does not make hands the foundation. It is the ninth in the teaching.

What does Simon want to buy? The power that on whomsoever he lays hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. What must you refuse if the gift of God cannot be purchased? A market. Money perish with thee. Neither part nor lot. Heart not right. Repent of this wickedness. Gall of bitterness. Bond of iniquity. Simon is in the ninth account so that you will not make the ninth a market. Teach the hands. Do not skip the rebuke.

Ananias: Brother Saul — the Lord Jesus sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. Hands on Saul. Sight and filling. Paul at Ephesus: laid his hands; the Holy Ghost came on them; they spake with tongues, and prophesied. Three accounts. One occasion. Not a tenth. Not a substitute for new birth. Not Christ cancelled as baptizer.

Through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given — that is what Simon saw. He offered money for the power. Peter’s sentences are part of these passages: money perish with thee; thought the gift of God may be purchased; neither part nor lot; heart not right; repent of this wickedness; gall of bitterness; bond of iniquity. Teach the hands. Do not skip the rebuke.

Course 3: Christ baptizes in the Holy Spirit; Spirit before water or after it; prerequisite new birth. This ninth occasion is imparting Spirit baptism by hands in these accounts. It does not cancel that agent. It does not make hands the foundation. Samaria, Saul, Ephesus — one teaching, not three extra occasions.

What does Simon want to buy? The power that on whomsoever he lays hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. Refuse the market. The gift of God cannot be purchased. Ananias was sent by the Lord Jesus. Paul laid hands at Ephesus; they spake with tongues and prophesied. Teach the hands. Do not skip the rebuke. Do not cancel Christ as Spirit-baptizer.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write Acts 8:17-20, 9:17, and 19:6. What does Simon want to buy? What must you refuse if the gift of God cannot be purchased? Word drill: received the Holy Ghost / money perish / filled / tongues and prophesied.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Acts 8:17-24, 9:17, and 19:6 in full. Page 2: Simon refused — part, lot, heart, repent, gall, bond; the gift cannot be purchased. Page 3: Christ remains Spirit-baptizer; hands are the ninth occasion, not the foundation, not a tenth. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
The ninth occasion vs buying the gift, or making hands the agent in place of Christ.

Charge
Write Acts 8:17-20, 9:17, and 19:6. What does Simon want to buy? What must you refuse if the gift of God cannot be purchased?

lessons.title: The nine as one teaching — no invented tenth
lessons.body:
Central principle
Nine occasions. Each has its own text. No tenth. Blessing children is not healing. Ordaining is not buying the gift.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:2 with the nine texts.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 5, section XI.

Teaching
Write them until you can teach them without a tenth. All these attest a record across Holy Scripture. Each occasion stays distinct.

Genesis 48:14. And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn.

Numbers 8:10. And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites.

Numbers 27:18. And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.

Numbers 27:23. And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.

Deuteronomy 34:9. And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

Matthew 19:13-15. Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.

Mark 6:2. And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?

Mark 6:5. And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.

Mark 16:18. They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

Acts 5:12. And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people.

Acts 19:11. And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul.

1 Timothy 4:14. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

2 Timothy 1:6. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.

Hebrews 6:2. Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Acts 8:17. Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

Acts 9:17. And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

Acts 19:6. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

1. Blessing men — Genesis 48:14. 2. Making offerings — Numbers 8:10. 3. Ordaining — Numbers 27:18, 23. 4. Imparting Spirit — Deuteronomy 34:9. 5. Blessing children — Matthew 19:13-15. 6. Healing the sick — Mark 6:2, 5; 16:18; Acts 5:12. 7. Performing miracles — Acts 19:11. 8. Imparting gifts — 1 Timothy 4:14; 2 Timothy 1:6; Hebrews 6:2. 9. Imparting Spirit baptism — Acts 8:17-24; 9:17; 19:6.

If you added a tenth, strike it and name why it is not among the nine. Cloth is not a tenth. A crossed-hands technique is not a tenth. A healing brand is not a tenth. Buying the gift is refused in the ninth, not added as a tenth. One vague “hands” practice is not the teaching.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write the nine with their texts from memory. No tenth. If you added one, strike it and name why it is not among the nine. Word drill: nine / each its own text / no tenth.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write the nine names with the key verses in full from the list above. Page 2: one flatten you refuse for each pair you have been merging (children/healing; ordaining/Deuteronomy 34; miracles/cloth). Page 3: strike every tenth; write why Foundation School does not name it. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Nine as one teaching vs one vague “hands” practice, or a tenth invented to make the teaching neater.

Charge
Write the nine with their texts from memory. No tenth. If you added one, strike it and name why it is not among the nine.

lessons.title: Charge — resultant practice
lessons.body:
Central principle
When? After the earlier foundations are laid. Hands remain among the first principles. They do not become the house.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:1-2.

Read
Chapter 5, section XII.

Teaching
This lesson is the examination of the principle, not a new doctrine. When? After the earlier foundations are laid.

Hebrews 6:1-2. Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

You should now be able to teach, from Scripture:

1. Resultant, not the foundation. Viable after Courses 1–3. Hands do not invent the son, replace metanoia, replace pistis, or replace the three baptisms.
2. Blessing men — Genesis 48:14. Israel; Ephraim and Manasseh; the blessing spoken; hands guided wittingly.
3. Offerings — Numbers 8:10. Levites offered before the LORD; the congregation’s hands; identification and presentation.
4. Ordaining — Numbers 27:18, 23. A man in whom is the spirit; charge as the LORD commanded; before the priest and the congregation.
5. Imparting Spirit — Deuteronomy 34:9. Full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands. Held beside Numbers 27, not flattened.
6. Blessing children — Matthew 19:13-15. The disciples rebuked; the Lord would not; not Course 1 for a child.
7. Healing — Mark 6:2, 5; 16:18; Acts 5:12. Nazareth limited; a few still healed; they shall recover; apostles’ hands.
8. Miracles — Acts 19:11. God wrought. By the hands of Paul. Cloth is not a tenth.
9. Imparting gifts — 1 Timothy 4:14; 2 Timothy 1:6; Hebrews 6:2 twice in the teaching. Neglect not. Stir up.
10. Imparting Spirit baptism — Acts 8:17-24 (Simon refused); 9:17; 19:6. Does not cancel Christ as Spirit-baptizer.
11. Nine. No tenth. No required companion Foundation School does not name.

Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? All three that stand before this one in Hebrews 6:1-2. A man who has not turned from dead works, who has not faith toward God, who has not been baptized into Christ, is not ready to make hands the house.

Name one practice you will not treat as a foundation. If the practice is one of these nine, keep it resultant. If it is a tenth you invented, put it down. The next principle is resurrection of the dead. Two kinds: spiritual and material.

Charge 26: write the nine with their texts. No tenth. Charge 27: which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? All three that stand before this one — repentance from dead works, faith toward God, the doctrine of baptisms. Charge 28: name one practice you will not treat as a foundation. Do not submit a feeling in the place of the teaching.

Deuteronomy 34:9 remains beside Numbers 27:18, 23 — not flattened. Acts 19:11 remains God wrought; cloth is not a tenth. Acts 8:17-24 remains Simon refused. Hebrews 6:2 remains twice: the principle among the six, and again under imparting gifts. No required companion. Christ remains Spirit-baptizer. Hands remain among the first principles. They do not become the house.

Write the nine with their texts. Blessing men. Offerings. Ordaining. Imparting Spirit. Blessing children. Healing. Miracles. Imparting gifts. Imparting Spirit baptism. Each has its own text. No tenth. If the practice is one of these nine, keep it resultant. If it is a tenth you invented, put it down. Do not submit a feeling in the place of the teaching. The next principle is resurrection of the dead — two kinds, spiritual and material. This examination is not that chapter.

Which earlier principle must already be laid? All three that stand before this one in Hebrews 6:1-2. A man who has not turned from dead works, who has not faith toward God, who has not been baptized into Christ, is not ready to make hands the house. Name one practice you will not treat as a foundation. Completing activities is not mastery. The teaching is nine. No required companion.

Labour
The Walk — write the nine as nine tight paragraphs, then the three charges (Charge 26–Charge 28). The doctrine is the same. Word drill: resultant / nine / no tenth / when?

Intensive — write the nine as nine full pages, then the three charges. Use the same passages. The doctrine is the same. Do not invent a tenth page that is a tenth occasion. On the charge pages: the three stones already laid; one practice you will not treat as a foundation; Simon refused; God wrought; no companion Foundation School does not name. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Completion of activities vs mastery. Resultant practice vs a new foundation made of hands.

Charge
Write the nine with their texts. Which earlier principle must already be laid before you treat hands as if they were the foundation? Name one practice you will not treat as a foundation. Do not submit a tenth. Do not submit a feeling in the place of the teaching.

lessons.title: Two kinds — spiritual and material
lessons.body:
Central principle
There are two main kinds of resurrection: spiritual and material. Spiritual is the new birth. Material is the body. Do not flatten them into one slogan.

Key Scripture
Hebrews 6:2; Ephesians 2:1-6; John 5:28-29.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 6, section I.

Teaching
This is Course 5 of Foundation School. One curriculum. The fifth of the six principles. Hebrews 6:2 names resurrection of the dead after laying on of hands. Course 4 left you at the fourth stone. This course opens the fifth: two kinds, not one heading you can recite without a distinction.

Hebrews 6:1-2. Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

The heading gives the teaching: two main kinds — spiritual and material. Spiritual resurrection is the new birth: being quickened from dead in trespasses and sins. Material resurrection is the resurrection of the body, not spirit. If you treat the heading as only a grave, you have already lost this lesson's distinction. If you treat the heading as only a conversion, you have already lost this lesson's distinction.

Ephesians 2:1-6. And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience: Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others. But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;) And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:

John 5:28-29. Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

Spiritual resurrection is now. Dead in trespasses. Quickened together with Christ. Raised up together. Sit in heavenly places. That is spiritual resurrection. It is not the graves of John 5:28-29. Course 1 already named you dead in trespasses and sins. Course 2 named the son. Course 3 baptized that son into Christ. This lesson will not lay those stones again. It will name what they already were: a resurrection, spiritual, in this life.

Material resurrection concerns the graves. All that are in the graves shall hear His voice and come forth. Two issues: life and damnation. The body comes forth. Not the spirit as if the person were a ghost waiting to be invented. A later lesson will hold John 5. A later lesson will time the two issues by a thousand years. Today you will not steal those lessons. Today you will refuse one slogan that swallows both kinds.

Do not postpone new birth past death and call it resurrection. That offer is refused by this lesson's Scripture. Do not raise the wicked before the Millennium and call it the first resurrection. That flatten is refused when Revelation 20 is opened. Do not flatten five companies into one rapture. Those later companies are outside this lesson. This lesson is two kinds.

Leaving the first principles is not forgetting them. A man who never received the new birth is not leaving spiritual resurrection when he talks about graves. He is skipping the first kind. Hebrews 6:2 will not let you treat the fifth name as only a future hour.

Two main kinds. Spiritual: Ephesians 2:1-6. Material: John 5:28-29. Write both. Teach both. Do not merge them to make the teaching neater. The later chronology will hang on this distinction. If you lose two kinds here, you will flatten every company later.

The Aletheia text distinguishes two main kinds of resurrection: Spiritual and Material. Spiritual resurrection is the new birth: being quickened (revived) from dead in trespasses and sins, renewed in the glorious likeness of God. Material resurrection is the resurrection of the body, not spirit. Hold both sentences. A teacher who can name five companies and cannot name two kinds has inverted the teaching. A student who can recite John 5 and has never been quickened has the second kind in his mouth and not the first in his life. Course 5 begins here, or it does not begin.

Labour
The Walk — one tight page. Write the two kinds with one governing text each. What does spiritual raise, and when? What does material raise? Word drill: two kinds / quickened / graves / not one slogan.

Intensive — three pages on the same Scripture set. Page 1: write Hebrews 6:1-2, Ephesians 2:1-6, and John 5:28-29 in full; mark two kinds. Page 2: spiritual is new birth now — not the graves. Page 3: material is the body — not a second conversion; write the flatten you will refuse. The doctrine is the same.

Distinction
Spiritual resurrection vs material resurrection. Two kinds, not one heading.

Charge
Write the two kinds with one governing text each. What does spiritual raise, and when? What does material raise? Do not submit one slogan.

lessons.title: Spiritual resurrection — Ephesians 2:1-6
lessons.body:
Central principle
Spiritual resurrection is the new birth: quickened from death in trespasses and sins. It is now. It is not the bodily raising.

Key Scripture
Ephesians 2:1-6.

Reference
School handbook, Chapter 6, section II.

Teaching
You hath He quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins. Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ — by grace ye are saved. Raised us up together. Made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.

Ephesians 2:1-6.
